 ## 9. Generation contract for a new language
 
 An AI (or a human) generating a Pathland DSL in a new language MUST produce the
 following and verify each item. This is a checklist; the authoritative details
 are the companion specs.
 
 ### 9.1 Required surface
 
 - [ ] **Views/controls** — every entry of [§4](#4-view-surface):
   `Text`, `Image`, `Color`, `Shape` (all `ShapeKind`s), `Divider`, `Spacer`,
   `ProgressView`, `Gauge`; `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`,
   `ScrollView`,
   `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`; `Button`,
   `TextField`, `SecureField`, `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`,
   `Picker`, `Menu`, `DatePicker`, `ColorPicker`.
 - [ ] **The three operations** — configure values, apply modifiers, supply
   children — available at creation or by chaining, in any order
   ([§2](#2-canonical-signature-notation)). Each language maps them to its idiom
   ([§9.3](#93-language-adaptation-rules)).
 - [ ] **Modifiers** — every entry of [§5](#5-modifier-surface), applicable to
   any view, innermost-first, emitting one property per underlying argument; a
   modifier's type carries no `Mod` suffix.
 - [ ] **Custom modifiers / unified mechanism** — a `ViewModifier` authoring
   surface (`body(content) -> View`) + a chainable `modifiers(...)` operation on
   **any** view; **core modifiers are implemented through the same mechanism**,
   never a separate syntax ([§5.6](#56-custom-modifiers-developer-authored)).
 - [ ] **Shared config with styles** — a style's `makeBody(Config)` receives the
   same config type the control configured via `make(...)`
   ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)).
 - [ ] **Signals** — `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `untracked`,
   `get`/`set`/`update`/`asReadonly`, with equality suppression, synchronous
   flush, glitch-free propagation, error caching, write discipline, circular
   detection ([§3.1](#31-signal-surface)).
 - [ ] **Two-way bindings** — every value control takes a writable signal (a
   config value) and exposes a sink the host routes its event into
   ([§3.2](#32-two-way-binding)).
 - [ ] **Persisted state** — `State<T>` keyed fields (or the language's
   equivalent wiring) against a platform-neutral store ([§3.3](#33-persisted-state-statet)).
 - [ ] **Gestures** — `.onTapGesture` (composed from raw pointer down/up) and
   raw `pointerEvents`/`EVENT_LISTENERS` bitmask ([§4.4](#44-gestures)).
 - [ ] **Structural reactivity (reactive bodies)** — a signal read in a
   component body (`if`/`switch`/`for`, or the language's equivalent) re-renders
   that component and reconciles it into `TREE` deltas with zero opcodes for
   identical structure; `View.of` is the inline supplier form
   ([§3.4](#34-structural-reactivity-reactive-bodies--slots)).
 - [ ] **Reactive lists** — `ForEach` over a static list or a
   `Signal<List<T>>`, each item a child component slot; static lists MAY use
   native iteration instead ([§3.4](#34-structural-reactivity-reactive-bodies--slots),
   [§9.3.1](#931-cross-language-reactive-vocabulary)).
 - [ ] **Navigation** — `Router` / `RouteTable` / `NavigationContainer` /
   `NavigationLink` over a plain `Signal<Route>`, the initial route host-seeded
   before mount, emitting `ROUTE` and `TRANSITION` and consuming the `NAVIGATE`
   event ([§4.5](#45-navigation)).
 - [ ] **Design tokens & theming** — a token surface: token-typed values usable
   in style modifiers (a `Color` accepting a token path, e.g. `Color.token("color.primary")`
   or the language's equivalent), a theme/override helper emitting
   `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (base values + `dark.`-prefixed dark values), and
   the **base=light / `dark.*`** color-scheme convention with renderer-derived
   scheme detection — see [§7](#7-theme-management) and [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md).
 
 ### 9.2 Mapping rules (signature → protocol)
 
 1. Each view/control maps to its **fixed component id** in PRIMITIVES.md.
    Application/custom component types live in `0x0100`–`0xFFFF`; a DSL must
    never reuse allocated ids.
 2. Each modifier maps to the **documented property id(s)** in MODIFIERS.md
    with the documented **value type** (U8/U32/I32/F32/STRING/ENUM/COLOR/
    DESIGN_TOKEN). Enumerated values use the numeric codes in MODIFIERS.md's
    appendix.
 3. `Color` values pack as sRGB `0xAARRGGBB`. A **token-typed** value instead
    carries the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type with the token path in the arena
    (never a packed literal); the renderer resolves it against the current
    scheme. A theme/override helper emits `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`
    (`A` = arenaRef path, `B` = valueType, `C` = value); a `dark.`-prefixed path
    supplies the dark design (base = light — [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md)).
 4. `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` sentinels: `FILL` = −1.0, `HUG_CONTENT` = −2.0.
 5. `Grid` counts map to the **config values** `GRID_COLUMNS` (`0x001E`) /
    `GRID_ROWS` (`0x001F`): a positive `int` count emits a positive F32; absent =
    auto-fit. A **`List<GridItem>`** value serializes to the **`GRID_TRACKS`**
    (`0x0020`, STRING) per-track spec, which takes precedence over the counts. A
    `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` frame on a grid is the grid's **box**, never a count
    ([§4.2](#42-layout--container-nodes)).
 6. `DatePicker` value/event use the two-field encoding **days since epoch
    (I32) + millis of day (U32)**; there is no `DATE_VALUE` property.
 7. Value/text/date events are gated by the transport-aware event guards; the
    DSL's controls emit the `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`/`EVENT_LISTENERS` that
    declare intent.
 8. Emission is **diff-based and reactive**: the DSL describes values, the
    emitter diffs. A generated DSL must keep the retained tree + emitter
    separation; it must not hand-serialize full trees.
 
 ### 9.3 Language adaptation rules
 
 **The three operations are normative; their spellings are not.** A conformant
 DSL MUST expose *configure values*, *apply modifiers*, and *supply children*,
 each available at creation or by chaining (any order), mapped to the host
 language's idioms. The canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) spelling is
 `Text("x").padding(16)`; Java spells values `make(...)` (views) / lowercase
 functions (modifiers) and chains `modifiers(...)` / `children(...)`.
 
 | Aspect | Java | C# | Rust | Go | Python |
 |--------|------|----|------|----|--------|
 | configure values | `make(c -> …)` (views) / `padding(c -> …)` (modifiers) | `Make(c => …)` | `Type::new(config)` / `with(\|c\| …)` | ctor + options | kwargs / `configure(…)` |
 | single-value shortcut | `make(value)` / `padding(value)` (sugar for the lambda) | `Make(value)` | `Type::new(value)` / `Type(sig)` | `Type(val)` | `Type(val=…)` / `Type(sig)` |
 | apply modifiers | `.modifiers(…)` | `.Modifiers(…)` | `.modifiers(…)` (single or tuple) | `.Modifiers(…)` | `.modifiers(…)` |
 | supply children | `.children(…)` | `.Children(…)` | `.children(vec![…])` / `vstack![…]` | ctor args / `.Children(…)` | `.children(*v)` |
 | creation + chaining | static on the view; chain on the returned builder | static on the view; chain via **extension methods** | associated fn `Type::new`; chain via a **trait** + macros | package ctor; chain via methods | kwargs + methods |
 | same-name static + chain | **builder split** (static on class, chain on builder) | extension methods (separate static class) | assoc fn + trait method | package func + method (not type-scoped) | **not expressible** (methods are last-wins) |
 | `with` name legal | yes | yes (`With`; lowercase `with` is the record keyword) | yes | yes | **no** — `with` is a keyword → kwargs / `configure` |
 | varargs children | yes | `params` | no — slices/arrays or macros | `...` | `*args` |
 | value *is* the modifier | enum OK | **enum can't implement an interface** → `record struct` / static readonly value | enum OK | typed const + method OK | enum member with `apply` OK |
 
 Rules:
 
 - A language that cannot express "static-or-chained under one name" (Python)
   MUST still offer the three operations — value configuration via kwargs /
   `configure(...)`, modifiers and children via chainable methods.
 - A language whose enums cannot implement the modifier interface (C#) MUST
   supply the equivalent single-value modifier form (a `record struct`, a static
   readonly value, or an implicit conversion).
 - **Reactive values are config members, in every language.** A config member
   accepts a raw value or a signal ([§2](#2-canonical-signature-notation)). Rust
   realizes this with `impl Into<Reactive<T>>` on each builder setter
   (`Reactive<T> { Static(T), Signal(SignalId) }`); the former `Bound` /
   `*.bound` modifier surface is folded into it and **removed**.
 - Names are recommendations; semantics
   ([§1](#1-design-principles-dsl-flavored)) are the contract.
 
 #### 9.3.1 Cross-language reactive vocabulary
 
 The **names and semantics** are shared; the syntax is the host language's.
 Swift is the canonical SwiftUI-shaped reference. Java spells the non-native
 helpers as `View.of` / `ForEach.of`; Kotlin and TypeScript use their native
 expression and collection forms; Rust parity is Phase 2.
 
 | Concept | Swift | Java | Kotlin | Rust | TypeScript |
 |---------|-------|------|--------|------|------------|
 | Component render | `var body: some View` | `View body()` | `View body()` | `fn build(&self)` | `body(props)` |
 | Signal read | `count` (`@State`), `signal.value` | `sig.get()` | `sig.value` / `sig()` | `sig.get()` | `sig()` |
 | Branch | `if`/`switch` in `@ViewBuilder` | `if`/`switch` in `body()`; `View.of(() -> …)` inline | `if`/`when` expressions | `if`/`match` expressions | ternary / `switch` expressions |
 | Inline subtree | `Group { … }` / `@ViewBuilder` | `View.of(() -> …)` | `View.of { … }` (rarely needed) | `View::of(\|\| …)` | `View.of(() => …)` |
 | Static list | `ForEach(items) { … }` / `for` in a builder | stream/`for` + `.children(…)` | `items.map { … }` + `.children(…)` | iterator + `.children(vec![…])` | `items.map(…)` |
 | Reactive list | `ForEach(items) { … }` | `ForEach.of(items, (item, i) -> …)` | `ForEach(items) { item, i -> … }` | `ForEach::of(items, \|item, i\| …)` | `ForEach(items, (item, i) => …)` |
 | Children | trailing closure | `.children(a, b)` | `.children(a, b)` / trailing lambda | `.children(vec![a, b])` | `children: [a, b]` |
 | Values | `VStack(spacing: 8)` | `VStack.make(v -> v.spacing(8))` | `VStack(spacing = 8)` | `VStack::new(\|v\| v.spacing(8.0))` | `VStack({ spacing: 8 })` |
 | Modifiers | `.padding(16)` / `.modifiers(…)` | `.modifiers(padding(16))` | `.modifiers(padding(16))` | `.modifiers(padding(16.0))` | `.modifiers(padding(16))` |
 | State | `@State` / `@Binding` | `State<T>` / `WritableSignal<T>` | `State<T>` / `WritableSignal<T>` | `State<T>` / `WritableSignal<T>` | `State<T>` / `WritableSignal<T>` |
 | Environment | `@Environment` | `Environment.value(key)` | `Environment.value(key)` | `Environment` | `useAppContext()` / `Environment` |
 
 Canonical examples:
 
 ```swift
 struct LibraryView: View {
     let tracks: [Track]
     @Binding var trackIndex: Int
 
     var body: some View {
         VStack(spacing: 8) {
             Text("Library")
             ForEach(tracks) { track in
                 TrackRow(track: track, trackIndex: $trackIndex)
             }
         }
     }
 }
 ```
 
 ```java
 VStack.make(v -> v.spacing(8)).children(
     Text.make("Library"),
     ForEach.of(tracks, (track, index) -> TrackRowView.make(r -> r
         .track(track)
         .index(index)
         .trackIndex(trackIndex))));
 ```
 
 ```kotlin
 VStack(spacing = 8) {
     Text("Library")
     ForEach(tracks) { track, index ->
         TrackRow(TrackRowProps(track, index, trackIndex))
     }
 }
 ```
 
 ```rust
 VStack::new(|v| v.spacing(8.0)).children(vec![
     Text::new("Library").into(),
     ForEach::of(tracks.clone(), |track, index| {
         TrackRow::new(track, index, track_index.clone()).into()
     }),
 ])
 ```
 
 ```ts
 VStack({ spacing: 8 }, [
   Text({ text: "Library" }),
   ForEach(tracks, (track, index) =>
     TrackRow({ track, index, trackIndex })),
 ])
 ```
 
 Rules:
 
 - **Use native control flow** where the language has it. `View.of` is the Java
   inline form because Java has no `if` expression; Swift/Kotlin/Rust/TypeScript
   use their own `if`/`switch`/`when`/`match`/ternary forms.
 - **Use native iteration for static lists.** `ForEach` is the reactive
   (component-scoped) list; static lists MAY use streams/`map`/`for` directly.
 - **Keep the anchors**: `View`, `Signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `State`,
   `ForEach`, `View.of`, `children`, `modifiers`. These are what make the DSLs
   recognizable; casing and construction follow the host language.
 - **`(item, index)` order** for `ForEach`, matching JavaScript `map` and Java
   `BiFunction`; Kotlin/Rust authors may name the lambda parameters.
 - **No keys yet.** The emitter reconciles by position + type; a keyed `ForEach`
   is a future protocol/emitter feature, not a syntax difference.
 - **Gaps**: Rust reactive-body/`ForEach` parity is Phase 2; the TypeScript plan
   currently defers structural reactivity; Swift is not implemented yet. Kotlin is
   implemented by `lib/java/pathland-view-kotlin` (a facade over the Java library;
   `Text("…")`, `VStack(spacing = 8) { … }`, `.padding(16)`), with its surface and
   gaps tracked in that module's `status.md`.
 
 ### 9.4 Conformance recipe
 
 A generated DSL is verified by proving it **emits the same bytes** as the
 reference implementations:
 
 1. Port the golden vectors in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md) into the new
    DSL's test harness; assert byte-identical `TREE`/`PARAMETER`/`EVENT`/`META`
    opcodes for each canonical element.
 2. Port the Java `EmitterTest` cases (mount → `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DATE`
    deltas; unchanged tree → zero opcodes; two-way routing: `TEXT_CHANGED`,
    `VALUE_CHANGED`, `DATE_CHANGED` write into the bound signal).
 3. Verify the no-heap-allocation steady-state property where the target
    language supports it (the Rust engine proves zero dynamic allocations during
    steady-state emission).
 4. Cross-check every referenced id against PRIMITIVES.md/MODIFIERS.md/EVENTS.md
    (the specs are the source of truth, never the reference code).

 **signals** — value, computed (lazy/memoized/equality-suppressed), and effect
 signals in a shared `no_std` runtime (`Signal<T>`/`WritableSignal<T>`,
 `Engine::signal`/`computed`/`effect`/`read`/`set`) with text/property binding —
 **two-way control bindings** (input sinks collected with
 `collect_input_handlers`) and **actions** (`Button::action`), plus
 **styles + environment** (a subtree `Environment` threaded through
 `View::build_env`, `ButtonStyle` applied with `ViewExt::button_style`),
 **structural reactivity + navigation** (`RouteTable`,
 `Router`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationLink`), and **persisted state**
 (a `StateStore` trait + `PersistentState::state` auto-load/auto-save). Both are
 per-project implementation status tracked in each project's `status.md`.
 
 ---
 
 ## Conformance
 
 - The wire footprint of every DSL element above is defined by the golden
   vectors in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md). A new DSL element MUST add
   vectors before any implementation depends on it.
 - Component ids: [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md); property ids and value
   types: [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md); event ids and listener bits:
   [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md). These specs are the single source of truth.
 - The v3 authoring surface (`make` + lowercase modifier functions,
   config-with-styles, no `Mod` suffix, single-value shortcuts) is a
   **source-surface** change only: it emits the **same bytes** as the prior
   v2 `.of(...)` / `with(...)` surface for an equivalent tree — no
   component/property/event/opcode change.

from pathlib import Path
import re
core_root=Path('lib/java/pathland-view-core/src/main/java')
mapping={}
dups=[]
for f in core_root.rglob('*.java'):
    m=re.search(r'^package\s+([\w.]+);', f.read_text(), re.M)
    if not m: continue
    pkg=m.group(1)
    name=f.stem
    if name in mapping and mapping[name]!=f'{pkg}.{name}':
        dups.append((name,mapping[name],f'{pkg}.{name}'))
    mapping[name]=f'{pkg}.{name}'
print('dups', dups)
# Build import additions for Java sources outside the defining package.
files=[]
for ext in ('*.java',):
    files += [p for p in Path('lib/java').rglob(ext) if 'target' not in p.parts]
for f in files:
    text=f.read_text()
    m=re.search(r'^package\s+([\w.]+);', text, re.M)
    if not m: continue
    pkg=m.group(1)
    lines=text.splitlines()
    # existing imports (simple -> fqcn) and declared types
    existing=set()
    for line in lines:
        mm=re.match(r'\s*import\s+(?:static\s+)?([\w.]+);', line)
        if mm:
            existing.add(mm.group(1))
    declared=set(re.findall(r'\b(?:class|interface|enum|record)\s+([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]*)', text))
    needed=[]
    for name, fq in sorted(mapping.items()):
        if name in declared: continue
        if fq.rsplit('.',1)[0] == pkg: continue
        if fq in existing: continue
        if re.search(rf'\b{re.escape(name)}\b', text):
            needed.append(fq)
    if not needed: continue
    # Insert imports after package declaration, before first import/type/comment.
    insert_at=m.end()
    # preserve newline right after package
    while insert_at < len(text) and text[insert_at] not in '\n': insert_at+=1
    insert_at+=1
    block=''.join(f'import {fq};\n' for fq in needed)
    text=text[:insert_at]+'\n'+block+text[insert_at:]
    f.write_text(text)
print('done')
PY

Starters tests use DSL; add test-scoped pathland-view to spring and quarkus starters. This creates potential cycle? pathland-view doesn't depend server; fine. Add.

Also remove Scheduler import from MultiSessionWebSocketTest.

from pathlib import Path
for name in ('pathland-spring-boot-starter','pathland-quarkus-starter'):
    p=Path(f'lib/java/{name}/pom.xml')
    s=p.read_text()
    needle='''        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-test-kit</artifactId>'''
    repl='''        <!-- Tests author views through the Java DSL; production stays core-only. -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-view</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-test-kit</artifactId>'''
    if needle not in s:
        print('needle missing', name)
    else:
        s=s.replace(needle,repl)
        p.write_text(s)

p=Path('lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/src/test/java/dev/pathland/spring/MultiSessionWebSocketTest.java')
s=p.read_text().replace('import dev.pathland.view.core.signal.Scheduler;\n','')
p.write_text(s)
PY
mvn -q test-compile -DskipTests 2>&1 | sed -n '1,260p'

# pathland-view (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 29, 2026

The hand-written, framework-agnostic Java 17+ DSL (`dev.pathland.view`):
declarative views, Angular-style signals, fine-grained emitter, `PLPL` wire
codec, lazy JNA ring interop, and cross-platform `State`. Protocol contract:
`spec/`. Runs on every LTS from Java 17.

## Implemented

- **Window metadata** (`windowMetadata(w -> w.title(...).description(...).locale(...))`): a root-scoped `ViewModifier` with signal-backed fields. The emitter emits the initial `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` fields at mount, re-emits only the changed field on a signal write, and re-sends every field in `renderFull` (resync). `FrameOpcodeSink` and the JNA `RingOpcodeSink` carry it; a route title is a `computed` over the router.
- **Per-component reactive bodies (#88)**: `body()` / `renderNode(Environment)` is a
  tracked render. Each child view is a `ViewSlot` with its own synchronous
  `Signals.tracked` computation; a signal read there re-renders only that component
  and the emitter diffs its retained subtree. Plain `if`/`switch`/`for` over signals
  now works in `body()` (bare control flow), with `View.of(Supplier<View>)` as the
  inline supplier form. The root chain (`body()` delegation, modifiers,
  environment/tap/navigation wrappers) stays in one slot; child views are child
  slots. A bound signal (`Text.make(t -> t.text(signal))`) remains fine-grained and
  does not re-run the body (initial binding reads are untracked). Non-signal reads
  are mount-time only. The root component type must stay stable. `render(Environment)`
  is the emitter entry point; primitives override `renderNode(Environment)`.
  `Conditional`/`Case` are removed (replaced by bare control flow + `View.of`).
- **`ForEach`** (`ForEach.of(list | Signal<List<T>>, (item, index) -> View)`):
  a Group-backed reactive list component. A static list maps once per render; a
  `Signal<List<T>>` re-renders only the list slot. Each item is a child component
  slot; null children are skipped; reconciliation is position + type (no keys).
  `ForEachTest`.
- **Cross-language vocabulary** (spec DSL.md §9.3.1): the shared anchors
  (`View`, `body`/`build`, `Signal`, `computed`, `State`, `ForEach`, `View.of`,
  `children`, `modifiers`) and the native spellings for Swift/Java/Kotlin/Rust/
  TypeScript. Swift is the canonical SwiftUI-shaped reference; Rust parity is
  Phase 2.
- **`ProxyView`** (`ProxyView.make(p -> p.endpoint(...).route(...).credential(...))`):
  a `PROXY_VIEW` (0x1E) container whose child subtree is served by **another**
  Pathland server (spec/PROXY.md). It authors **no** children — the origin root is
  spliced in at runtime — and takes size modifiers like any view. The immutable
  `ProxyConfig` snapshot rides the node (`PathlandNode.proxyConfig`) and is
  surfaced to the host through `RenderResult.proxyViews()` (node id → config) so
  `pathland-server-core` opens an origin connection per proxy node. The emitter's
  internal `onStructureReconciled(Runnable)` hook (like `snapshotEmission`) fires
  after each structural reconcile — after the routing maps reflect the new subtree
  — so the host reconciles origin connections against the live `proxyViews` map
  (a proxy lives exactly while its node is in the retained tree, spec/PROXY.md §7).
- **`SizeThatFits` fit slot** (`SizeThatFits.make(Fit...)` + `Fit.of(view, minWidth)`):
  a structural slot (`SIZE_THAT_FITS` 0x17) emitting `FIT_QUERY` (LIST, ascending
  thresholds) + the single selected child — unselected candidates never transmit.
  The host routes `FIT_CHANGED` into the slot's fit sink
  (`RenderResult.fitInputs`, via `InputDispatcher`), which re-renders only the fit
  component (an unchanged index re-emits zero opcodes). The LIST
  value type is written by `FrameOpcodeSink`/`RingOpcodeSink`
  (`[count][f32 × count]` arena entries). A slot's selection is **retained node
  state** (`PathlandNode.fitSelection`): a parent re-render creates a fresh fit
  component with a default index, so the emitter seeds it from the node it replaces
  (`ViewSlot.oldNodeHint` / `Emitter.currentSlotOldFitSelection`) — a nested fit
  (the player bar's controls slot under the root row) keeps its candidate instead
  of resetting to compact (a reset would strand the DOM client, which never
  re-reports an unchanged width). The **web-SSR full-snapshot emission** (issue #141) is an
  internal emitter mode (`Emitter.snapshotEmission(true)`, armed by
  `PathlandSession`): on mount/resync the slot emits EVERY candidate in `FIT_QUERY`
  order so the SSR renders all branches gated by CSS container queries (a no-JS
  correct first paint) — the authored DSL is unchanged. `PathlandNode.fitReported`
  and the emitter's `snapshotActive` flag keep the multi-candidate presentation
  until the first `FIT_CHANGED`; that report re-renders the fit component with one
  selected child, and the web client unwraps the gated branches. The downgrade is a
  **clean N→1** (`Emitter.reconcileSnapshotFit`): it keeps the SELECTED candidate's
  node as-is (retaining its id + subtree, zero churn) and removes the others — it
  never positionally diffs, because both candidates are frequently the same
  component and morphing the loser's node into the winner would relocate the winner
  into the SSR's loser wrapper and break the renderer's candidate-position CSS gate.
  **View reuse** (issue #159): the same `View` instance may not be the candidate
  of two `Fit`s — `SizeThatFits.make` rejects it (`IllegalStateException`), since
  it would be materialized once per candidate and leak shared state / ids.
  Sharing a subtree **inside** two distinct candidate roots stays allowed; every
  materialized copy gets a distinct node id. The emitter enforces the frame's
  **unique-node-id invariant** (spec/OPCODE.md §Frame Lifecycle) with
  `Emitter.duplicateIds` / a fail-loud guard at mount, resync, and after each
  structural reconcile, so an id-overriding pass (an identity-stable node pinning
  a playback key) can never silently corrupt an id-keyed consumer.
  `ROLE` catalog (mirrors `pathland_core::constants::role` / `spec/OPCODE.md`,
  dense 0–13): `HEADER`, `PARAGRAPH`, `LIST`, `LIST_ITEM`, `SUMMARY`, `BANNER`,
  `NAVIGATION`, `MAIN`, `CONTENT_INFO`, `COMPLEMENTARY`, `ARTICLE`, `SECTION`,
  `SEARCH`. Interactive/control roles are NOT roles — they are intrinsic to the
  control components, so `accessibilityRole(int)` **throws** for codes
  outside the semantic catalog (a custom button uses `Button` + `ButtonStyle`).
- **`Icon` + `IconName`** (the `ICON` primitive, spec/ICONS.md): a canonical
  `IconName` written once and mapped by each renderer to its native symbol
  (Adwaita on GTK, Lucide on the web). `Icon.make(i -> i.name(IconName))` /
  `Icon.make(i -> i.name(String))` / `Icon.make(i -> i.name(Signal<String>))` /
  `Icon.labeled(…, label)`;
  `Label.make(l -> l.title(..).icon(View))` composes the icon part;
  a reactive name re-emits only `ICON_NAME`. Size/tint follow `FONT_SIZE` /
  `COLOR`; `LABEL` makes the icon presentable.
- **`Font` (is itself the modifier)** — the `Font` spec: a
  predefined typography (`Font.title2()` → `TEXT_STYLE`, heading styles imply a
  heading element), a custom family + size (`Font.custom(name, size)` →
  `FONT_FAMILY` + `FONT_SIZE`), a fully-custom typography
  (`Font.custom(name, size, weight, design)` → all four axes), or a system
  size/weight/design (`Font.system(size, weight, design)`). `TextStyle` is the
  design-system typography enum (`TEXT_STYLE` codes). The individual font
  modifiers (`FontSize`, `FontWeight`, `FontFamily`, `FontDesign`,
  `FontStyle`, `FontWidth`, `Italic`) remain available for one-off overrides.
- **Value types**: `ValueTypes.forProperty` mirrors `value_type_for` —
  `COLOR` family → `COLOR`; `VISIBLE`/`ENABLED`/`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`/`UNDERLINE`/
  `STRIKETHROUGH`/`COLOR_INVERT`/`ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`/`IS_SECURE`/
  `IS_INDETERMINATE`/`FIXED_SIZE_*`/`SELECTED` → `U8`; `LINE_LIMIT`/`SELECTION`/
  `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`/`EVENT_LISTENERS`/`BORDER_EDGES` → `U32`;
  `LABEL`/`PROMPT`/`FONT_FAMILY`/`IMAGE_SOURCE` → `STRING`; enum-valued
  properties ride as `F32` holding the numeric enum code. `FontWeight` uses the
  spec's numeric 100–900 scale.
- **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.signal`): `signal`/`computed`/`effect`/
  `untracked` — glitch-free synchronous flush, equality suppression,
  circular-dependency detection. The `Scheduler`'s global effect queue is
  **thread-safe** (all entry points synchronized) so a request/SSR-thread flush can
  never race the actor's mid-flush mutation of another session's pending effects.
  An effect that **throws during a flush is not permanently unsubscribed**: its
  pre-run producer edges are restored, so it retries on the next dependency change
  (a transient error can't silently kill a node's binding).
- **Emitter** (`emit`): mounts once, stable ids, node-level binding effects
  (a signal change re-emits only that node), `FrameOpcodeSink` /
  `RingOpcodeSink`. For the ring path, a bound `text`/`value`/`date` control

  and a newly created subtree — so a control materialized by a structural slot

- **Structural reactivity** (spec DSL.md §3.4): per-component tracked bodies

input.content:
# pathland-view-core (JVM engine) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 1, 2026

The shared, framework-agnostic JVM engine and runtime for the Pathland protocol.
It owns the `View` SPI and shared authoring vocabulary, the retained-tree
diff emitter, signals/computed/effects, the wire codec, router, cross-platform
state, and JNA ring interop. The Java DSL (`pathland-view`) and the Kotlin DSL
(`pathland-view-kotlin`) are authoring layers over this module; server and
renderer modules depend on core only.

## Implemented

- **Protocol** (`dev.pathland.view.core.protocol`): `Components`, `Properties`,
  `Commands`, `Categories`, `ValueTypes`, `Opcode`, `ValueEncoder`, `WireValue`,
  `TokenPath`.
- **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.core.signal`): `signal`/`computed`/`effect`/
  `untracked`, synchronous glitch-free flush, equality suppression, error
  caching/retry, circular-dependency detection, and a thread-safe global
  `Scheduler`.
- **State** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): `State`/`PersistentState`,
  untyped `StateStore`, in-memory store and provider.
- **Transport** (`dev.pathland.view.core.transport`): `ProtocolFrame`,
  `FrameCodec`, `Event`, `EnvironmentData`, `OpcodeSink`, `FrameOpcodeSink`.
- **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.core.router`): `Route`, `RouteTable`, `Router`,
  `Navigation`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationIntent`, `Params`, `Chrome`,
  `NavOp`. `NavigationLink` stays in the Java DSL because it composes `Button`.
- **JNA interop** (`dev.pathland.view.core.ffm`): lazy `PathlandCore` binding and
  `RingOpcodeSink` over `libpathland_core`.
- **Emitter** (`dev.pathland.view.engine`): `Emitter`, `PathlandNode`, `ViewSlot`,
  `RenderResult`, `InputDispatcher`, `ReactiveValues`, `DateInput`, `MediaInput`.
  Implements mount/id assignment, diff-based reactive emission, node-level binding
  effects, structural reconciliation, fit/media/navigation routing, and the
  zero-opcode unchanged recompute contract.
- **Shared SPI/values** (`dev.pathland.view.core`): `View`, `ViewModifier`,
  `Configurable`, `ChildrenView`, `Modified`, `ViewBuilder`, `Configurators`,
  `Environment*`, `Platform`, `Theme*`, `MediaController`, `WindowMetadata`,
  `ProxyConfig`, `Color`, `Length`, shared enums, style protocols, and modifier
  wrappers.
- **Test coverage**: the Java DSL module's test suite exercises the engine
  end-to-end (emitter/reconcile, signals, state, router, transport, JNA ring),
  plus the server/HTML/desktop consumers.

## Package boundary

- `pathland-view-core` is one Maven module for now: `core`/`engine` are logical
  subpackages inside it, with a few deliberate intra-module references
  (`Color`/`MediaController`/`Modified` materialize `PathlandNode`). Splitting
  `core` and `engine` into separate artifacts requires a node SPI first.
- Production modules (`pathland-server-core`, `pathland-render-html`,
  `pathland-state-redis`, `pathland-test-kit`, starters) depend on core, not on
  the Java DSL. Tests that author views through the DSL add `pathland-view` in
  test scope.

+//! Generates the JVM engine's protocol constant classes from the canonical Rust
+//! protocol definitions (`pathland_core::constants`). A renamed or renumbered Rust
+//! constant breaks this crate's compilation or changes the emitted Java, so the
+//! committed `pathland-view-core` mirror cannot drift silently.
+//!
+//! Regenerate from `lib/rust`:
+//!
+//! ```text
+//! cargo run -p pathland-jvm-codegen
+//! ```
+//!
+//! CI runs the same command and fails on a dirty diff.
+
+use pathland_core::{
+    category, color_scheme_mode, component_type, environment, event, flag, listener, meta,
+    parameter, property_id, size, tree, value_type, value_type_for, window_field,
+};
+use std::fmt::Write;
+use std::io;
+use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
+
+fn output_dir() -> PathBuf {
+    Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
+        .join("../../../java/pathland-view-core/src/main/java/dev/pathland/view/core/protocol")
+}
+
+fn header(out: &mut String) {
+    out.push_str(
+        "// Generated by `cargo run -p pathland-jvm-codegen` (lib/rust). Do not edit.\n\
+         // Wire constants are bound to `pathland_core::constants`; regenerate from\n\
+         // lib/rust, not from the Java mirror.\n\n",
+    );
+}
+
+fn package(out: &mut String) {
+    out.push_str("package dev.pathland.view.core.protocol;\n\n");
+}
+
+fn fmt_u8(v: u8) -> String {
+    format!("{v:#04x}")
+}
+
+fn fmt_u16(v: u16) -> String {
+    format!("{v:#06x}")
+}
+
+fn write_int_const(out: &mut String, name: &str, value: String) {
+    writeln!(out, "    public static final int {name} = {value};").unwrap();
+}
+
+fn write_u8_consts(out: &mut String, items: &[(&str, u8)]) {
+    for (name, value) in items {
+        write_int_const(out, name, fmt_u8(*value));
+    }
+}
+
+fn write_u16_consts(out: &mut String, items: &[(&str, u16)]) {
+    for (name, value) in items {
+        write_int_const(out, name, fmt_u16(*value));
+    }
+}
+
+fn emit_components() -> String {
+    let mut out = String::new();
+    header(&mut out);
+    package(&mut out);
+    out.push_str(
+        "/** Protocol component type ids (spec/PRIMITIVES.md). */\n\
+         public final class Components {\n\n",
+    );
+    write_u16_consts(
+        &mut out,
+        &[
+            ("TEXT", component_type::TEXT),
+            ("IMAGE", component_type::IMAGE),
+            ("COLOR", component_type::COLOR),
+            ("SHAPE", component_type::SHAPE),
+            ("DIVIDER", component_type::DIVIDER),
+            ("SPACER", component_type::SPACER),
+            ("PROGRESS_VIEW", component_type::PROGRESS_VIEW),
+            ("GAUGE", component_type::GAUGE),
+            ("VIDEO", component_type::VIDEO),
+            ("ICON", component_type::ICON),
+            ("VSTACK", component_type::VSTACK),
+            ("HSTACK", component_type::HSTACK),
+            ("ZSTACK", component_type::ZSTACK),
+            ("GRID", component_type::GRID),
+            ("SCROLLVIEW", component_type::SCROLLVIEW),
+            ("LAZY_VGRID", component_type::LAZY_VGRID),
+            ("LAZY_HGRID", component_type::LAZY_HGRID),
+            ("SIZE_THAT_FITS", component_type::SIZE_THAT_FITS),
+            ("LAZY_VSTACK", component_type::LAZY_VSTACK),
+            ("LAZY_HSTACK", component_type::LAZY_HSTACK),
+            ("GRID_ROW", component_type::GRID_ROW),
+            ("PROXY_VIEW", component_type::PROXY_VIEW),
+            ("BUTTON", component_type::BUTTON),
+            ("TEXT_FIELD", component_type::TEXT_FIELD),
+            ("TEXT_EDITOR", component_type::TEXT_EDITOR),
+            ("TOGGLE", component_type::TOGGLE),
+            ("SLIDER", component_type::SLIDER),
+            ("STEPPER", component_type::STEPPER),
+            ("DATE_PICKER", component_type::DATE_PICKER),
+            ("PICKER", component_type::PICKER),
+            ("MENU", component_type::MENU),
+            ("COLOR_PICKER", component_type::COLOR_PICKER),
+            ("MEDIA_CONTROLLER", component_type::MEDIA_CONTROLLER),
+            ("COMMENT", component_type::COMMENT),
+        ],
+    );
+    out.push_str("\n    private Components() {}\n}\n");
+    out
+}
+
+fn emit_categories() -> String {
+    let mut out = String::new();
+    header(&mut out);
+    package(&mut out);
+    out.push_str(
+        "/** Opcode categories (spec/OPCODE.md). */\n\
+         public final class Categories {\n\n",
+    );
+    write_u8_consts(
+        &mut out,
+        &[
+            ("TREE", category::TREE),
+            ("PARAMETER", category::PARAMETER),
+            ("EVENT", category::EVENT),
+            ("META", category::META),
+        ],
+    );
+    out.push_str("\n    private Categories() {}\n}\n");
+    out
+}
+
+fn emit_commands() -> String {
+    let mut out = String::new();
+    header(&mut out);
+    package(&mut out);
+    out.push_str(
+        "/** Commands, field ids, flags, and listener bits per category. */\n\
+         public final class Commands {\n\n\
+         \x20   private Commands() {}\n",
+    );
+
+    out.push_str("\n    /** TREE commands. */\n    public static final class Tree {\n");
+    write_u8_consts(
+        &mut out,
+        &[
+            ("CREATE_NODE", tree::CREATE_NODE),
+            ("DELETE_NODE", tree::DELETE_NODE),
+            ("INSERT_CHILD", tree::INSERT_CHILD),
+            ("REMOVE_CHILD", tree::REMOVE_CHILD),
+            ("MOVE_CHILD", tree::MOVE_CHILD),
+        ],
+    );
+    out.push_str("\n        private Tree() {}\n    }\n");
+
+    out.push_str("\n    /** PARAMETER commands. */\n    public static final class Parameter {\n");
+    write_u8_consts(
+        &mut out,
+        &[
+            ("SET_PROPERTY", parameter::SET_PROPERTY),
+            ("SET_DESIGN_TOKEN", parameter::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN),
+            ("SET_TEXT", parameter::SET_TEXT),
+            ("SET_DATE", parameter::SET_DATE),
+        ],
+    );
+    out.push_str("\n        private Parameter() {}\n    }\n");
+
+    out.push_str("\n    /** EVENT commands (host -> guest raw inputs). */\n    public static final class Event {\n");
+    write_u8_consts(
+        &mut out,
+        &[
+            ("POINTER_DOWN", event::POINTER_DOWN),
+            ("POINTER_MOVE", event::POINTER_MOVE),
+            ("POINTER_UP", event::POINTER_UP),
+            ("KEY_DOWN", event::KEY_DOWN),
+            ("KEY_UP", event::KEY_UP),
+            ("VALUE_CHANGED", event::VALUE_CHANGED),
+            ("TEXT_CHANGED", event::TEXT_CHANGED),
+            ("FOCUS_CHANGED", event::FOCUS_CHANGED),
+            ("EDITING_CHANGED", event::EDITING_CHANGED),
+            ("SUBMIT", event::SUBMIT),
+            ("SCROLL", event::SCROLL),
+            ("WHEEL", event::WHEEL),
+            ("DATE_CHANGED", event::DATE_CHANGED),
+            ("NAVIGATE", event::NAVIGATE),
+            ("MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED", event::MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED),
+            ("MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED", event::MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED),
+            ("MEDIA_ENDED", event::MEDIA_ENDED),
+            ("MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED", event::MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED),
+            ("FIT_CHANGED", event::FIT_CHANGED),
+            ("MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED", event::MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED),
+        ],
+    );
+    out.push_str("\n        private Event() {}\n    }\n");
+
+    out.push_str("\n    /** META commands. */\n    public static final class Meta {\n");
+    write_u8_consts(
+        &mut out,
+        &[
+            ("RESET", meta::RESET),
+            ("ENVIRONMENT", meta::ENVIRONMENT),
+            ("RESYNC", meta::RESYNC),
+            ("PING", meta::PING),
+            ("PONG", meta::PONG),
+            ("SET_COLOR_SCHEME", meta::SET_COLOR_SCHEME),
+            ("RESET_THEME", meta::RESET_THEME),
+            ("SET_WINDOW_METADATA", meta::SET_WINDOW_METADATA),
+        ],
+    );
+    out.push_str("\n        private Meta() {}\n    }\n");
+
+    out.push_str("\n    /** META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA field ids. */\n    public static final class WindowFields {\n");
+    write_u16_consts(
+        &mut out,
+        &[
+            ("TITLE", window_field::TITLE),
+            ("DESCRIPTION", window_field::DESCRIPTION),
+            ("LOCALE", window_field::LOCALE),
+        ],
+    );
+    out.push_str("\n        private WindowFields() {}\n    }\n");
+
+    out.push_str("\n    /** META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME modes. */\n    public static final class ColorSchemeMode {\n");
+    write_int_const(
+        &mut out,
+        "PLATFORM",
+        color_scheme_mode::PLATFORM.to_string(),
+    );
+    write_int_const(&mut out, "LIGHT", color_scheme_mode::LIGHT.to_string());
+    write_int_const(&mut out, "DARK", color_scheme_mode::DARK.to_string());
+    out.push_str("\n        private ColorSchemeMode() {}\n    }\n");
+
+    out.push_str(
+        "\n    /** META::ENVIRONMENT field ids. */\n    public static final class Environment {\n",
+    );
+    write_u16_consts(
+        &mut out,
+        &[
+            ("VIEWPORT_WIDTH", environment::VIEWPORT_WIDTH),
+            ("VIEWPORT_HEIGHT", environment::VIEWPORT_HEIGHT),
+            ("ROUTE", environment::ROUTE),
+        ],
+    );
+    out.push_str("\n        private Environment() {}\n    }\n");
+
+    out.push_str(
+        "\n    /** Flag bits shared across categories. */\n    public static final class Flags {\n",
+    );
+    write_u16_consts(
+        &mut out,
+        &[
+            ("POINTER_SECONDARY", flag::POINTER_SECONDARY),
+            ("HOVER_ENTER", flag::HOVER_ENTER),
+            ("HOVER_LEAVE", flag::HOVER_LEAVE),
+            ("KEY_REPEAT", flag::KEY_REPEAT),
+            ("NAVIGATE_URL", flag::NAVIGATE_URL),
+        ],
+    );
+    out.push_str("\n        private Flags() {}\n    }\n");
+
+    out.push_str("\n    /** Bits for the EVENT_LISTENERS semantic property. */\n    public static final class Listeners {\n");
+    for (name, value) in [
+        ("POINTER_DOWN", listener::POINTER_DOWN),
+        ("POINTER_MOVE", listener::POINTER_MOVE),
+        ("POINTER_UP", listener::POINTER_UP),
+        ("KEY_DOWN", listener::KEY_DOWN),
+        ("KEY_UP", listener::KEY_UP),
+        ("FOCUS", listener::FOCUS),
+        ("EDITING", listener::EDITING),
+        ("SUBMIT", listener::SUBMIT),
+        ("SCROLL", listener::SCROLL),
+        ("WHEEL", listener::WHEEL),
+    ] {
+        write_int_const(&mut out, name, format!("{value:#x}"));
+    }
+    write_int_const(&mut out, "POINTER", format!("{:#x}", listener::POINTER));
+    out.push_str("\n        private Listeners() {}\n    }\n");
+
+    out.push_str("\n    /** Special size constants for WIDTH / HEIGHT. */\n    public static final class Size {\n");
+    writeln!(out, "    public static final float FILL = {}f;", size::FILL).unwrap();
+    writeln!(
+        out,
+        "    public static final float HUG_CONTENT = {}f;",
+        size::HUG_CONTENT
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+    out.push_str("\n        private Size() {}\n    }\n");
+
+    out.push_str("}\n");
+    out
+}

+        ("DATE_PICKER_MODE", property_id::DATE_PICKER_MODE),
+        ("PICKER_STYLE", property_id::PICKER_STYLE),
+        ("ACTION_ID", property_id::ACTION_ID),
+        ("BINDING_ID", property_id::BINDING_ID),
+        ("TOGGLE_STYLE", property_id::TOGGLE_STYLE),
+        ("ROUTE", property_id::ROUTE),
+        ("NAV_DEPTH", property_id::NAV_DEPTH),
+        ("NAV_CHROME", property_id::NAV_CHROME),
+    ]
+}
+
+fn emit_properties() -> String {
+    let mut out = String::new();
+    header(&mut out);
+    package(&mut out);
+    out.push_str(
+        "/** Protocol property ids (spec/MODIFIERS.md, spec/OPCODE.md). */\n\
+         public final class Properties {\n\n",
+    );
+    write_u16_consts(&mut out, &properties());
+    out.push_str("\n    private Properties() {}\n}\n");
+    out
+}
+
+fn emit_value_types() -> String {
+    let mut out = String::new();
+    header(&mut out);
+    package(&mut out);
+    out.push_str(
+        "/** Value types for PARAMETER::SET_PROPERTY (spec/OPCODE.md). */\n\
+         public final class ValueTypes {\n\n",
+    );
+    write_u8_consts(
+        &mut out,
+        &[
+            ("U8", value_type::U8),
+            ("U32", value_type::U32),
+            ("I32", value_type::I32),
+            ("F32", value_type::F32),
+            ("STRING", value_type::STRING),
+            ("ENUM", value_type::ENUM),
+            ("COLOR", value_type::COLOR),
+            ("DESIGN_TOKEN", value_type::DESIGN_TOKEN),
+            ("LIST", value_type::LIST),
+        ],
+    );
+
+    out.push_str(
+        "\n    /** The protocol value type for a property id (bound to `value_type_for`). */\n\
+         \x20   public static int forProperty(int prop) {\n\
+         \x20       return switch (prop) {\n",
+    );
+    let mut groups: Vec<(u8, Vec<&str>)> = Vec::new();
+    for (name, value) in properties() {
+        let vt = value_type_for(value);
+        if vt == value_type::F32 {
+            continue;
+        }
+        if let Some((_, names)) = groups.iter_mut().find(|(g, _)| *g == vt) {
+            names.push(name);
+        } else {
+            groups.push((vt, vec![name]));
+        }
+    }
+    for (vt, names) in groups {
+        let value = match vt {
+            value_type::U8 => "U8",
+            value_type::U32 => "U32",
+            value_type::I32 => "I32",
+            value_type::F32 => "F32",
+            value_type::STRING => "STRING",
+            value_type::ENUM => "ENUM",
+            value_type::COLOR => "COLOR",
+            value_type::DESIGN_TOKEN => "DESIGN_TOKEN",
+            value_type::LIST => "LIST",
+            _ => "F32",
+        };
+        let labels: Vec<String> = names
+            .iter()
+            .map(|name| format!("Properties.{name}"))
+            .collect();
+        writeln!(
+            out,
+            "                case {} -> {};",
+            labels.join(", "),
+            value
+        )
+        .unwrap();
+    }
+    out.push_str(
+        "                default -> F32;\n\
+         \x20           };\n\
+         \x20   }\n\n\
+         \x20   private ValueTypes() {}\n\
+         }\n",
+    );
+    out
+}
+
+fn main() -> io::Result<()> {
+    let dir = output_dir();
+    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir)?;
+    for (name, source) in [
+        ("Components.java", emit_components()),
+        ("Categories.java", emit_categories()),
+        ("Commands.java", emit_commands()),
+        ("Properties.java", emit_properties()),
+        ("ValueTypes.java", emit_value_types()),
+    ] {
+        let path = dir.join(name);
+        std::fs::write(&path, source)?;
+        println!("wrote {}", path.display());
+    }
+    Ok(())
+}

Output huge. Key: current branch main. Need create branch. Name e.g. `refactor/jvm-engine-split` or `feat/phase2-jvm-engine-conformance`. User wants phase 1 commit and start phase 2. Could branch `refactor/java-engine-split`. We'll create and commit.

Need decide commit split. Since Kotlin module is untracked and was prior work, but it's part of current working tree. User said commit phase 1; if we commit all including Kotlin facade under phase 1, commit message might be misleading. We can create two commits:
1. `feat(java): add Kotlin DSL facade` (all Kotlin module files + maybe AGENTS addition? But AGENTS now includes both, can't split easily).
2. `refactor(java): split JVM engine into pathland-view-core` (everything else).
However, the Kotlin module is referenced in parent pom and AGENTS, so commit 1 would require parent pom change and AGENTS changes, which also include core. Hard to split cleanly. Could just one commit "refactor(java): split JVM engine into pathland-view-core" including Kotlin facade. That's acceptable because branch/PR can describe both. But user specifically says commit phase 1. Maybe use message:
`refactor(java): split JVM engine into pathland-view-core`
Body: phase 1 engine split; also includes Kotlin DSL facade from prior work? Hmm.

Alternatively commit all with `feat(java): add Kotlin DSL and split JVM engine core`. But phase 1 is main. I'd do one commit with message `refactor(java): split JVM engine into pathland-view-core` and body mentioning package moves, core module, DSL decoupling, tests. The Kotlin module is included as existing uncommitted work; not ideal but okay. Could mention in final that commit includes prior Kotlin facade.

Maybe better: commit Kotlin module separately first (with just its files + parent pom + AGENTS lines) impossible to separate docs. We can use `git add lib/java/pathland-view-kotlin lib/java/pom.xml` for first commit, but then commit parent pom also references core module not yet present -> broken commit. Could create first commit with Kotlin module and parent pom without core? Edit staged version? Too much. Not worth untangling; one commit.

Need stage all current changes including untracked. `git add -A` would include `.entire`? ignored. Check `git status --short` untracked only 4 expected. Fine. But `git add -A` will stage all modifications. Then commit.

Branch creation:
`git switch -c refactor/java-engine-split` (or `feat/phase2-engine-conformance`). Phase 2 will continue on same branch. Name should encompass both: `feat/java-engine-core-conformance` or `refactor/jvm-engine-phase1`. I'd use `feat/jvm-engine-core`? Since phase 2 codegen. Maybe `refactor/jvm-engine-split` then phase 2 commit on same branch; branch name still okay. User said start phase 2, so branch can be `feat/jvm-engine-core-conformance`. Let's pick `refactor/jvm-engine-core` concise.

Need run tests before commit? Already did clean test/install. After docs-only no code. Fine.

Commit.

Promote the package-private seams needed across the new boundary, decouple Environment from DSL default styles, and update processor FQCNs, consumers, tests, docs, and the release workflow. Includes the Kotlin DSL facade module already in the working tree.

Verified with mvn clean test and mvn -DskipTests install."

/// Emit the token conventions (`lib/typescript/src/generated/tokens-core.ts`)
/// from `pathland_render_html::token_spec` — the pure data + pure functions the
/// DOM client imports, so the `--pl-*` naming / length rules cannot drift.
pub fn emit_tokens_core_ts() -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    out.push_str(
        "// Generated by `cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen` (lib/rust). Do not edit.\n\
         // Canonical design-token conventions from `pathland-render-html::token_spec`\n\
         // (spec/TOKENS.md). Regenerate with `npm run regen`.\n\n",
    );
    let q = |s: &str| format!("{s:?}");
    let list = |items: &[&str]| {
        let joined: Vec<String> = items.iter().map(|s| q(*s)).collect();
        format!("[{}]", joined.join(", "))
    };
    let pair_list = |items: &[(&str, &str)]| {
        let joined: Vec<String> = items
            .iter()
            .map(|(a, b)| format!("[{}, {}]", q(*a), q(*b)))
            .collect();
        format!("[{}]", joined.join(", "))
    };
    writeln!(out, "export const DARK_PREFIX = {};", q(token_spec::DARK_PREFIX)).unwrap();
    writeln!(out, "export const VAR_PREFIX = {};", q(token_spec::VAR_PREFIX)).unwrap();
    writeln!(
        out,
        "export const FORCED_DARK_VAR_PREFIX = {};",
        q(token_spec::FORCED_DARK_VAR_PREFIX)
    )
    .unwrap();
    writeln!(out, "export const SPACE_FAMILY = {};", q(token_spec::SPACE_FAMILY)).unwrap();
    writeln!(
        out,
        "export const LENGTH_PREFIXES: readonly string[] = {};",
        list(token_spec::LENGTH_PREFIXES)
    )
    .unwrap();
    writeln!(
        out,
        out,
        "export const LENGTH_PREFIX_SUFFIX: ReadonlyArray<readonly [string, string]> = {};",
        pair_list(token_spec::LENGTH_PREFIX_SUFFIX)
    )
    .unwrap();
    writeln!(
        out,
        "export const LENGTH_EXACT: readonly string[] = {};",
        list(token_spec::LENGTH_EXACT)
    )
    .unwrap();
    writeln!(
        out,
        "export const LENGTH_ELEVATION_SUFFIXES: readonly string[] = {};",
        list(token_spec::LENGTH_ELEVATION_SUFFIXES)
    )
    .unwrap();
    out.push_str(
        "\n/** The canonical CSS custom property for a token path: `--pl-` prefix, `.` → `-`.\n \
         *  The `dark.` scheme prefix is stripped — the dark variant overrides the same\n \
         *  variable inside a media query. */\n\
         export function tokenToCssVar(path: string): string {\n\
         \x20 const bare = path.startsWith(DARK_PREFIX) ? path.slice(DARK_PREFIX.length) : path;\n\
         \x20 return VAR_PREFIX + bare.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/g, \"-\");\n\
         }\n\n\
         /** Whether a token path selects the dark variant. */\n\
         export function isDarkToken(path: string): boolean {\n\
         \x20 return path.startsWith(DARK_PREFIX);\n\
         }\n\n\
         /** The forced-dark variable for a token path (`--pl-dark-<path>`). */\n\
         export function tokenToForcedDarkCssVar(path: string): string {\n\
         \x20 const bare = path.startsWith(DARK_PREFIX) ? path.slice(DARK_PREFIX.length) : path;\n\
         \x20 return FORCED_DARK_VAR_PREFIX + bare.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/g, \"-\");\n\
         }\n\n\
         /** Token paths whose F32 values are CSS lengths (emitted with `px`). */\n\
         export function isLengthToken(path: string): boolean {\n\
         \x20 for (const prefix of LENGTH_PREFIXES) {\n\
         \x20\x20 if (path.startsWith(prefix)) return true;\n\
         \x20 }\n\
         \x20 for (const [prefix, suffix] of LENGTH_PREFIX_SUFFIX) {\n\
         \x20\x20 if (path.startsWith(prefix) && path.endsWith(suffix)) return true;\n\
         \x20 }\n\
         \x20 if (LENGTH_EXACT.includes(path)) return true;\n\
         \x20 return path.startsWith(\"elevation.\") && LENGTH_ELEVATION_SUFFIXES.some((s) => path.endsWith(s));\n\
         }\n\n\
         /** Resolve a `DESIGN_TOKEN` property reference to a CSS expression: the\n\
          *  generative `space.<N>` family resolves to `calc(var(--pl-space-base) * N)`;\n\
          *  an explicit `dark.` reference uses the forced-dark variable family; every\n\
          *  other token resolves to `var(--pl-<path>, unset)`. */\n\
         export function resolveTokenCssRef(path: string): string {\n\
         \x20 const forcedDark = path.startsWith(DARK_PREFIX);\n\
         \x20 const bare = forcedDark ? path.slice(DARK_PREFIX.length) : path;\n\
         \x20 if (bare.startsWith(SPACE_FAMILY)) {\n\
         \x20\x20 const rest = bare.slice(SPACE_FAMILY.length);\n\
         \x20\x20 if (rest.length > 0 && !Number.isNaN(Number(rest))) {\n\
         \x20\x20\x20 const base = forcedDark ? \"--pl-dark-space-base\" : \"--pl-space-base\";\n\
         \x20\x20\x20 return `calc(var(${base}) * ${rest})`;\n\
         \x20\x20 }\n\
         \x20 }\n\
         \x20 if (forcedDark) {\n\
         \x20\x20 return `var(${tokenToForcedDarkCssVar(bare)}, unset)`;\n\
         \x20 }\n\
         \x20 return `var(${tokenToCssVar(bare)}, unset)`;\n\
         }\n",
    );
    out
}

/// Emit the role→semantic-element conventions (`generated/role-spec.ts`) from
/// `pathland_render_html::role_spec` — the single source the Rust SSR renderer
/// and the DOM client share for semantic tags / ARIA fallbacks.
pub fn emit_role_spec_ts() -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    out.push_str(
        "// Generated by `cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen` (lib/rust). Do not edit.\n\
         // Canonical ROLE → semantic HTML element mapping from\n\
         // `pathland-render-html::role_spec` (spec/OPCODE.md §semantic properties).\n\
         // Regenerate with `npm run regen`.\n\n",
    );
    let q = |s: &str| format!("{s:?}");
    let nums = |items: &[u16]| {
        let joined: Vec<String> = items.iter().map(|v| format!("{v:#06x}")).collect();
        format!("[{}]", joined.join(", "))
    };
    writeln!(
        out,
        "export const GENERIC_COMPONENTS: readonly number[] = {};",
        nums(role_spec::GENERIC_COMPONENTS)
    )
    .unwrap();
    writeln!(
        out,
        "export const NATIVE_ROLE_COMPONENTS: readonly number[] = {};",
        nums(role_spec::NATIVE_ROLE_COMPONENTS)
    )
    .unwrap();
    out.push_str(
        "export interface RoleTag {\n\
         \x20 role: number;\n\
         \x20 tag: string;\n\
         \x20 aria: string;\n\
         }\n\n",
    );
    out.push_str("export const ROLE_TAGS: readonly RoleTag[] = [\n");
    for rt in role_spec::ROLE_TAGS {
        writeln!(out, "  {{ role: {}, tag: {}, aria: {} }},", rt.role, q(rt.tag), q(rt.aria)).unwrap();
    }
    out.push_str("];\n\n");
    let heading_pairs: Vec<String> = role_spec::HEADING_STYLES
        .iter()
        .map(|(style, level)| format!("[{style}, {level}]"))
        .collect();
    writeln!(
        out,
        "export const HEADING_STYLES: ReadonlyArray<readonly [number, number]> = [{}];",
        heading_pairs.join(", ")
    )
    .unwrap();
    out.push_str(
        "\n/** The heading level a `TEXT_STYLE` typography implies, or null for the\n \
         *  non-heading styles (Subheadline, Body, Caption, …). */\n\
         export function headingLevel(textStyle: number): number | null {\n\
         \x20 const found = HEADING_STYLES.find(([s]) => s === textStyle);\n\
         \x20 return found ? found[1] : null;\n\
         }\n\n\
         /** The heading element tag for a level (1 → `h1` … 5 → `h5`). */\n\
         export function headingTag(level: number): string {\n\
         \x20 return \"h\" + String(level);\n\
         }\n\n\
         /** A shell's role behavior (see `pathland-render-html::role_spec`).\n \
          *  Generic `div`/`span` shells may be retagged; native controls convey\n \
          *  their own role; anything else only gets an ARIA attribute. */\n\
         export type ShellKind = \"generic\" | \"native\" | \"other\";\n\n\
         /** The semantic tag a `(shell kind, role)` pair resolves to, or null. */\n\
         export function semanticTag(kind: ShellKind, role: number): string | null {\n\
         \x20 if (kind !== \"generic\") return null;\n\
         \x20 const found = ROLE_TAGS.find((r) => r.role === role);\n\
         \x20 return found ? found.tag : null;\n\
         }\n\n\
         /** The effective tag for a generic TEXT shell: a heading `TEXT_STYLE`\n\
          *  wins (always a heading), then the semantic role (`ROLE_HEADER` → `<h2>`,\n\
          *  `ROLE_PARAGRAPH` → `<p>`, landmarks), else null (→ `<span>`). */\n\
         export function textTag(kind: ShellKind, role: number, textStyle: number | null): string | null {\n\
         \x20 if (kind === \"generic\" && textStyle !== null) {\n\
         \x20\x20 const level = headingLevel(textStyle);\n\
         \x20\x20 if (level !== null) return headingTag(level);\n\
         \x20 }\n\
         \x20 return semanticTag(kind, role);\n\
         }\n\n\
         /** The ARIA `role` value to emit for `(shell kind, role)`, or null when\n\
          *  the element already conveys the role (a semantic tag or a native control). */\n\
         export function ariaRole(kind: ShellKind, role: number): string | null {\n\
         \x20 if (kind === \"native\") return null;\n\
         \x20 const tagged = ROLE_TAGS.find((r) => r.role === role);\n\
         \x20 if (tagged) {\n\
         \x20\x20 return kind === \"generic\" ? null : tagged.aria;\n\
         \x20 }\n\
         \x20 return null;\n\
         }\n",
    );
    out
}

fn main() -> io::Result<()> {
    let consts = constants_ts_path();
    std::fs::write(&consts, emit_constants_ts())?;
    println!("wrote {}", consts.display());
    let tokens = tokens_core_ts_path();
    if let Some(parent) = tokens.parent() {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
    }
    std::fs::write(&tokens, emit_tokens_core_ts())?;
    println!("wrote {}", tokens.display());
    let roles = role_spec_ts_path();
    if let Some(parent) = roles.parent() {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
    }
    std::fs::write(&roles, emit_role_spec_ts())?;
    println!("wrote {}", roles.display());
    Ok(())
}

/// Emit the token conventions (`lib/typescript/src/generated/tokens-core.ts`)
/// from `pathland_render_html::token_spec` — the pure data + pure functions the
/// DOM client imports, so the `--pl-*` naming / length rules cannot drift.
pub fn emit_tokens_core_ts() -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    out.push_str(
        "// Generated by `cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen` (lib/rust). Do not edit.\n\
         // Canonical design-token conventions from `pathland-render-html::token_spec`\n\
         // (spec/TOKENS.md). Regenerate with `npm run regen`.\n\n",
    );
    let q = |s: &str| format!("{s:?}");
    let list = |items: &[&str]| {
        let joined: Vec<String> = items.iter().map(|s| q(*s)).collect();
        format!("[{}]", joined.join(", "))
    };
    let pair_list = |items: &[(&str, &str)]| {
        let joined: Vec<String> = items
            .iter()
            .map(|(a, b)| format!("[{}, {}]", q(*a), q(*b)))
            .collect();
        format!("[{}]", joined.join(", "))
    };
    writeln!(out, "export const DARK_PREFIX = {};", q(token_spec::DARK_PREFIX)).unwrap();
    writeln!(out, "export const VAR_PREFIX = {};", q(token_spec::VAR_PREFIX)).unwrap();
    writeln!(
        out,
        "export const FORCED_DARK_VAR_PREFIX = {};",
        q(token_spec::FORCED_DARK_VAR_PREFIX)
    )
    .unwrap();
    writeln!(out, "export const SPACE_FAMILY = {};", q(token_spec::SPACE_FAMILY)).unwrap();
    writeln!(
        out,
        "export const LENGTH_PREFIXES: readonly string[] = {};",
        list(token_spec::LENGTH_PREFIXES)
    )
    .unwrap();
    writeln!(
        out,
        out,
        "export const LENGTH_PREFIX_SUFFIX: ReadonlyArray<readonly [string, string]> = {};",
        pair_list(token_spec::LENGTH_PREFIX_SUFFIX)
    )
    .unwrap();
    writeln!(
        out,
        "export const LENGTH_EXACT: readonly string[] = {};",
        list(token_spec::LENGTH_EXACT)
    )
    .unwrap();
    writeln!(
        out,
        "export const LENGTH_ELEVATION_SUFFIXES: readonly string[] = {};",
        list(token_spec::LENGTH_ELEVATION_SUFFIXES)
    )
    .unwrap();
    out.push_str(
        "\n/** The canonical CSS custom property for a token path: `--pl-` prefix, `.` → `-`.\n \
         *  The `dark.` scheme prefix is stripped — the dark variant overrides the same\n \
         *  variable inside a media query. */\n\
         export function tokenToCssVar(path: string): string {\n\
         \x20 const bare = path.startsWith(DARK_PREFIX) ? path.slice(DARK_PREFIX.length) : path;\n\
         \x20 return VAR_PREFIX + bare.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/g, \"-\");\n\
         }\n\n\
         /** Whether a token path selects the dark variant. */\n\
         export function isDarkToken(path: string): boolean {\n\
         \x20 return path.startsWith(DARK_PREFIX);\n\
         }\n\n\
         /** The forced-dark variable for a token path (`--pl-dark-<path>`). */\n\
         export function tokenToForcedDarkCssVar(path: string): string {\n\
         \x20 const bare = path.startsWith(DARK_PREFIX) ? path.slice(DARK_PREFIX.length) : path;\n\
         \x20 return FORCED_DARK_VAR_PREFIX + bare.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/g, \"-\");\n\
         }\n\n\
         /** Token paths whose F32 values are CSS lengths (emitted with `px`). */\n\
         export function isLengthToken(path: string): boolean {\n\
         \x20 for (const prefix of LENGTH_PREFIXES) {\n\
         \x20\x20 if (path.startsWith(prefix)) return true;\n\
         \x20 }\n\
         \x20 for (const [prefix, suffix] of LENGTH_PREFIX_SUFFIX) {\n\
         \x20\x20 if (path.startsWith(prefix) && path.endsWith(suffix)) return true;\n\
         \x20 }\n\
         \x20 if (LENGTH_EXACT.includes(path)) return true;\n\
         \x20 return path.startsWith(\"elevation.\") && LENGTH_ELEVATION_SUFFIXES.some((s) => path.endsWith(s));\n\
         }\n\n\
         /** Resolve a `DESIGN_TOKEN` property reference to a CSS expression: the\n\
          *  generative `space.<N>` family resolves to `calc(var(--pl-space-base) * N)`;\n\
          *  an explicit `dark.` reference uses the forced-dark variable family; every\n\
          *  other token resolves to `var(--pl-<path>, unset)`. */\n\
         export function resolveTokenCssRef(path: string): string {\n\
         \x20 const forcedDark = path.startsWith(DARK_PREFIX);\n\
         \x20 const bare = forcedDark ? path.slice(DARK_PREFIX.length) : path;\n\
         \x20 if (bare.startsWith(SPACE_FAMILY)) {\n\
         \x20\x20 const rest = bare.slice(SPACE_FAMILY.length);\n\
         \x20\x20 if (rest.length > 0 && !Number.isNaN(Number(rest))) {\n\
         \x20\x20\x20 const base = forcedDark ? \"--pl-dark-space-base\" : \"--pl-space-base\";\n\
         \x20\x20\x20 return `calc(var(${base}) * ${rest})`;\n\
         \x20\x20 }\n\
         \x20 }\n\
         \x20 if (forcedDark) {\n\
         \x20\x20 return `var(${tokenToForcedDarkCssVar(bare)}, unset)`;\n\
         \x20 }\n\
         \x20 return `var(${tokenToCssVar(bare)}, unset)`;\n\
         }\n",
    );
    out
}

/// Emit the role→semantic-element conventions (`generated/role-spec.ts`) from
/// `pathland_render_html::role_spec` — the single source the Rust SSR renderer
/// and the DOM client share for semantic tags / ARIA fallbacks.
pub fn emit_role_spec_ts() -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    out.push_str(
        "// Generated by `cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen` (lib/rust). Do not edit.\n\
         // Canonical ROLE → semantic HTML element mapping from\n\
         // `pathland-render-html::role_spec` (spec/OPCODE.md §semantic properties).\n\
         // Regenerate with `npm run regen`.\n\n",
    );
    let q = |s: &str| format!("{s:?}");
    let nums = |items: &[u16]| {
        let joined: Vec<String> = items.iter().map(|v| format!("{v:#06x}")).collect();
        format!("[{}]", joined.join(", "))
    };
    writeln!(
        out,
        "export const GENERIC_COMPONENTS: readonly number[] = {};",
        nums(role_spec::GENERIC_COMPONENTS)
    )
    .unwrap();
    writeln!(
        out,
        "export const NATIVE_ROLE_COMPONENTS: readonly number[] = {};",
        nums(role_spec::NATIVE_ROLE_COMPONENTS)
    )
    .unwrap();
    out.push_str(
        "export interface RoleTag {\n\
         \x20 role: number;\n\
         \x20 tag: string;\n\
         \x20 aria: string;\n\
         }\n\n",
    );
    out.push_str("export const ROLE_TAGS: readonly RoleTag[] = [\n");
    for rt in role_spec::ROLE_TAGS {
        writeln!(out, "  {{ role: {}, tag: {}, aria: {} }},", rt.role, q(rt.tag), q(rt.aria)).unwrap();
    }
    out.push_str("];\n\n");
    let heading_pairs: Vec<String> = role_spec::HEADING_STYLES
        .iter()
        .map(|(style, level)| format!("[{style}, {level}]"))
        .collect();
    writeln!(
        out,
        "export const HEADING_STYLES: ReadonlyArray<readonly [number, number]> = [{}];",
        heading_pairs.join(", ")
    )
    .unwrap();
    out.push_str(
        "\n/** The heading level a `TEXT_STYLE` typography implies, or null for the\n \
         *  non-heading styles (Subheadline, Body, Caption, …). */\n\
         export function headingLevel(textStyle: number): number | null {\n\
         \x20 const found = HEADING_STYLES.find(([s]) => s === textStyle);\n\
         \x20 return found ? found[1] : null;\n\
         }\n\n\
         /** The heading element tag for a level (1 → `h1` … 5 → `h5`). */\n\
         export function headingTag(level: number): string {\n\
         \x20 return \"h\" + String(level);\n\
         }\n\n\
         /** A shell's role behavior (see `pathland-render-html::role_spec`).\n \
          *  Generic `div`/`span` shells may be retagged; native controls convey\n \
          *  their own role; anything else only gets an ARIA attribute. */\n\
         export type ShellKind = \"generic\" | \"native\" | \"other\";\n\n\
         /** The semantic tag a `(shell kind, role)` pair resolves to, or null. */\n\
         export function semanticTag(kind: ShellKind, role: number): string | null {\n\
         \x20 if (kind !== \"generic\") return null;\n\
         \x20 const found = ROLE_TAGS.find((r) => r.role === role);\n\
         \x20 return found ? found.tag : null;\n\
         }\n\n\
         /** The effective tag for a generic TEXT shell: a heading `TEXT_STYLE`\n\
          *  wins (always a heading), then the semantic role (`ROLE_HEADER` → `<h2>`,\n\
          *  `ROLE_PARAGRAPH` → `<p>`, landmarks), else null (→ `<span>`). */\n\
         export function textTag(kind: ShellKind, role: number, textStyle: number | null): string | null {\n\
         \x20 if (kind === \"generic\" && textStyle !== null) {\n\
         \x20\x20 const level = headingLevel(textStyle);\n\
         \x20\x20 if (level !== null) return headingTag(level);\n\
         \x20 }\n\
         \x20 return semanticTag(kind, role);\n\
         }\n\n\
         /** The ARIA `role` value to emit for `(shell kind, role)`, or null when\n\

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, 'docs/**', 'feature/**', 'fix/**', 'spec/**']
  pull_request:

jobs:
  design:
    name: Design (Style Dictionary)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: design/package-lock.json

      # Build the generated token CSS / manifest / bundle and validate the
      # three token layers against the protocol catalog, dark/forced-dark
      # rules, and the canonical length conventions.
      - name: Install, build, check
        working-directory: design
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run build
          npm run check

      # The Rust renderer embeds the generated bundle (committed for packaging).
      - name: Verify the committed renderer CSS matches the design build
        run: scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check

  rust:
    name: Rust (workspace + C ABI + no_std/wasm)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [design]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # The workspace includes pathland-render-gtk (GTK4 + libadwaita + GStreamer)
      # and pathland-render-qt (Qt Quick), so the runner needs the GTK4,
      # libadwaita, GStreamer, and Qt system libraries before `cargo test` can
      # link them. GStreamer is required because the GTK renderer plays app-driven
      # media through a direct GStreamer playbin (GTK4's own media backend is
      # compiled out of some builds); the plugins are the runtime set the audio
      # stack uses (playbin, volume/audioconvert, mp3 decode). The Qt libraries
      # are installed in the next step.
      - name: Install GTK4 + libadwaita + GStreamer system dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libgtk-4-dev \
            libadwaita-1-dev \
            libglib2.0-dev \
            libcairo2-dev \
            libpango1.0-dev \
            libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-dev \
            libgraphene-1.0-dev \
            libgstreamer1.0-dev \
            gstreamer1.0-plugins-base \
            gstreamer1.0-plugins-good \
            gstreamer1.0-libav

      - name: Install Qt6 (QML/Quick) system dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            qt6-base-dev \
            qt6-declarative-dev \
            qt6-declarative-private-dev \
            qt6-multimedia-dev \
            qml6-module-qtqml \
            qml6-module-qtqml-models \
            qml6-module-qtqml-workerscript \
            qml6-module-qtquick \
            qml6-module-qtquick-layouts \
            qml6-module-qtquick-controls \
            qml6-module-qtquick-templates \
            qml6-module-qtquick-window \
            qml6-module-qtmultimedia
        # The dev headers alone don't ship the QML runtime modules; the Qt
        # renderer's offscreen tests instantiate the QML (QtQml + WorkerScript,
        # Items, stacks/Grid via QtQuick.Layouts, Qt Quick Controls, Multimedia)
        # through QQmlComponent, so the qml6-module-* runtime files are required
        # too. Note the Qt6 package names: `-window` (the Qt5 `-window2` name
        # does not exist), and private headers need qt6-declarative-private-dev.

      - name: Install Rust (stable + wasm32 target)
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown

      - name: Cache cargo
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: lib/rust -> target

      - name: Test workspace
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo test

      - name: Qt renderer headless smoke
        working-directory: lib/rust
        env:
          QT_QPA_PLATFORM: offscreen
          QT_QUICK_BACKEND: software
        run: cargo test -p pathland-render-qt

      # The DOM renderer's constants/token conventions and the cross-renderer SSR
      # golden fixtures are GENERATED from Rust (pathland-ts-codegen /
      # pathland-html-golden). Regenerate them here and fail if the committed
      # files drifted — so a renumbered constant or a changed SSR shape can't land
      # without its TS/fixture counterparts.
      - name: Verify generated TS + golden fixtures are current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen
          cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit
          git diff --exit-code -- \
            lib/typescript/src/constants.ts \
            lib/typescript/src/generated \
            lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr

      - name: Build the C ABI (cdylib, used by the Java JNA ring interop / native hosts)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-core-capi

      - name: no_std / wasm32 direction guard
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: ./check-wasm.sh

      # The Java HTML renderer shim needs the Rust renderer cdylib (the jar embeds
      # it so it travels with the artifact). Build it here and hand it to the java
      # job via an artifact.
      - name: Build the HTML renderer cdylib
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-render-html

      - name: Upload the renderer dylib for the java job
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pathland-render-html-native
          path: lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_html.so
          retention-days: 1

  java:
    name: Java (Maven reactor, JDK ${{ matrix.java }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [rust]
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        java: ['17', '21', '25']
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Whole-stack floor is Java 17 (maven.compiler.release=17; JNA native binding,
      # thread-local environment); the matrix proves every LTS from 17.
      - name: Set up JDK ${{ matrix.java }}
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: ${{ matrix.java }}
          cache: maven

      # The renderer jar embeds the Rust cdylib (built by the rust job). Restore it
      # into the debug dir the jar-embed step copies.
      - name: Download the Rust renderer dylib
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pathland-render-html-native
          path: lib/rust/target/debug

      - name: Test reactor (incl. the SSR web demos)
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: mvn -q -B test

  web-client:
    name: Web client (TypeScript DOM renderer)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: lib/typescript/package-lock.json

      - name: Install, typecheck, test, build
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run typecheck
          npm test
          npm run build

      # The demos serve the committed bundle from their static resource dirs
      # (content-hashed dom-renderer-<sha256>.js + the dom-renderer.current
      # pointer; stale hashed copies are pruned); copying the freshly built one
      # must not change the working tree.
      - name: Verify the committed bundle matches the source (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: |
          npm run copy-to-demos
          git diff --exit-code -- lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/src/main/resources lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-demo/src/main/resources

      # Real-browser guard for the per-window-id service worker: the browser-variance
      # bugs (WebKit reports an empty clientId on navigations; relative cache keys are
      # rejected) only appear in a real worker engine, never in jsdom/happy-dom.
      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit

      - name: Service worker E2E (Chromium + WebKit)
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: npm run test:e2e

Agreed — that generator was the wrong shape. It embeds Java package names, class structure, formatting, and constant lists in Rust, so Rust is “writing Java,” not defining protocol data. I’ve stopped.

## Corrected Phase 2 direction

Rust should emit **target-neutral protocol data**, not Java source. A Java-side consumer should decide how Java represents it.

### Option A — Neutral manifest + Java-side generator (recommended)

1. Add a Rust `pathland-protocol-manifest` tool.
   - Reads `pathland_core::constants`.
   - Emits a neutral file such as `spec/protocol.tsv` or `spec/protocol.json`.
   - Contains only data: `kind`, `group`, `name`, `value`.
   - No Java packages, class names, comments, or formatting.

2. Add a small Java generator in the Java reactor.
   - Reads the neutral manifest.
   - Emits `Components`, `Categories`, `Commands`, `Properties`, `ValueTypes`.
   - Owns all Java formatting and naming.
   - Runs via a Maven profile or a dedicated codegen module.

3. CI:
   - Rust emits the manifest.
   - Java regenerates constants.
   - `git diff --exit-code` catches drift.

This keeps Rust as the wire-ID source while removing Rust→Java source coupling.

### Option B — Neutral manifest + validation only

- Rust emits the same neutral manifest.
- Keep Java constants hand-written.
- Add a Java test that parses the manifest and asserts every Java constant matches.
- No generated Java at all.

This is the lowest-risk option, but property additions still require two manual edits; CI only catches the mistake.

### Option C — Protocol-first IDL

- Move IDs into a neutral `spec/protocol.toml`/`protocol.json`.
- Generate both Rust and Java from it.
- Best long-term separation, but a much larger migration because Rust currently uses compile-time constants throughout.

## Recommendation

Option A: neutral manifest, Java-owned generation. It preserves automation without Rust handcoding Java.

## Cleanup plan for the abandoned attempt

- Delete `lib/rust/crates/pathland-jvm-codegen/`.
- Revert generated formatting/header changes to the five Java protocol classes.
- Keep the separate `FIT_QUERY -> LIST` correction in Rust `value_type_for` only if we want to fix that drift independently.
- Revert `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` changes from the abandoned crate.
- Then implement the chosen manifest mechanism.
- After that, continue with `spec/ENGINE.md` and shared engine trace fixtures.
