 name: CI
 
 on:
   push:
     branches: [main, 'docs/**', 'feature/**', 'fix/**', 'refactor/**', 'spec/**']
   pull_request:
 
 jobs:
   design:
     name: Design (Style Dictionary)
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
 
       - name: Set up Node 22
         uses: actions/setup-node@v4
         with:
           node-version: '22'
           cache: npm
           cache-dependency-path: design/package-lock.json
 
       # Build the generated token CSS / manifest / bundle and validate the
       # three token layers against the protocol catalog, dark/forced-dark
       # rules, and the canonical length conventions.
       - name: Install, build, check
         working-directory: design
         run: |
           npm ci
           npm run build
           npm run check
 
       # The Rust renderer embeds the generated bundle (committed for packaging).
       - name: Verify the committed renderer CSS matches the design build
         run: scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check
 
   rust:
     name: Rust (workspace + C ABI + no_std/wasm)
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     needs: [design]
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
 
       # The workspace includes pathland-render-gtk (GTK4 + libadwaita + GStreamer)
       # and pathland-render-qt (Qt Quick), so the runner needs the GTK4,
       # libadwaita, GStreamer, and Qt system libraries before `cargo test` can
       # link them. GStreamer is required because the GTK renderer plays app-driven
       # media through a direct GStreamer playbin (GTK4's own media backend is
       # compiled out of some builds); the plugins are the runtime set the audio
       # stack uses (playbin, volume/audioconvert, mp3 decode). The Qt libraries
       # are installed in the next step.
       - name: Install GTK4 + libadwaita + GStreamer system dependencies
         run: |
           sudo apt-get update
           sudo apt-get install -y \
             libgtk-4-dev \
             libadwaita-1-dev \
             libglib2.0-dev \
             libcairo2-dev \
             libpango1.0-dev \
             libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-dev \
             libgraphene-1.0-dev \
             libgstreamer1.0-dev \
             gstreamer1.0-plugins-base \
             gstreamer1.0-plugins-good \
             gstreamer1.0-libav
 
       - name: Install Qt6 (QML/Quick) system dependencies
         run: |
           sudo apt-get install -y \
             qt6-base-dev \
             qt6-declarative-dev \
             qt6-declarative-private-dev \
             qt6-multimedia-dev \
             qml6-module-qtqml \
             qml6-module-qtqml-models \
             qml6-module-qtqml-workerscript \
             qml6-module-qtquick \
             qml6-module-qtquick-layouts \
             qml6-module-qtquick-controls \
             qml6-module-qtquick-templates \
             qml6-module-qtquick-window \
             qml6-module-qtmultimedia
         # The dev headers alone don't ship the QML runtime modules; the Qt
         # renderer's offscreen tests instantiate the QML (QtQml + WorkerScript,
         # Items, stacks/Grid via QtQuick.Layouts, Qt Quick Controls, Multimedia)
         # through QQmlComponent, so the qml6-module-* runtime files are required
         # too. Note the Qt6 package names: `-window` (the Qt5 `-window2` name
         # does not exist), and private headers need qt6-declarative-private-dev.
 
       - name: Install Rust (stable + wasm32 target)
         uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
         with:
           targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown
 
       - name: Cache cargo
         uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
         with:
           workspaces: lib/rust -> target
 
       - name: Test workspace
         working-directory: lib/rust
         run: cargo test
 
       - name: Qt renderer headless smoke
         working-directory: lib/rust
         env:
           QT_QPA_PLATFORM: offscreen
           QT_QUICK_BACKEND: software
         run: cargo test -p pathland-render-qt
 
       # The DOM renderer's constants/token conventions and the cross-renderer SSR
       # golden fixtures are GENERATED from Rust (pathland-ts-codegen /
       # pathland-html-golden). Regenerate them here and fail if the committed
       # files drifted — so a renumbered constant or a changed SSR shape can't land
       # without its TS/fixture counterparts.
       - name: Verify generated TS + golden fixtures are current (no drift)
         working-directory: lib/rust
         run: |
           cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen
           cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit
           git diff --exit-code -- \
             lib/typescript/src/constants.ts \
             lib/typescript/src/generated \
             lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr
 
       # The neutral protocol manifest is the machine-readable mirror consumed by
       # non-Rust bindings. Regenerate it from the canonical Rust constants and fail
       # if the committed `spec/protocol.tsv` drifted. The Java job validates its
       # hand-written constants against this file.
       - name: Verify the protocol manifest is current (no drift)
         working-directory: lib/rust
         run: |
           cargo run -p pathland-protocol-manifest
           git -C ../.. diff --exit-code -- spec/protocol.tsv
 
+      # The shared engine traces are emitted by the canonical Rust engine and
+      # compared byte-for-byte by the JVM engine test. Verify the committed
+      # fixtures have not drifted from the current engine behavior.
+      - name: Verify engine trace fixtures are current (no drift)
+        working-directory: lib/rust
+        run: cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --check
+
       - name: Build the C ABI (cdylib, used by the Java JNA ring interop / native hosts)
         working-directory: lib/rust
         run: cargo build -p pathland-core-capi
 
       - name: no_std / wasm32 direction guard
         working-directory: lib/rust
         run: ./check-wasm.sh
 
       # The Java HTML renderer shim needs the Rust renderer cdylib (the jar embeds
       # it so it travels with the artifact). Build it here and hand it to the java
       # job via an artifact.
       - name: Build the HTML renderer cdylib
         working-directory: lib/rust
         run: cargo build -p pathland-render-html
 
       - name: Upload the renderer dylib for the java job
         uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
         with:
           name: pathland-render-html-native
           path: lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_html.so
           retention-days: 1
 
   java:
     name: Java (Maven reactor, JDK ${{ matrix.java }})
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     needs: [rust]
     strategy:
       fail-fast: false
       matrix:
         java: ['17', '21', '25']
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
 
       # Whole-stack floor is Java 17 (maven.compiler.release=17; JNA native binding,
       # thread-local environment); the matrix proves every LTS from 17.
       - name: Set up JDK ${{ matrix.java }}
         uses: actions/setup-java@v4
         with:
           distribution: temurin
           java-version: ${{ matrix.java }}
           cache: maven
 
       # The renderer jar embeds the Rust cdylib (built by the rust job). Restore it
       # into the debug dir the jar-embed step copies.
       - name: Download the Rust renderer dylib
         uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
         with:
           name: pathland-render-html-native
           path: lib/rust/target/debug
 
       - name: Test reactor (incl. the SSR web demos)
         working-directory: lib/java
         run: mvn -q -B test
 
   web-client:
     name: Web client (TypeScript DOM renderer)
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
 
       - name: Set up Node 22
         uses: actions/setup-node@v4
         with:
           node-version: '22'
           cache: npm
           cache-dependency-path: lib/typescript/package-lock.json
 
       - name: Install, typecheck, test, build

           npm ci
           npm run typecheck

       - name: Verify the committed bundle matches the source (no drift)

--- AGENTS.md	
+++ AGENTS.md	
@@ -1,694 +1,701 @@
 # Pathland Project - AI Agent Guide
 
 This document provides essential context for AI agents (or human contributors) working on the **Pathland** protocol. It captures the project's direction, architectural decisions, and implementation details to ensure consistency.
 
 **Last Updated**: November 1, 2026
 
 ---
 
 ## Architecture: Rust Opcode Engine
 
 > The canonical core is a **Rust engine** that emits the application's
 > **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding,
 > alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer** into shared linear
 > memory, consumed by host renderers. View components and modifiers are written
 > in Rust with a SwiftUI-like API, and in Java with the hand-written
 > **`dev.pathland.view` DSL** (reusable library, Java 17+); both drive the engine
 > through the flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-view-native`) over a zero-copy shared
 > ring on desktop.
 
 ### The 16-byte Opcode Engine
 
 - Every opcode is exactly **16 bytes**: `Category (1B) | Command ID (1B) | Flags (2B) | A (4B) | B (4B) | C (4B)`, `#[repr(C, packed)]`, little-endian.
 - A 64-byte cache line holds exactly **4 opcodes** → L1-cache-friendly.
 - Opcodes live in a **ring buffer** in linear memory; the guest writes at `writeCursor`, the host reads from `readCursor`; frame boundaries via a monotonic `frameCount` in the header block.
 - **Both directions are binary**: a second **event ring** (host → guest) carries `EVENT`-category opcodes. The renderer writes raw inputs at `eventWriteCursor`; the guest drains them at `eventReadCursor`. Events are 16-byte opcodes through the engine, never a side-channel callback.
 - **Variable-length data** (strings, token paths) lives in a bump **arena**; opcodes reference entries by offset (`[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`), so every opcode stays 16 bytes. A second host-owned **event arena** mirrors this in the host → guest direction (shared-memory event strings, e.g. `TEXT_CHANGED`); over the network, host → guest strings ride the batch's string section.
 - **Window metadata** (`META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA`, field family `TITLE`/`DESCRIPTION`/`LOCALE`) carries the hosting surface's presentation metadata; renderers map it to their own chrome (browser `<title>`/meta description/`<html lang>`, GTK/Qt window title). It is root-scoped and signal-backed, so a route title is a computed over the router. Web-only artifacts (canonical/robots/sitemap) stay host-owned.
 - Spec: **`spec/OPCODE.md`** (primary) + **`spec/CONFORMANCE.md`** (golden vectors). Companion catalogs: **`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`** (views), **`spec/MODIFIERS.md`** (modifiers/properties), **`spec/EVENTS.md`** (events), **`spec/LAYOUT.md`** (frame & layout allocation contract) — draft IDs are allocated there spec-first.
 
 ### Declarative, not positioned (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The engine describes WHAT the UI is — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
 > padding, alignment — never WHERE it is. It does not compute layout and does
 > not emit rects.**
 
 - The engine emits **declarative structure** (`TREE` create/delete/insert/remove/move) + **constraint properties** (`PARAMETER` spacing/padding/alignment/FILL/HUG hints).
 - **Native elements everywhere**: each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that platform's native elements — GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the browser, HTML server-side — and those native elements lay themselves out. Never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent.
 - **Reactive emission**: emission is diff-based. Only the nodes that changed emit opcodes (property diffs via `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT`, structural diffs via `TREE` opcodes). An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes. Signals in the application mark the tree dirty; the engine reconciles.
 - **Zero dynamic heap allocations** during steady-state emission (proven by test).
 
 ### no_std / wasm32 direction guard (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 `pathland-core` and `pathland-view` must remain `#![no_std]` + `alloc` and
 compile for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`. This is the guarantee that the protocol
 core can still target a browser / embedded / remote projection later (goal #15,
 Quarkus SSR + WebSocket). The desktop path (`pathland-view-native`) is the only
 consumer today, but the core must not become desktop-only. Verify with
 `lib/rust/check-wasm.sh` (i.e. `cargo build -p pathland-core -p pathland-view
 --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`).
 
 ### Reactive signals (Angular-style)
 
 `pathland-core::signal` provides writable signals that live in the engine. A
 node binds its text (`Node::text_binding`), a property
 (`Node::property_bindings`) or a **string property** (`Node::string_bindings`,
 e.g. a media controller's `MEDIA_SOURCE`) to a `SignalId`; during emit the engine
 resolves the binding and records the dependency, and `Engine::set_signal`
 re-emits **only the bound nodes** (`SET_TEXT` / `SET_PROPERTY`) — no full tree
 walk. Signal values
 are one of `F32`/`U32`/`Bool`/`Enum`/`Str` (packed to the wire's `u32` value or
 arena string). Foreign hosts reach signals via the flat C ABI
 (`pathland_native_signal_create_*` / `signal_set_*` / `node_bind_text` /
 `node_bind_property`) and the Java `Signal` type. Binding then calling `emit`
 records the dependency; a subsequent `set` is a partial emit. (Computed/derived
 signals + effects are the planned next step.)
 
 ### Rust Workspace (`lib/rust/`)
 
 ```
 # ── The three elements ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 crates/pathland-view/     # RETAINED UI — SwiftUI-style view DSL: VStack/HStack/Text/Button +
                           #   decoupled modifiers (spacing/padding/fontSize/color/background)
                           #   + Video (a MediaController's surface) + attach() (no_std)
 crates/pathland-core/     # PROTOCOL — 16-byte opcode, ring buffer, arena, constants, events,
                           #   memory layout, Guest/Host/Frame surface (no_std, zero-alloc).

 ### HTML base design (`design/`)
 
 The HTML renderer's built-in stylesheet is generated from a **three-layer Style
 Dictionary pipeline** plus hand-authored reset/component CSS (one built-in base
 design; no app-facing base-design selection):
 
 ```
 design/tokens/base/*.tokens.json      # internal palette + scales (not emitted)
 design/tokens/semantic/*.tokens.json  # protocol catalog semantics (emitted)
 design/tokens/component/*.tokens.json # per-component surface (emitted)
 design/html/{reset,components}.css    # hand-authored CSS consuming var(--pl-*)
 design/scripts/{build,dev,check}.mjs  # SD build, watcher/preview, validation
 design/build/base.css                 # generated: reset + tokens + components
 design/build/base.css.name            # content hash: base-<sha256-12>.css
 ```
 
 - Tokens are flat DTCG entries (`$value`/`$type`/`$extensions.pathland`) because
   the catalog has both leaf and group paths (`control.border` vs
   `control.border.width`). Dark values live on `$extensions.pathland.dark`;
   durations/z-index/`em` icon sizes are marked internal.
 - `npm --prefix design run build` generates
   `design/build/{tokens.css,manifest.json,base.css,base.css.name}`;
   `npm --prefix design run check` validates catalog coverage, layer direction,
   dark/forced-dark declarations, dimension/`isLengthToken` rules, and the CSS
   content hash.
 - `scripts/sync-design-css.sh` copies the bundle + name to
   `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/` (committed; `--check` fails on
   drift). `css.rs` embeds both with `include_str!` (`builtin_css()` /
   `builtin_css_name()`).
 - The renderer's library default is inline (`render_document`); the linked mode
   (`render_document_linked`, C ABI `pathland_html_render_linked` +
   `pathland_html_base_css[_name]`, Java `renderLinked`/`baseCss`/`baseCssName`)
   emits `{base}/base-<hash>.css`. The Spring Boot and Quarkus starters use it
   and serve the renderer-owned bytes immutable (global + mounted bases); token
   overrides/fit rules stay inline.
 - `scripts/lib.sh` (`build_rust_html`), the Maven `refresh-ide` profile, and CI
   run the design build + sync. Do not edit generated CSS by hand.
 
 ### Native C-ABI shim (`pathland-view-native` + `pathland-core-capi`)
 
 The **desktop/cross-language zero-copy path**: `pathland-view-native` exposes the
 flat world (the flat `builder`/`engine` surface) as `pathland_native_*` C
 functions with a **shared-memory ring** the host driver reads in place. Any
 language that links the dylib (Swift/Java/C# via FFI) calls the flat surface —
 no per-component wrappers — and consumes opcodes zero-copy.
 
 `pathland-core-capi` (`libpathland_core`) is the **minimal ring C ABI** for the
 Java DSL: `pathland_core_create`/`destroy`, `pathland_ring_buffer_push` (one
 raw 16-byte opcode), `pathland_core_arena_alloc`, frame boundaries, zero-copy
 `ring_ptr`/`ring_len`, and event drain/send. The Java DSL
 (`dev.pathland.view.core.ffm`) binds it with **JNA** (lazily loaded, zero JNI) and
 owns the retained tree + diff emission itself.
 
 ### GTK4 Renderer (`pathland-render-gtk`)
 
 The desktop renderer: a single crate that owns **all** GTK/glib/pango usage and
 maps opcode frames **incrementally** onto native GTK widgets (a retained
 `id → gtk::Widget` map). Both the Rust demo and the Java demo render through
 it — the demos **never call GTK or Swing directly**:
 
 - Rust demo links `pathland-render-gtk` as an `rlib` and calls `GtkRenderer::run(...)`
   with a wake closure.
 - Java demo (`pathland-gtk-demo`) loads `pathland-render-gtk` as a `cdylib` via JNA and
   calls `pathland_gtk_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` over the Java DSL's own
   `libpathland_core` ring; native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes through the shared
   ring. The renderer **writes** the events and **wakes** the host (no payload); the host
   drains the event ring itself via `pathland_core_drain_events`. Events are never
   delivered through a side-channel callback — they flow through the opcode engine.
   The demo mounts `MusicPlayerView` (the same shared views the web demos use) with the
   app-driven media contract: the renderer plays the tracks through a direct GStreamer
   `playbin` and reports `MEDIA_*` events back; the demo's web-style
   `/_pathland/assets/...` paths resolve against an extracted local asset root
   (`pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`).
 
 The renderer maps native inputs onto the raw `Event` surface via GTK4
 controllers (`Button::clicked` → pointer up, `EventControllerMotion` →
 pointer move/enter/leave), emitting events through the same `Pump::send_input`
 path.
 
 `pathland_gtk::run` passes an explicit empty argv to GTK (the process command
 line belongs to the embedding host — e.g. the JVM's `-cp`/`-D` flags — and must
 not be parsed as GTK options).
 
 ### Native Java DSL (`dev.pathland.view`, in `lib/java/pathland-view`)
 
 The **hand-written, zero-dependency Java 17+ DSL** (no codegen). It is the
 SwiftUI-like authoring surface shared by desktop, Spring Boot, and Quarkus
 apps. Components and modifiers:
 
 - `View` is an **open interface** — the library ships `Text`/`Image`/`Color`/
   `Rectangle`, `VStack`/`HStack`/`ZStack`, `Spacer`, `Button`,
   `TextField(placeholder, WritableSignal<String>)`, `Video` (a
   `MediaController`'s surface), and application code (Quarkus/Spring/desktop)
   defines its own views by implementing `View`. **Media is a state object, not a
   view** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MediaController` owns the resource + transport as
   signals, a `Video` surface renders it, and **audio has no view** — the app
   binds its own buttons/sliders (`controller.attach()` materializes the
   controller's node once, outside any swapping branch, so a band swap never
   restarts playback).
 - **Custom views and styles use the configurator** (spec DSL.md §2): an
   app-authored `View` with values implements `Configurable<View.Config>`, holds a
   **`private` constructor**, and exposes
   `static ViewBuilder<View, Config> make(Consumer<Config>)`; a style
   (`ButtonStyle`/`LabelStyle`/`VideoStyle`) expose a
   **lowercase static factory** on their own type returning the style value
   (`BorderedButtonStyle.borderedButtonStyle(s -> s…)`), mirroring the library's
   `Modifiers.*` lowercase functions (e.g.
   `borderedButtonStyle(b -> b.padding(..).background(..)…)`). Creation goes
   through the configurator, never a parameterized constructor. The
   `pathland-view-processor` `ViewAuthoringProcessor` **errors** on
   public/protected constructors **with parameters** in custom `View` **and**
   `Style` implementations (no-arg roots and abstract types are exempt), so the
   convention is compile-enforced where the processor is wired
   (`annotationProcessorPaths`). The library's own views/styles follow the same
   shape (`Video`, `Text`, `BorderedButtonStyle`, …).
 - **SwiftUI-style `body()` / reactive components**: composite views declare
   `View body()` (their subtree); the library's primitives override
   `renderNode(Environment)` to materialize a `PathlandNode` (`render(Environment)` is
   the emitter entry point and must not be overridden). `body()` is a **tracked
   render function**: a signal read there subscribes that component, and a later
   write re-renders only that component and diffs its retained subtree — so plain
   `if`/`switch`/`for` over signals works. A signal **bound** to a node
   (`Text.make(t -> t.text(Signal))`) stays fine-grained and does not re-run the
   body. Non-signal reads are mount-time only; render bodies must be pure/idempotent
   and must not write signals. Each child view is a component slot; the root chain
   (body delegation, modifiers, environment/tap/navigation wrappers) is one slot.
   `View.of(Supplier<View>)` is the inline form (Java has no `if` expression);
   `ForEach.of(list | Signal<List<T>>, (item, index) -> View)` is the reactive
   list component (static lists may use streams/`for` directly).
   `NavigationContainer` / `SizeThatFits` are ordinary components. The root
   component type must stay stable across re-renders. (Rust parity is Phase 2.)
 - **Cross-language vocabulary** (spec DSL.md §9.3.1): the same anchors across
   Swift, Java, Kotlin, Rust, and TypeScript — `View`, `body`/`build`, `Signal`,
   `computed`, `State`, `ForEach`, `View.of`, `children`, `modifiers`. Use native
   control flow (`if`/`switch` in Swift/Java, `if`/`when` in Kotlin, `if`/`match`
   in Rust, ternary/`switch` in TypeScript); Java uses `View.of` only where an
   inline expression is needed. Swift is the canonical SwiftUI-shaped reference;
   Kotlin is implemented by `lib/java/pathland-view-kotlin` (a facade over the Java
   library), Swift is not implemented yet, and Rust parity is Phase 2.
 - **The three operations (spec DSL.md §2)**: every concrete view exposes
   `make(...)` (values — the only static; `make(Consumer<Config>)`, `make(value)`,
   `make()`), and the instance operations `.modifiers(ViewModifier...)` and
   `.children(View...)` chain on the returned builder. Java's static-vs-instance
   rule means the statics sit on the view class, the chain on the builder; a bare
   `View` value applies modifiers through the interface default
   `View.modifiers(...)`. Values are a
   fluent per-view `Config` (`VStack.make(v -> v.alignment(...).spacing(8))`,
   `Text.make(t -> t.text("hi"))`); modifiers are `ViewModifier` values built by
   the **`Modifiers` facade's lowercase functions** — one
   `import static dev.pathland.view.Modifiers.*;` brings the whole modifier
   vocabulary (`padding(p -> p.uniform(16))`, `frame(f -> f.width(100))`,
   `borderedButtonStyle(b -> …)`) — or, for single values, the value itself
   (`FontWeight.BOLD`, `Font.headline()`, a `ButtonStyle`). The `View` interface has
   **no per-modifier sugar** (`font`/`navigate`/`environment`/`onPathChange` were
   removed — use `.modifiers(Font…)`, `.modifiers(NavigationIntent.navigate(…))`,
   `.modifiers(environmentBinding(e -> e.key(…).value(…)))`,
   `.modifiers(pathChange(p -> p.listener(…)))`), and the `*Mod` shims
   (`EnvironmentMod`→`EnvironmentBinding`, `router/NavigationMod`→`NavigationIntent`,
   `PathChangeMod`→`PathChange`, `FontWeightMod`→`FontWeight`, …) are **removed**.
 - **Single-value shortcuts (spec DSL.md §2)**: a view/modifier whose config has a
   designated primary member also exposes a single-value construction overload that
   is pure sugar for the lambda — views construct with `make(value)` / `make(Signal<T>)`
   (`Text.make("hi")`), modifiers with the lowercase function's value form
   (`padding(16)`, `fontSize(sizeSignal)`). Multi-member configs (`Padding.edges`, `Offset`,
   `Gauge`, `Border`, …) have **no** shortcut — use the lambda. The shortcut delegates
   to the same `make(Consumer<Config>)` (views) / `Modifiers` facade
   (modifiers) factory via the package-private
   `Configurators` helper (one construction path). The former `.of(...)` construction
   factories are **removed** — a shortcut (or the lambda / `.children(...)` / empty
   `make()` for config-less views) replaces every one. Only data/branch factories keep
   `of`: `Color.of/rgb/argb/token`, `Fit.of`, `View.of`, `ForEach.of`,
   `EnvironmentKey.of`, `Route.of`, `Params.of`, `Signals.*`.
   Sizing is the `Frame` modifier value
   (`frame(f -> f.width(w).height(h).alignment(..))` and the lambda
   configurator `frame(f -> f.minWidth(..).maxWidth(..).alignment(..))`
   (min/ideal/max bounds)); all
   compile to the same `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT`/min-max `SET_PROPERTY`s.
   Typed enums
   (`Alignment`/`TextAlignment`/`FontWeight`/`Truncation`), not raw ints.
 - **Environment scoping via a `ThreadLocal`** (Java 17+): a `ButtonStyle` modifier
   injects a style down the whole child tree; `ButtonStyle.makeBody(Configuration)`
   with built-in `PlainButtonStyle` / `BorderedButtonStyle`. Custom wrappers via
   `ViewModifier.body(View)`. The `Environment` also carries the session's
   `PersistentState`.
 - **Reactivity (Angular parity)** in `dev.pathland.view.core.signal`:
   `Signals.signal/computed/effect/untracked` — lazy+memoized computeds,
   glitch-free synchronous flush, equality suppression, error caching, write
   discipline (`allowWrites()`), circular-dependency detection.
 - **Persisted view state** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): a `State<T>` field (e.g.
   `State<Integer> count = new State<>(0);`) is auto-wired to the session's
   `PersistentState` (keyed by field name, or `new State<>(0, "key")` for an explicit
   key) by the `pathland-view-processor` annotation processor, which detects `State`
   fields by type and generates a `<View>_StateBinder` per view class. Each view
   connects its own `State` when it renders (`View.render` calls `Environment.state()
   → PersistentState.connect(view)`), so nested views can be instantiated inline in
   `body()` and need not be declared as fields. `PersistentState.signal(name, initial)`
   auto-loads the persisted value and auto-saves on change (key `name:scope`), and
   `StateStore` is untyped (one store serves all signal types).
 - **Fine-grained emitter** (`dev.pathland.view.engine`): mounts a view tree once,
   assigns stable ids, and registers a **node-level binding effect** per reactive
   text/property — a signal change re-emits only that node's `SET_TEXT` /
   `SET_PROPERTY` (unchanged signals emit zero opcodes). Sinks: `FrameOpcodeSink`
   (self-contained frames for SSR/WebSocket) and `RingOpcodeSink` (JNA into
   `libpathland_core`). The wire codec (`dev.pathland.view.core.transport`) mirrors
   `pathland_core_transport` (`PLPL` batch format, self-contained frames + events).
 
 Consistency with `pathland_core::constants` is enforced by the emitter/HTML
 tests (golden byte layout + round-trips), replacing the old codegen assert pass.
 
 - **Single signal value convention**: a view or modifier holds **one `Signal<T>`
   field** for a reactive value — never a raw field *plus* a signal field for the
   same value. Static values are authored through the raw config setter (or the
   `.of(T)` convenience), which
   wraps them in `Signals.constant(...)` (e.g. `Text.make(t -> t.text("Hello"))` ≡
   `Text.make(t -> t.text(Signals.constant("Hello")))`); the emitter treats a
   `ConstantSignal` as
   a plain, non-reactive property (no binding/effect), so statics carry zero
   binding overhead. Controls' config fields for *distinct* properties
   (`min`/`max`/`step`/`placeholder`/`mode`/`style`) stay raw.

 ## Project Vision
 
 **Pathland is a cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol** that enables retained-mode UI development with multiple renderer backends. It is **protocol-first**, meaning the protocol specification is the source of truth, not any particular implementation.
 
 **Primary Goal**: Write once, run anywhere - Enable UI code to be written once and deployed across web, mobile, desktop, and embedded platforms through different renderer implementations.
 
 **Status**: The Rust opcode engine (16-byte opcode, ring buffer, arena, diff-based reactive emission) is implemented and tested (`cargo test`). See the Architecture section above.
 
 ---
 
 ## CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLES
 
 ### Principle 1: Renderer Statelessness (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The renderer MUST NOT retain application state.**
 
 - Renderers are **pure functions** of the opcode stream: same opcodes → same output
 - A renderer MAY retain its **rendered-output tree** (id → native element + computed layout) for drawing, hit-testing, and event routing — this is a cache of its own output, not state
 - The renderer MUST NOT retain component property values as business state, application control flow, or anything the application can change without emitting an opcode
 - The application owns the canonical retained UI tree
 - The engine emits **deltas only**; the renderer applies them to its native elements
 
 **Violation of this principle is a bug, not a feature.**
 
 ### Principle 2: Command-Based Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol transmits tree mutations as a stream of commands, NOT as serialized trees.**
 
 - Each frame is a **batch of delta commands** describing changes
 - Only **actual changes** are transmitted (diff-based reactive emission)
 - Protocol acts like a **VM instruction stream** / ABI
 - Deterministic, linear decoding without schema lookup or reflection
 
 ### Principle 3: Binary Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol MUST be binary.**
 
 - Open-source, cross-platform binary format
 - Fixed **16-byte instructions** in a ring buffer shared with the host via linear memory
 - Custom instruction-based bytecode, not schema-driven serialization
 - **Both directions are binary**: tree mutations (app → renderer) AND raw-input events (renderer → app) share the same instruction format, so the wire is language- and platform-agnostic
 
 ---
 
 ## Protocol Quick Reference
 
 The semantic surface is catalogued in the companion specs: **`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`**
 (primitive views + component IDs), **`spec/MODIFIERS.md`** (core modifiers = the
 `PARAMETER` properties), **`spec/EVENTS.md`** (core events + listener bits),
 **`spec/LAYOUT.md`** (frame & layout allocation contract). The
 tables below are a quick recap of the protocol surface; the companion files
 carry the authoritative ID allocations.
 
 > **Implementation status lives in each project's `status.md`**, not in the
 > specs: `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/status.md`,
 > `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-gtk/status.md`,
 > `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/status.md`,
 > `lib/java/pathland-view-core/status.md`, `lib/java/pathland-view/status.md`, `lib/java/pathland-view-kotlin/status.md`,
 > `lib/java/pathland-render-html/status.md`,
 > and the other Rust crates' `status.md` files.
 
 ### Opcode Format
 
 Every opcode is exactly 16 bytes:
 
 ```
 [Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
 ```
 
 See `spec/OPCODE.md` for the full format, ring buffer, arena, and frame lifecycle.
 
 ### Machine-readable protocol manifest
 
 `spec/protocol.tsv` is the target-neutral ID manifest emitted from
 `pathland_core::constants` by `pathland-protocol-manifest` (`cargo run -p
 pathland-protocol-manifest`). It contains only `kind`, `group`, `name`, and
 `value`; each language binding keeps its own representation and validates or
 reads the manifest. There is no Rust→Java source generation.
 
 The JVM mirror is hand-written and checked by
 `pathland-view-core/src/test/java/.../ProtocolManifestTest`: every manifest row
 must match a Java constant, no extra public numeric constants may exist, and
 `ValueTypes.forProperty` must match `property_value_type`. CI regenerates the
 manifest from Rust and fails on drift.
 
+Engine behavior beyond individual opcodes is specified in `spec/ENGINE.md` and
+enforced by shared self-contained frame traces under `spec/engine-traces/`.
+`pathland-engine-golden` emits them from the Rust engine and the JVM
+`EngineTraceTest` compares its encoded frames byte-for-byte.
+
 ### Categories
 
 | Category | Value | Direction | Description |
 |----------|-------|-----------|-------------|
 | TREE | 0x01 | Guest → Host | Node create/delete/insert/remove/move |
 | PARAMETER | 0x02 | Guest → Host | Constraint properties (spacing, padding, …), design tokens |
 | EVENT | 0x03 | Host → Guest | Raw inputs: pointer down/move/up, key down/up |
 | META | 0x04 | Both | Reset, environment, window metadata |

 ### Key Property IDs
 
 **Stack**: SPACING=0x0001, ALIGNMENT=0x0002, CONTENT_MARGINS=0x0005  
 **Text**: TEXT=0x000A, TEXT_ALIGNMENT=0x000C, LINE_LIMIT=0x000B, TRUNCATION_MODE=0x000D  
 **Style**: COLOR=0x100A, FONT_SIZE=0x1007, FONT_WEIGHT=0x1008, FONT_FAMILY=0x1009, BACKGROUND_COLOR=0x1001, BORDER_WIDTH=0x1003, BORDER_COLOR=0x1004, BORDER_RADIUS=0x1005, OPACITY=0x100D, VISIBLE=0x100E, Z_INDEX=0x100F, CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS=0x1010, PADDING=0x1011, PADDING_TOP/RIGHT/BOTTOM/LEFT=0x1012-0x1015  
 **Special**: WIDTH=0x100B (use -1=FILL, -2=HUG_CONTENT), HEIGHT=0x100C  
 **Semantic**: ROLE=0x2001, STATE=0x2002, ENABLED=0x2003, SELECTED=0x2004, EVENT_LISTENERS=0x2005 (u32 bitmask — which raw events a node wants reported), VALUE=0x2006, MIN_VALUE=0x2007, MAX_VALUE=0x2008, LABEL=0x200A, PROMPT=0x200B  
 **Binding/action**: ACTION_ID=0x2016, BINDING_ID=0x2017, TOGGLE_STYLE=0x2018 (Switch=0, Checkbox=1, Button=2)  
 **Media** (spec/MEDIA.md): MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID=0x103A (a `VIDEO`'s controller), MEDIA_SOURCE=0x103B, MEDIA_MUTED=0x103C, MEDIA_LOOP=0x103D, MEDIA_RATE=0x103E; PLAYBACK_STATE=0x1035 / MEDIA_POSITION=0x1036 / MEDIA_VOLUME=0x1037 live on the controller
 
 ### Colors
 
 - Literal colors are **sRGB** with D65 white point, packed as `0xAARRGGBB`
 - A color property may instead carry a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference to a token path
 - Semantic token resolution and theme adaptation are **renderer-owned**
 
 ### Design Token System
 
 **Core Principle**: Application defines intent, overrides, and the theme.
 Renderer defines visual appearance, behavior, defaults, and interaction states.
 
 - The **application owns the theme**: token overrides (base = **light**, `dark.`-prefixed = **dark**) and token references in style properties. Token refs cover COLOR and non-color values (`Length` for spacing/padding/font size/radius/border/frame; `FontFamily.Token` for STRING) in the Rust and Java DSLs.
 - The **renderer owns** default token values (light + dark, the full Tier-1 catalog), token resolution (including explicit `dark.` = forced dark and parent fallback), effective color-scheme detection, interaction states (hover, pressed, focus, disabled), and theme adaptation
 - `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` identifies tokens by **dot-separated string paths** (e.g. `color.primary`, `space.2`) with the standard value-type encoding — there is no separate numeric tokenId system. A `dark.` prefix selects the dark variant (`dark.color.primary`); a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference whose path starts with `dark.` forces the dark value in either scheme
 - **Runtime theming**: `META::RESET_THEME` clears every app override; a replacement theme is reset + `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides in one frame. `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` forces `platform`/`light`/`dark`. Both are renderer state — no node is re-emitted. Java: `Emitter.replaceTheme`/`setColorScheme` + `PathlandSession.setTheme`/`setColorScheme`; Rust: `Engine::reset_theme`/`set_color_scheme`.
 - An unresolvable token reference leaves the property **unset** (renderer default), never an error or stale value.
 - The protocol MUST NEVER describe hover styles, click styles, visual transitions, conditional styling, or layout tuning for interaction states
 - **Deferred**: applying per-component tokens to native GTK/Qt leaf control chrome; web parent-path fallback.
 
 The HTML renderer's default token values are generated from `design/` (see
 "HTML base design" above). Full details: [Design Token System](./spec/OPCODE.md#design-token-system)
 and the canonical catalog / color-scheme contract in [spec/TOKENS.md](./spec/TOKENS.md).
 
 ---
 
 ## Implementation Guidelines
 
 ### Adding New Component
 1. Add to `component_type` in `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs`
 2. Document in `spec/OPCODE.md`
 3. Implement the component type in `pathland-core` (if it affects the retained tree)
 4. Implement native-element mapping in the target renderer (Goal 3–5)
 5. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Adding New Property
 1. Add to the appropriate property module in `constants.rs`
 2. Document in `spec/OPCODE.md`
 3. Handle the value type in `pathland-core`'s diff emission (if a stack/text/size property)
 4. Implement in each renderer's property application
 5. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Modifying Protocol
 1. Update `spec/OPCODE.md` first (and `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` vectors)
 2. Update `constants.rs` and `pathland-core` encoding/emitters
 3. Run `cd lib/rust && cargo run -p pathland-protocol-manifest` and commit the
    updated `spec/protocol.tsv`
 4. Update the hand-written JVM protocol constants (the Java manifest test fails
    with the exact missing/stale row otherwise)
-5. Verify backward compatibility; update `pathland-core`/renderers + tests
-6. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
+5. If emission behavior changed, run
+   `cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --emit` and commit the trace fixtures
+6. Verify backward compatibility; update `pathland-core`/renderers + tests
+7. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Changing the Wire Format
 - Bump the wire `version` field in `spec/OPCODE.md` and `pathland-core`'s header (currently 1). Pre-release format changes are acceptable while version stays 1.
 
 ### Keeping implementation status updated (MANDATORY)
 
 **The agent MUST keep the per-project `status.md` files in sync with the code.**
 Whenever you land a protocol or renderer change — a new component/property/
 command/event, a new encoder/decoder, a new widget mapping, a new modifier or
 renderer feature, a test that proves new surface — **update the affected
 project's `status.md`** (Implemented / Not implemented / gaps) in the same
 change. The specs (`spec/`) describe the protocol contract only and MUST NOT
 carry implementation status; status lives in `status.md` next to each
 implementing project.
 
 ---
 
 ## Common Pitfalls
 
 ### NEVER Do These
 | Anti-Pattern | Why Wrong | Correct |
 |--------------|-----------|---------|
 | Renderer stores application state | Violates statelessness | Application owns the tree |
 | Engine computes layout / emits rects | Violates declarative model | Emit structure + constraints; native elements lay out |
 | Send full trees | Inefficient | Diff-based reactive emission |
 | String property names | Larger payloads | Use numeric IDs |
 | String component names | Larger payloads | Use numeric IDs |
 | Generic RGB | Ambiguous | Explicitly sRGB |
 | Hover styles in protocol | Renderer job | Define in theme |
 | Heap allocation in steady-state emission | Slow | Preallocated snapshot slab + arena |
 
 ---

-1. Read this file and `spec/OPCODE.md`

 ---
 
 ## Pathland Mindset
 
 **Always remember**:
 1. Protocol is King
 2. Renderers are Dumb (execute commands only)
 3. Applications are Smart (generate commands)
 4. Only Changes Matter (transmit mutations / reactive emission)
 5. Binary is Beautiful (efficient, deterministic)
 
 **When in doubt**: Check `spec/OPCODE.md`, the conformance vectors in `spec/CONFORMANCE.md`, and the companion catalogs (`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`, `spec/MODIFIERS.md`, `spec/EVENTS.md`, `spec/LAYOUT.md`), and the reference implementation (`pathland-core`). Ask: "Does this maintain stateless renderers?" "Does this only transmit actual changes?" "Does this describe WHAT the UI is, never WHERE?" "Is this representable as a 16-byte opcode in any language?"

 # Contributing to Pathland
 
 Thanks for your interest in Pathland — an open, cross-platform, cross-language
 UI protocol. This guide covers how to build, test, and contribute.
 
 ## Code of conduct
 
 This project is governed by the [Contributor Covenant](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). By
 participating you agree to abide by its terms.
 
 ## Security
 
 Found a vulnerability? **Do not open a public issue** — report it privately per
 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).
 
 ## Project map
 
 - `lib/rust/` — the Rust workspace: `pathland-core` (protocol), `pathland-engine`
   (emitter/signals), `pathland-view` (DSL), `pathland-core-transport`,
   `pathland-core-capi` (C ABI), `pathland-render-gtk`, `pathland-render-html`,
   `pathland-view-native`, `pathland-render-gtk-demo`.
 - `lib/java/` — the Maven reactor: `pathland-view-core`
   (`dev.pathland.view.core*` + `dev.pathland.view.engine`), `pathland-view`
   (the Java DSL, `dev.pathland.view`), `pathland-view-processor`,
   `pathland-view-kotlin` (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`), `pathland-render-html`,
   `pathland-state-redis`, `pathland-demo-views`, the Quarkus/Spring demos, and
   the TypeScript DOM renderer (`lib/typescript`).
 - `spec/` — the protocol contract: `OPCODE.md` (primary), `PRIMITIVES.md`,
-  `MODIFIERS.md`, `EVENTS.md`, `CONFORMANCE.md` (golden vectors), `DSL.md`
-  (authoring surface), and `protocol.tsv` (the target-neutral ID manifest).
+  `MODIFIERS.md`, `EVENTS.md`, `CONFORMANCE.md` (golden vectors), `ENGINE.md`
+  (retained-tree behavior), `DSL.md` (authoring surface), `protocol.tsv` (the
+  target-neutral ID manifest), and `engine-traces/` (shared frame fixtures).
 
 Implementation status per project lives in each crate/module's `status.md`.
 
 ## Prerequisites
 
 - **Rust**: stable toolchain (`rustup`); `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target for the
   `no_std` direction guard.
 - **Java**: JDK 17+ (Maven `release=17`; the whole stack runs on every LTS from 17).
 - **GTK4** (Linux) for `pathland-render-gtk`.
 
 ## Build & test
 
 ```bash
 # Rust workspace
 cd lib/rust && cargo test
 
 # no_std / wasm32 direction guard (requires: rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown)
 cd lib/rust && ./check-wasm.sh
 
 # Regenerate the target-neutral protocol manifest after changing Rust constants
 cd lib/rust && cargo run -p pathland-protocol-manifest
 
+# Regenerate the shared engine trace fixtures after an emission change
+cd lib/rust && cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --emit
+
 # C ABI (cdylib) used by Java JNA / native hosts
 cd lib/rust && cargo build -p pathland-core-capi
 
 # Java reactor (the core libraries; the Quarkus/Spring demos are excluded from
 # CI but buildable with: cd lib/java && mvn -q install)
 cd lib/java && mvn -q -B test -pl '!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo'
 ```
 
 CI runs exactly these commands (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`).
 
 ## Making changes
 
 1. Open an issue first (or pick an open one) so the work is visible. Issues are
    labelled by epic: `hardening`, `benchmarking`, `tooling`, `a11y-seo`,
    `packaging`, and grouped into milestones `1 · Hardening & Memory Safety`
    through `5 · Packaging & Grant Readiness`.
 2. Create a focused branch (`fix/…`, `feat/…`, `docs/…`).
 3. Keep changes small and reviewable; add/update tests with every change.
 4. Update the relevant `status.md` file when you land protocol or renderer work
    (the specs describe the contract; implementation status lives in `status.md`).
 5. Keep commits atomic with clear messages (see below). No DCO sign-off is
    required.
 
 ## Commit style
 
 - Short, imperative subject line (`feat(view): …`, `fix(transport): …`,
   `docs(spec): …`, `refactor(…): …`).
 - Follow the repo's existing history as the style guide.
 - Reference the issue where useful (`Fixes #NN`).
 
 ## Protocol changes (important)
 
 - Update `spec/OPCODE.md` **first**, plus the affected companion catalog and the
   golden vectors in `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` **before** implementations depend on
   the change.
 - Keep the 16-byte opcode format stable; wire-format changes must bump the
   `version` field (currently 1) per `spec/OPCODE.md`.
 - New components/properties: allocate IDs in the specs + `constants.rs`
   (`lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs`), then mirror across
   `lib/java/…/Components.java`/`Properties.java` and `lib/typescript/src/constants.ts`,
   and update each renderer + its `status.md`.
 
 ## Non-negotiable principles
 
 - Renderers are **stateless pure functions** of the opcode stream.
 - The engine emits **structure + constraints**, never positions/rects.
 - Emission is **diff-based**: only changed nodes emit; unchanged trees emit zero
   opcodes.
 - Binary both ways: tree mutations (app → renderer) and raw-input events
   (renderer → app) share the 16-byte opcode format.
 
 ## Communication
 
 - Issues/PRs are the primary channel.
 - Contact the maintainers at `michael@apaq.dk` for private matters.

   tracked render. Each child view is a `ViewSlot` with its own synchronous
   `Signals.tracked` computation; a signal read there re-renders only that component
   and the emitter diffs its retained subtree. Plain `if`/`switch`/`for` over signals
   now works in `body()` (bare control flow), with `View.of(Supplier<View>)` as the
   inline supplier form. The root chain (`body()` delegation, modifiers,
   environment/tap/navigation wrappers) stays in one slot; child views are child
   slots. A bound signal (`Text.make(t -> t.text(signal))`) remains fine-grained and
   does not re-run the body (initial binding reads are untracked). Non-signal reads
   are mount-time only. The root component type must stay stable. `render(Environment)`
   is the emitter entry point; primitives override `renderNode(Environment)`.
   `Conditional`/`Case` are removed (replaced by bare control flow + `View.of`).
 - **`ForEach`** (`ForEach.of(list | Signal<List<T>>, (item, index) -> View)`):
   a Group-backed reactive list component. A static list maps once per render; a
   `Signal<List<T>>` re-renders only the list slot. Each item is a child component
   slot; null children are skipped; reconciliation is position + type (no keys).
   `ForEachTest`.
 - **Cross-language vocabulary** (spec DSL.md §9.3.1): the shared anchors
   (`View`, `body`/`build`, `Signal`, `computed`, `State`, `ForEach`, `View.of`,
   `children`, `modifiers`) and the native spellings for Swift/Java/Kotlin/Rust/
   TypeScript. Swift is the canonical SwiftUI-shaped reference; Rust parity is
   Phase 2.
 - **`ProxyView`** (`ProxyView.make(p -> p.endpoint(...).route(...).credential(...))`):
   a `PROXY_VIEW` (0x1E) container whose child subtree is served by **another**
   Pathland server (spec/PROXY.md). It authors **no** children — the origin root is
   spliced in at runtime — and takes size modifiers like any view. The immutable
   `ProxyConfig` snapshot rides the node (`PathlandNode.proxyConfig`) and is
   surfaced to the host through `RenderResult.proxyViews()` (node id → config) so
   `pathland-server-core` opens an origin connection per proxy node. The emitter's
   internal `onStructureReconciled(Runnable)` hook (like `snapshotEmission`) fires
   after each structural reconcile — after the routing maps reflect the new subtree
   — so the host reconciles origin connections against the live `proxyViews` map
   (a proxy lives exactly while its node is in the retained tree, spec/PROXY.md §7).
 - **`SizeThatFits` fit slot** (`SizeThatFits.make(Fit...)` + `Fit.of(view, minWidth)`):
   a structural slot (`SIZE_THAT_FITS` 0x17) emitting `FIT_QUERY` (LIST, ascending
   thresholds) + the single selected child — unselected candidates never transmit.
   The host routes `FIT_CHANGED` into the slot's fit sink
   (`RenderResult.fitInputs`, via `InputDispatcher`), which re-renders only the fit
   component (an unchanged index re-emits zero opcodes). The LIST
   value type is written by `FrameOpcodeSink`/`RingOpcodeSink`
   (`[count][f32 × count]` arena entries). A slot's selection is **retained node
   state** (`PathlandNode.fitSelection`): a parent re-render creates a fresh fit
   component with a default index, so the emitter seeds it from the node it replaces
   (`ViewSlot.oldNodeHint` / `Emitter.currentSlotOldFitSelection`) — a nested fit
   (the player bar's controls slot under the root row) keeps its candidate instead
   of resetting to compact (a reset would strand the DOM client, which never
   re-reports an unchanged width). The **web-SSR full-snapshot emission** (issue #141) is an
   internal emitter mode (`Emitter.snapshotEmission(true)`, armed by
   `PathlandSession`): on mount/resync the slot emits EVERY candidate in `FIT_QUERY`
   order so the SSR renders all branches gated by CSS container queries (a no-JS
   correct first paint) — the authored DSL is unchanged. `PathlandNode.fitReported`
   and the emitter's `snapshotActive` flag keep the multi-candidate presentation
   until the first `FIT_CHANGED`; that report re-renders the fit component with one
   selected child, and the web client unwraps the gated branches. The downgrade is a
   **clean N→1** (`Emitter.reconcileSnapshotFit`): it keeps the SELECTED candidate's
   node as-is (retaining its id + subtree, zero churn) and removes the others — it
   never positionally diffs, because both candidates are frequently the same
   component and morphing the loser's node into the winner would relocate the winner
   into the SSR's loser wrapper and break the renderer's candidate-position CSS gate.
   **View reuse** (issue #159): the same `View` instance may not be the candidate
   of two `Fit`s — `SizeThatFits.make` rejects it (`IllegalStateException`), since
   it would be materialized once per candidate and leak shared state / ids.
   Sharing a subtree **inside** two distinct candidate roots stays allowed; every
   materialized copy gets a distinct node id. The emitter enforces the frame's
   **unique-node-id invariant** (spec/OPCODE.md §Frame Lifecycle) with
   `Emitter.duplicateIds` / a fail-loud guard at mount, resync, and after each
   structural reconcile, so an id-overriding pass (an identity-stable node pinning
   a playback key) can never silently corrupt an id-keyed consumer.

   the three operations — values via the static `View.make(...)`
   (`make(Consumer<Config>)`, `make(value)` shortcuts, empty `make()`),
   `.modifiers(ViewModifier...)` (an **instance** operation — the `View` interface
   ships a `default View.modifiers(ViewModifier...)` so a bare `View` value
   (a style's `config.label()`, a `Color`, a `FitSlot`) applies modifiers too, and
   `ViewBuilder` overrides it covariantly), and (content-bearing views) `.children(View...)`
   (static first-call retained as a value-less convenience). Values are configured
   via `make(c -> …)`, the chain lives on the returned generic
   `ViewBuilder<V, C>` (`View.Config`, `Configurable<C>`, `ChildrenView`; `View`
   keeps only `body()`/`render()`/`modifiers(...)` — Java's static-vs-instance rule
   means `make(...)` is the only static of the three; the former static
   `X.modifiers(...)` first-call entry points are **removed**). Modifiers/styles are
   built through the **`Modifiers` facade's lowercase functions** — one
   `import static dev.pathland.view.Modifiers.*;` brings the whole vocabulary
   (`padding(p -> p.uniform(16))`, `frame(f -> f.width(100).height(24))`,
   `foregroundStyle(f -> f.color(c))`, `borderedButtonStyle(b -> …)`); the

   construction seam remains for the facade). **Single-value modifiers are the value

   scopes the matching environment key — an app-authored style exposes a lowercase
   static factory on its own type (`BorderedButtonStyle.borderedButtonStyle(s -> s…)`).

   (`font`/`navigate`/`environment`/`onPathChange`), the former
   `View.with(ViewModifier...)` general modifier chain, and the `*Mod` shims
   (`EnvironmentMod`→`EnvironmentBinding`, `NavigationMod`→`NavigationIntent`,

   construction overload** replaces them where the config has
   a designated primary member (views `make(value)` — `Text.make("hi")`;
   modifiers the lowercase value form — `padding(16)`,
   `fontSize(sizeSignal)` — pure sugar for the lambda, via the package-private

   setter (sugar for `Signals.constant`) and a `Signal<T>` setter — layout included
   (`spacing`, `alignment`, `padding`, `frame`, `columns`/`tracks`, …). A
   non-constant signal becomes a **node-level binding** (re-emits only that
   property); a constant carries zero binding overhead. Two-way control *values*
   take `WritableSignal<T>`; every other member takes a one-way `Signal<T>`
   (`WritableSignal extends Signal`). Views and modifiers place values through the
   single `PathlandNode.property(id, Signal<?>)` path; `emit.ReactiveValues`
   coerces a signal's value to the property's declared wire type
   (`ValueTypes.forProperty`) and maps `WireValue` enums to their numeric code.
   `State`/`Signals` are unchanged.

   built with <View>.make(c -> …) / .children(...) / .modifiers(...)

   `HorizontalAlignment` (leading/center/trailing) for `VStack`s,
   `VerticalAlignment` (top/center/bottom) for `HStack`s, and a 2D `Alignment`

   PRIMITIVES.md §ZStack). Stretching is a child's `FILL` size kind, never an

   `ViewModifier` values built via `padding(c -> …)` (`Modifiers.*` lowercase function)
   (`padding(p -> p.uniform(16))`, `foregroundStyle(f -> f.color(c))`,
   `border(b -> b.color(c).width(w))`, …) or passed as the bare value when the
   value *is* the modifier (`FontWeight.BOLD`, `Font.headline()`, `MyButtonStyle`),
   applied via `.modifiers(...)` (one or several,

   configurator `frame(f -> f.width(w).height(h).alignment(..))` /
   `frame(f -> f.minWidth(..).maxWidth(..).alignment(..))` (the fluent

   freely combinable). The width/height setters leave `ALIGNMENT` unset
   (alignment optional, so a stack's own cross-axis alignment is preserved);
   `±∞` width/height is normalized to `Commands.Size.FILL` and `NaN` omits the
   axis; an infinite min/ideal/max bound is omitted (no limit).
   The `View` interface has **no per-modifier factory methods** (application
   authors' views share the modifier-value surface — spec `DSL.md` §5.6), and
   the `*Mod` shims are removed. A style is itself a modifier: `buttonStyle` is a
   `ButtonStyle` value (an **environment** binding — it scopes
   `Environment.BUTTON_STYLE`, an `EnvironmentKey<ButtonStyle>`, down the subtree).

   `EnvironmentKey<LabelStyle>`; `LabelStyle` is an **interface** with
   `DefaultLabelStyle`/`TitleOnlyLabelStyle`/`IconOnlyLabelStyle`; the style shapes
   the emitted child tree, never a wire property).

   component + interaction and attaches the content as its child (Composite Override
   Mode). `Button` renders a `BUTTON` node and wires the action/`EVENT_LISTENERS` on

   a style decorates content and never installs the tap. `PlainButtonStyle` returns

   `Frame`; the wire batch type is `emit.ProtocolFrame` (renamed from `emit.Frame`,

   object owning the resource and transport as signals. It exposes the *command*
   signals (`source`/`playing`/`position`/`volume`/`muted`/`loop`/`rate`, each
   rebindable to an app-owned `WritableSignal` so the controller drives the state
   the rest of the UI reads), the *report* feeds

   convenience transport

   `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` (the natural-end stop, or a media error) feeds
   `playingReport`, so the app's `PLAYBACK_STATE` intent survives and the track
   advanced on `MEDIA_ENDED` keeps playing.
   The emitter materializes **one `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node per controller** (in
   place at its `attach()` marker, with a **pinned** id). The pinned id is
   reserved in the id allocator (no other node can take it) and honored on **every**
   emission path — including a subtree re-emission that reassigns ids (`freshIdFor`)
   — so the playback key survives a content swap / band swap and the renderer never
   tears down playback. A controller must therefore be created **once** by the app
   (a view field, not inline in a route/destination factory: `body()` re-runs on a
   path change and would make a new controller); `Video` is the only media view (a `VIDEO`

   its own buttons/sliders. `VideoStyle` supplies a custom control surface; the
   default (`EmptyContent`) keeps the node a leaf with renderer-native controls.

   report never echoes back as a seek/volume command (spec/EVENTS.md Media echo
   guard). `Commands.Event`/`transport.Event`/`FrameCodec` decode the events.

   **thread-safe** (all entry points synchronized) so a request/SSR-thread flush can
   never race the actor's mid-flush mutation of another session's pending effects.

   pre-run producer edges are restored, so it retries on the next dependency change
   (a transient error can't silently kill a node's binding).

   carries `BINDING_ID` on **every** emission path — mount, a matched reconcile,
   and a newly created subtree — so a control materialized by a structural slot
   (e.g. the player bar's wide volume slider, created when its nested
   `SIZE_THAT_FITS` swaps) still reports `VALUE_CHANGED`; the frame/SSR sink

   sugar for a constant); the emitter treats a constant as a plain, non-reactive
   property (no binding/effect).
 - **Structural reactivity** (spec DSL.md §3.4): per-component tracked bodies
   (above). `NavigationContainer`, `SizeThatFits`, and `View.of` are ordinary
   components whose render reads their selector signal; a change re-renders only
   that component — position+type-stable ids, `TREE`/`PARAMETER` deltas only,
   identical recompute emits **zero** opcodes, nested components reconcile
   independently. `RenderResult` routing maps are live unmodifiable views (a
   re-render updates tap/text/value/date/media/fit routing).
 - **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.core.router`, spec DSL.md §4.5): `Route` (absolute
   path, `pathOnly()` strips query/fragment), `RouteTable` (literal + `:param`
   patterns, guards → `replace()` redirect, `fallback` 404), `Router`
   (`Signal<Route>` + back-stack; `navigate`/`push`/`pop`/`replace`/`back`,
   `handlePlatformNavigation`/`handleEvent`), **`Navigation`** (the ergonomic
   facade: `Navigation.navigator(initialPath).route(...).fallback(...).build()`
   collapses table + router + seeding, `Navigation.container(router)` is the slot,
   `Navigation.isActive(router, path)` → a reactive `Signal<Boolean>` for
   active-route styling, `Navigation.ROUTER` = the `EnvironmentKey<Router>`),
   **`Params`** (typed path-param access — `get`/
   `intValue`/`longValue`/`doubleValue`/`booleanValue`/`path` — replacing the raw
   `Map` in `RouteHandler`), **a bound router** (`Navigation.navigator()...
   .build(WritableSignal<String>)` — the router binds to the host-provided
   `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` signal: external writes are re-routed **guard-aware**,
   its own navigation is mirrored back, the initial value is guard-processed), and
   **generic scoped environment values**
   (`EnvironmentKey`/`EnvironmentValues` + the `EnvironmentBinding` modifier value
   (`environmentBinding(e -> e.key(key).value(value))`) +
   `Environment.value(key)` — the `.environment` style, hierarchical nearest-
   wins; a `NavigationContainer` scopes `Navigation.ROUTER` to its destination
   subtree, and each component slot captures its environment scope at render and
   re-applies it on its own re-renders (`ViewSlot.envScope`); **reads always
   return a signal** — `Environment.value(key)` → `Signal<T>`, a value injected as
   a `Signal` comes back as the same instance (bindable for reactive updates) and a
   plain value is wrapped in a constant signal; a read made before the key is bound
   returns a **lazy signal** that captures the binding on the first `.get()` during
   render, enabling the `@Environment` **field style**
   (`private final Signal<Router> router = Environment.value(Navigation.ROUTER);`)),
   plus the
   **universal active platform path** (`Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` =
   `EnvironmentKey<String>`, the host injects a writable signal — provided for every
   app with or without navigation — read via `Environment.value` and observed via
   the `PathChange` modifier value (`pathChange(p -> p.listener(...))`) /
   reading the signal; fires on every change incl.
   the initial value),
   `NavigationContainer` (structural
   slot emitting the `ROUTE` property coalesced into the same frame as the
   destination swap, plus a `NAV_DEPTH` U32 back-stack-depth property
   (`router.depth()` = stack size + 1; `push`+1 / `pop`−1 / `replace` unchanged)
   so native navigation adapters reconcile their page stack by depth, a
   `NAV_CHROME` chrome-mode property (`Chrome.PLATFORM_DEFAULT` / `Chrome.CUSTOM`
   — the renderer supplies default navigation chrome, or the developer owns all
   nav UI), and a `TRANSITION` PlatformDefault hint renderers may use
   to animate the swap), `NavigationLink` (a `BUTTON` that pushes — both
   explicit-router and **router-agnostic** overloads). **Any component can change
   the route** (spec DSL.md §4.5): `Button.make(b -> …).modifiers(NavigationIntent.navigate/push/replace(path))`
   (`NavigationIntent`) and router-agnostic
   `NavigationLink.make(l -> l.label("..").to(path))` record a
   `NavOp` intent on the node; the emitter resolves it to the **nearest
   enclosing** `Router` (the `NavigationContainer` the component lives under)
   during the retained-tree walk and exposes it on
   `RenderResult.navigateActions` (a live `node id → Runnable` map like
   `tapActions`), which the host routes on tap before `tapActions`. The route is a
   **plain signal** (not persisted; the URL is the web's persistence layer) and
   the host **seeds it before mount** via `navigate(...)` — no `Location`, no
   environment-carried route. A `NAVIGATE` event (`Event.navigate(url)` /
   `Event.navigateBack()`, wire round-trip via `FrameCodec`) routes into the
   router through `RenderResult.navigateHandler`.
 - **Wire codec** (`transport`): `FrameCodec` — self-contained `PLPL` frames
   both directions, `encodeEvents`/`decodeEvents` (host→guest events with
   `TEXT_CHANGED` string-section offsets), and **`META::ENVIRONMENT`**
   (`isEnvironment`/`decodeEnvironment` → `EnvironmentData` — the platform
   environment: viewport + initial route; SSR synthesizes it from the request,
   the DOM client sends/enriches it over the WebSocket).
 - **JNA ring interop** (`ffm`): lazy `libpathland_core` binding, zero JNI;
   `PathlandCore.ringMut(handle)` borrows the underlying ring for the in-process
   GTK renderer (`pathland_gtk_run_ring`), and `RingOpcodeSink` is the zero-copy
   guest writer.
 - **Input dispatch** (`emit.InputDispatcher`): routes raw `EVENT`s into the
   `RenderResult` registries (tap / navigate / text / value / date, `NAVIGATE`
   URL → active path, back → router). Shared by the server session
   (`PathlandSession.dispatch`) and the native GTK host, so both route events
   identically and neither reaches into view internals.
 - **`BINDING_ID` on the ring path**: for a `RingOpcodeSink`, the emitter sets
   `BINDING_ID` (= the node's id) on every text/value/date-bound control so the
   GTK renderer's transport-aware event guard fires (`TEXT_CHANGED` /
   `VALUE_CHANGED`). The frame (SSR) path never emits it, keeping server output
   unchanged.
 - **State** (`state`): `StateStore`/`PersistentState`/`State`, auto-wired by
   `pathland-view-processor`.
 - **Design tokens**: `Color` is `(argb, token)` — `Color.token("color.primary")`
   (incl. `dark.*` paths) usable in every color-taking modifier
   (`ForegroundStyle`/`Background`/`Border`/`Tint`, and the `Color` view). The
   emitter sends token refs as the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (path in the frame's
   string section / arena) in both `FrameOpcodeSink` and `RingOpcodeSink`
   (spec/TOKENS.md).
 - **`Theme` / `AdaptiveTheme` (global overrides)**: `Theme` — single-value
   builders (`color`/`f32`/`u32`/`u8`/`string`) for one scheme; `AdaptiveTheme(light,
   dark)` composes a light + dark pair. Both implement the `ThemeData` interface
   (`emit`/`emitInto`); `Theme.emit`/`AdaptiveTheme.emit` write one frame of
   `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides (the dark theme's with the `dark.` prefix),
   and `OpcodeSink.setDesignToken` puts path + STRING values into the string
   section (frame) / arena (ring). The `Emitter` takes a `ThemeData` and rides it
   into the mount + resync frames. Overrides are renderer-global — they never
   re-emit nodes.
 - **Non-color token refs**: `Length` (`Length.of(float)` / `Length.token(path)`)
   is accepted by `Padding`, `FontSize`, stack/grid `spacing`, `Border` width,
   `CornerRadius`, and `Frame` width/height; `FontFamily.Token` covers the
   `FONT_FAMILY` STRING token. The emitter detects `TokenPath` and sends
   `DESIGN_TOKEN`; literal/signal values keep their existing forms.
 - **Runtime theming**: `Emitter.replaceTheme(ThemeData)` / `resetTheme()` and
   `setColorScheme(ThemeMode)`; `PathlandSession.setTheme` / `resetTheme` /
   `setColorScheme` delegate to the same emission path. Replacement emits
   `META::RESET_THEME` + overrides in one frame; `ThemeMode` is
   `PLATFORM`/`LIGHT`/`DARK`. `OpcodeSink.resetTheme`/`setColorScheme` are
   implemented by both the frame and ring sinks.
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID` are usable as modifiers (`actionId`/`bindingId`); the
   Java model routes events by node id through the emitter's registries
   (`RenderResult`), so the frame (SSR) path does not set them automatically.
   On the ring (desktop) path the emitter auto-sets `BINDING_ID` for bound
   controls (see Implemented) — the GTK renderer gates value/text events on it.
 - Structural reconcile does not emit `SET_PROPERTY` for a *removed* property on
   a matched node (the wire has no unset; the renderer keeps the last value) —
   consistent with the Rust engine.
 
 ## Verified by
 
-`mvn test` (JDK 17+) — emitter, codec round-trips (incl. `NAVIGATE`), signals,
+`mvn test` (JDK 17+) — emitter, shared engine traces (`EngineTraceTest` against
+`spec/engine-traces/`), codec round-trips (incl. `NAVIGATE`), signals,
 state, reactive bodies (`ReactiveBodyTest`), reactive slots (`ViewOfTest`),
 reactive lists (`ForEachTest`) and the router (`RouterTest`:
 initial route + `ROUTE` property + `NAV_DEPTH` depth tracking + `NAV_CHROME`
 chrome mode, destination swap deltas, back-stack, params, guard redirect,
 fallback, `NAVIGATE` routing, `NavigationLink`, the **declarative nav
 intents** (`.navigate/.push/.replace` + router-agnostic `NavigationLink`
 resolving to the nearest enclosing router via `navigateActions`), the
 **`Navigation` facade / `Params` / `isActive`**, the **scoped environment
 values** (`View.environment` + `Environment.value` hierarchy/restore), and the
 **universal active path** (a bound router re-routing guard-aware on external
 signal writes + mirroring its own navigation; `onPathChange` firing on changes));
 the JNA ring
 test runs when `libpathland_core` is on `java.library.path`. The v2 authoring
 surface is covered by `ViewBuilderTest` (with/modifiers/children any-order) and
 `ModifierWithTest` (modifier `with(...)`, enum/`Font` value-is-modifier,
 `Frame.with` builder); signals-first configs by `ReactiveConfigTest` (a
 non-constant value member re-emits exactly one `SET_PROPERTY` — boolean, float,
 enum, string, container spacing — and a constant registers no binding). CI proves
 every LTS from 17 (Temurin 17/21/25).

@@ -1,137 +1,147 @@
 # Pathland Rust Workspace
 
 The Rust core of Pathland: the **opcode engine** that emits the declarative
 view structure as a fixed 16-byte opcode ring buffer into shared linear memory,
 consumed by host renderers. Runs natively on desktop (C ABI + GTK renderer).
 
 ```
 crates/
 │  # ── The three elements ────────────────────────────────────────────────
 ├── pathland-view/          # RETAINED UI — SwiftUI-style view DSL: VStack/HStack/Text/
 │                           #   Button + chainable modifiers (spacing/padding/fontSize/
 │                           #   color/background) building a retained tree (no_std)
 ├── pathland-core/          # OPCODE ENGINE — retained tree types (Node/Component) + the
 │                           #   diff-based reactive emitter + 16-byte opcode, ring buffer,

 ## Java libraries (framework-agnostic)
 
 The reusable Java libraries live in `../java/` (Maven reactor, `dev.pathland`):
 
 - `pathland-view` — SwiftUI-like view DSL + Angular-style signals/computed/effects,
   fine-grained opcode emitter, wire codec, JNA ring interop (`dev.pathland.view`)
 - `pathland-render-html` — pure-function HTML renderer (SSR) over the opcode stream
 - `pathland-state-redis` — Redis-backed `StateStore` (Lettuce)
 - `pathland-quarkus-demo` — Quarkus SSR + WebSocket demo consuming the libraries
 
 ## Specification
 
 - [`spec/OPCODE.md`](../../spec/OPCODE.md) — the 16-byte opcode protocol
 - [`spec/CONFORMANCE.md`](../../spec/CONFORMANCE.md) — golden byte vectors
 
 ## Protocol manifest
 
 `pathland-protocol-manifest` emits `spec/protocol.tsv`, the target-neutral
 machine-readable ID manifest consumed by non-Rust bindings. It emits data only;
 each language owns its own representation. Regenerate after changing
 `pathland-core` constants:
 
 ```bash
 cargo run -p pathland-protocol-manifest
 ```
 
+## Engine trace fixtures
+
+`pathland-engine-golden` emits shared self-contained PLPL frames under
+`spec/engine-traces/`; the JVM `EngineTraceTest` compares against them
+byte-for-byte. Regenerate after an emission change:

+cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --emit
+```
+
 ## Run tests
 
 ```bash
 PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo test
 ```
 
 ## Verify the no_std / wasm32 direction guard
 
 `pathland-core` and `pathland-view` must stay `no_std` + `alloc` and compile for
 `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, so the core can still target a browser/embedded/remote
 projection later. Verify with:
 
 ```bash
 ./check-wasm.sh
 ```
 
 ## Run the GTK desktop demo (native, zero-copy shared ring)
 
 ```bash
 PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo run -p pathland-render-gtk-demo
 ```
 
 Requires GTK4 (`brew install gtk4` on macOS).
 
 ## Run the Java libraries (build + test)
 
 The Java libraries build against `libpathland_core` when the native ring path is
 used (desktop/JNA). Build and test the whole reactor:
 
 ```bash
 PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo build -p pathland-core-capi
 cd ../java && mvn -q install
 ```
 
 The `pathland-view` core (views, signals, emitter, codec, HTML renderer) needs no
 native library and runs on the JVM alone; only the JNA ring sink loads
 `libpathland_core`.
 
 
 ## Engine example
 
 The engine emits declarative structure (no rects). A signal changes a property;
 the next `emit` writes only the delta opcodes.
 
 ```rust
 use pathland_core::{init_memory, Guest, MemoryLayout};
 use pathland_view::{assign_ids, text, vstack, View, ViewExt};
 
 let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
 let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
 init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
 
 let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut mem, &layout);
 let mut engine = pathland_core::Engine::new();
 
 let mut root = vstack![text("Hello")]
     .spacing(4.0)
     .padding(8.0)
     .build();
 assign_ids(&mut root, &mut 1);
 
 guest.begin_frame();
 engine.emit(&root, &mut guest).unwrap(); // full structure
 guest.end_frame();
 
 root.properties.insert(pathland_core::property_id::SPACING, 12.0f32.to_bits());
 
 guest.begin_frame();
 engine.emit(&root, &mut guest).unwrap(); // exactly one SET_PROPERTY
 guest.end_frame();
 ```
 
 Emission in the steady state allocates nothing; only changed nodes produce
 opcodes, so an unchanged tree emits zero opcodes. Native renderers map the
 structure onto their native elements (GTK4 widgets, DOM elements).
 
 ## Network transport example
 
 Frames emitted into the ring can be serialized into network batches and flushed
 on a time/size policy (`BatchEncoder` / `Batcher`); a `BatchDecoder` rebuilds a
 `Frame`-compatible view so the same `RenderTree::apply_frame` consumes batches
 and shared-memory frames identically. See `spec/OPCODE.md#transport`.

+# pathland-engine-golden — implementation status
+
+**Last updated:** November 1, 2026
+
+Emits shared engine trace fixtures from the canonical Rust engine. Each fixture
+is a self-contained PLPL batch (opcodes + string table) stored as hex under
+`spec/engine-traces/`.
+
+## Implemented
+
+- `mount_text_stack`: mount a `VStack(spacing: 8)` containing `Text("Hello")`.
+- `signal_text_delta`: mount a bound text signal, then change it to `"World"`.
+- `property_signal_delta`: mount a bound `SPACING` signal, then change `8 → 12`.
+- `styled_text_mount`: styled text with `FONT_SIZE` and `SET_TEXT`, proving the
+  canonical property-before-text order.
+- `structural_add_remove`: append a text child, then remove it
+  (`REMOVE_CHILD` + `DELETE_NODE`).
+- `--emit` regenerates the committed fixtures.
+- `--check` compares the committed fixtures with current engine output.
+- CI runs `--check` (via regeneration + `git diff --exit-code`).
+
+The Java engine test (`EngineTraceTest`) builds the same scenarios through the
+Java DSL and compares its encoded frames byte-for-byte.
+
+## Not implemented / gaps
+
+- Scenario construction is still duplicated between this Rust generator and the
+  JVM test; a neutral scenario DSL is future work.

+  recompute, tokens/lists, fit, media, navigation, and window metadata are next.
