 # pathland-engine — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** October 27, 2026
 
 The retained-tree **emitter**: the application's canonical UI tree and the
 diff-based reactive emission into `TREE`/`PARAMETER` opcodes. Protocol contract:
 `spec/`.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Window metadata bindings**: `Engine::bind_window_metadata`/`bind_window_field` bind fields to signals; mount emits the initial `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` fields, a signal write emits only the changed field, and unchanged values emit zero opcodes.
 
 - **Retained tree** (`node.rs`): `Node` (id, component, children, properties,
   `string_properties`, `token_properties`, text/property signal bindings,
   app-side gestures). Components include `Icon` (→ `component_type::ICON`).
 - **String-valued properties**: `Node::string_properties` (property → value,
   e.g. `FONT_FAMILY`, `LABEL`, `IMAGE_SOURCE`) emit as `SET_PROPERTY` with the
   `STRING` value type (arena-allocated); unchanged strings reuse their arena
   offset — steady-state emission stays zero-alloc with string props present
   (proven by test).
 - **Components** (`Component` enum): the full spec set — `VStack`, `HStack`,
   `ZStack`, `Text`, `Button`, `Spacer`, `Image`, `Color`, `Shape`, `Divider`,
   `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Grid`, `ScrollView`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`,
   `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `TextField`, `TextEditor`,
   `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`, `ColorPicker` — all mapped to
   `component_type` ids via `component_type_id`.
 - **Diff emitter** (`engine.rs`): create/delete/insert/move deltas,
   property/text deltas, steady-state zero emission.
 - **Design-token property refs**: `Node::token_properties` (property → token
   path) emit as `SET_PROPERTY` with the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type; unchanged
   refs reuse their arena offset across passes — **steady-state emission stays
   zero-alloc with token refs present** (proven by test).
 - **`Engine::set_design_token`** — emits a global `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`
   override (base or `dark.`-prefixed) into the current frame.
 - **Global theme overrides** (`theme.rs`): `Theme` — single-value builders
   (`color`/`f32`/`u32`/`u8`/`string`) for one scheme; `AdaptiveTheme { light,
   dark }` composes a light + dark pair. `Engine::apply_theme` (light-only) and
   `Engine::apply_adaptive_theme` (light as base, dark with the `dark.` prefix;
   STRING values arena-alloc'd) emit the overrides once at mount — they never
   re-emit nodes.
 - **Runtime theming** (`Engine::reset_theme`, `Engine::set_color_scheme`,
   `Engine::replace_theme`, `Engine::replace_adaptive_theme`): emits
   `META::RESET_THEME` / `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME`; `ColorSchemeMode`
   (`Platform`/`Light`/`Dark`) mirrors the wire modes. Replacement is
   reset + apply in one frame; no tree node is re-emitted.
+- **Shared engine traces**: `pathland-engine-golden` emits self-contained
+  PLPL frames for mount and signal-delta scenarios under `spec/engine-traces/`;
+  the JVM `EngineTraceTest` compares byte-for-byte. The canonical mount order is
+  documented in `spec/ENGINE.md`.
 - **Reactive runtime** (`signal.rs`): a shared `Runtime`
   (`Rc<RefCell<Store>>`, `no_std` — no thread-local; the "current computation"
   is an explicit stack in the store) owns value signals, **computed** signals
   (lazy, memoized, equality-suppressed, chained) and **effects** (run
   immediately, then on dependency change) plus `untracked` reads. Typed handles
   `Signal<T>`/`WritableSignal<T>` (`SignalValueKind`/`IntoSignalId`);
   `Engine::signal`/`computed`/`effect`/`read`/`set`. Node text/properties bound
   to a signal re-emit only the bound node on change — including a computed's
   bound nodes (`set_signal` re-emits every changed cell's node deps).
 - **Signals bound to node text/properties**: `set_signal` re-emits only the
   bound nodes (`SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`); `get_signal` returns the current value.
 - **Gestures / input sinks**: `Gesture::Tap` (app-side callback) plus the
   two-way binding sinks `Gesture::ValueInput`/`TextInput`/`DateInput` (with
   `TapHandler`/`ValueInputHandler`/`TextInputHandler`/`DateInputHandler` aliases).
   `collect_tap_handlers` and `collect_input_handlers` (→ `InputHandlers`) expose
   the app-side registries; sinks are never serialized.
 - **Media controller** (`media.rs`, spec/MEDIA.md): `MediaController` — the
   app-side state object owning a resource (`source`/`bind_source`) and its
   transport as signals: commands `playing`/`position`/`volume`/`muted`/
   `looping`/`rate` (each rebindable to an app-owned signal), report feeds
   `time`/`duration`/`volume_report`, `on_ended`, and the convenience transport
   (`play`/`pause`/`toggle`/`seek`/`set_volume`/`set_muted`/`set_looping`/
   `set_rate`). A node references one through the identity-compared
   `MediaControllerRef` (`Node.media_controller`); `Component::MediaController`
   (0x30, non-visual) is the controller's node and `Component::Video` is its
   surface. **Audio has no view.**
 - **String property bindings** (`Node.string_bindings`): a `STRING`-valued
   property bound to a signal (e.g. a controller's `MEDIA_SOURCE`) re-emits only
   that property (`SET_PROPERTY`, `STRING`, arena-allocated) on change — a track
   change emits exactly one opcode.
 - **`assign_ids`** (pre-order stable ids) — the **single id authority**: it hands
   out unique ids, satisfying the frame's **unique-node-id invariant**
   (spec/OPCODE.md §Frame Lifecycle — a frame never carries two nodes with the same
   id). **Media controllers are pinned**: a `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node keeps the id it
   was first given, so a structural swap that shifts other ids never changes the
   playback key; the same pass links each `VIDEO` surface's `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID`
   to the controller node.
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - Only the `Tap` gesture plus value/text/date input sinks; no other gesture.
 - Signal-bound properties cannot carry token refs (a token ref is a static path).
 - `get_signal` returns an owned value (the store is shared via `Rc<RefCell>`).

 `cargo test -p pathland-engine` — emitter deltas, signals (values, computed,
 effects, `untracked`), `component_type_id`.

 # Pathland Conformance Test Vectors
 
 **Wire protocol version:** 1
 **Encoding:** little-endian
 **Opcode size:** 16 bytes
 
 This document provides **golden byte arrays** for the Pathland opcode protocol (see [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md)). A conforming implementation MUST:
 
 - encode each opcode to exactly these 16 bytes, and
 - decode these bytes to the equivalent opcode.
 
 The vectors are enforced by the reference Rust encoder (`pathland-core`,
 `crates/pathland-core/src/conformance.rs`).
 
+Engine-level frames (mount order, signal deltas, zero-op recomputes) are defined
+in [ENGINE.md](./ENGINE.md) and enforced by the shared
+[`engine-traces/`](./engine-traces/) fixtures.
+
 Companion catalogs: [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md) (views), [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md)
 (modifiers/properties), [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md) (events), [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md)
 (design tokens / theming). New IDs allocated there must gain vectors before
 implementations depend on them.
 
 ## Opcode Layout
 
 ```
 [Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
 ```
 
 All multi-byte fields little-endian. `A`/`B`/`C` may carry `f32` bit patterns.
 
 ## Vectors
 
 ### 1. TREE:CREATE_NODE (id=1, VSTACK=0x0010)
 
 ```
 01 01 00 00 01 00 00 00 10 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
 ```
 
 - `01` category = TREE
 - `01` command = CREATE_NODE
 - `00 00` flags = 0
 - `01 00 00 00` A = nodeId = 1
 - `10 00 00 00` B = componentType = 0x0010 (VSTACK)
 - `00 00 00 00` C = 0
 
 ### 2. TREE:INSERT_CHILD (parent=0, child=1, index=APPEND)
 
 ```
 01 03 00 00 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 00 FF FF FF FF
 ```
 
 - `01` category = TREE
 - `03` command = INSERT_CHILD
 - `00 00` flags = 0
 - `00 00 00 00` A = parentId = 0
 - `01 00 00 00` B = childId = 1
 - `FF FF FF FF` C = APPEND (`u32::MAX`)
 
 ### 3. TREE:MOVE_CHILD (parent=1, child=2, newIndex=0)
 
 ```
 01 05 00 00 01 00 00 00 02 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
 ```
 
 - `01` category = TREE
 - `05` command = MOVE_CHILD
 - `00 00` flags = 0
 - `01 00 00 00` A = parentId = 1
 - `02 00 00 00` B = childId = 2
 - `00 00 00 00` C = newIndex = 0
 
 ### 4. PARAMETER:SET_PROPERTY (id=1, propertyId=SPACING=0x0001, valueType=F32, 4.0)
 
 ```
 02 01 00 00 01 00 00 00 01 00 04 00 00 00 80 40
 ```
 
 - `02` category = PARAMETER
 - `01` command = SET_PROPERTY
 - `00 00` flags = 0
 - `01 00 00 00` A = nodeId = 1
 - `01 00 04 00` B = `(valueType << 16) | propertyId` = `(0x04 << 16) | 0x0001`
   - low two bytes `01 00` = propertyId = 0x0001 (SPACING)
   - high byte `04` = valueType = 0x04 (F32)
 - `00 00 80 40` C = 4.0 (f32 LE: 0x40800000)
 
 ### 5. PARAMETER:SET_PROPERTY (id=1, propertyId=COLOR=0x100A, valueType=COLOR=0x07, rgba=0xFF0000FF)
 
 ```
 02 01 00 00 01 00 00 00 0A 10 07 00 FF 00 00 FF
 ```
 
 - `02` category = PARAMETER
 - `01` command = SET_PROPERTY
 - `00 00` flags = 0
 - `01 00 00 00` A = nodeId = 1
 - `0A 10 07 00` B = `(valueType << 16) | propertyId` = `(0x07 << 16) | 0x100A`
   - low two bytes `0A 10` = propertyId = 0x100A (COLOR)
   - high byte `07` = valueType = 0x07 (COLOR)
 - `FF 00 00 FF` C = 0xFF0000FF (opaque blue, `0xAARRGGBB`)
 
 ### 6. PARAMETER:SET_TEXT (id=1, arenaRef=0)
 
 ```
 02 03 00 00 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
 ```
 
 - `02` category = PARAMETER
 - `03` command = SET_TEXT
 - `00 00` flags = 0
 - `01 00 00 00` A = nodeId = 1
 - `00 00 00 00` B = arenaRef = 0 (entry is `[u32 length][bytes]` in the arena)
 - `00 00 00 00` C = 0

 ```
 04 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
 ```
 
 - `04` category = META
 - `01` command = RESET
 - `00 00` flags = 0
 - `00 00 00 00` A = 0
 - `00 00 00 00` B = 0
 - `00 00 00 00` C = 0

 - `01` command = POINTER_DOWN
 - `00 00` flags = 0
 - `05 00 00 00` A = targetId = 5

 - `00 00` flags = 0
 - `05 00 00 00` A = targetId = 5

 ```

 ```
 
 - `04` category = META
 - `03` command = RESYNC (host → guest: request a full snapshot)
 - `00 00` flags = 0
 - `00 00 00 00` A = 0
 - `00 00 00 00` B = 0
 - `00 00 00 00` C = 0

 ```
 04 04 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
 ```
 
 - `04` category = META
 - `04` command = PING (guest → host: transport-liveness heartbeat probe)
 - `00 00` flags = 0
 - `00 00 00 00` A = 0
 - `00 00 00 00` B = 0
 - `00 00 00 00` C = 0
 
 ### 13b. META:PONG
 
 ```
 04 05 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
 ```
 
 - `04` category = META
 - `05` command = PONG (host → guest: reply to `META::PING`)
 - `00 00` flags = 0
 - `00 00 00 00` A = 0
 - `00 00 00 00` B = 0
 - `00 00 00 00` C = 0
 
 > Heartbeat scope: `META::PING`/`META::PONG` are **network batch transport only**
 > (see [OPCODE.md §Transport heartbeat](./OPCODE.md#transport-heartbeat)). A
 > shared-memory ring consumer MUST NOT emit, expect, or relay them; they carry no
 > application state and are never routed into the app's tree, signals, or events.
 
 ---
 
 ## Directions
 
 - `TREE` / `PARAMETER` are **guest → host** (application → renderer).
 - `EVENT` is **host → guest** (renderer → application): raw pointer/keyboard
   inputs with a host-resolved `targetId`. A conforming EVENT encoder/decoder
   MUST reproduce vectors 8–12 and 21–22 exactly.
 - `META` is both directions.
 
 ## Frame Conformance
 
 A complete frame is: delta opcodes written into consecutive ring slots, then a
 `frameCount` increment in the header block. Ring slot `i` occupies bytes
 `[ringOffset + i*16, ringOffset + i*16 + 16)`.
 
 The header block layout and ring semantics are defined in [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#linear-memory-layout).
 
 The host → guest event ring shares the same 16-byte slot format and lives at
 `eventRingOffset` (header `0x2A`), with `eventReadCursor` (0x36, guest-owned)
 and `eventWriteCursor` (0x3A, host-owned). A host writing `EVENT:POINTER_UP`
 into the event ring must reproduce the exact vector-11 bytes in the slot at
 `eventWriteCursor`, then advance `eventWriteCursor`; the guest advances
 `eventReadCursor` after draining.
 
 String-bearing events (`TEXT_CHANGED`, `NAVIGATE` with the `NAVIGATE_URL`
 flag) resolve their text from the host → guest **event arena** (header
 `eventArenaOffset` 0x40 / `eventArenaCursor` 0x48, host-owned, shared memory)
 or the batch's string section (network) — the same dual absolute/relative
 convention as `PARAMETER::SET_TEXT`. See OPCODE.md's
 [event arena](./OPCODE.md#event-arena-host--guest) section.
 
 ## Network Batch Conformance
 
 A network batch serializes opcodes + an arena delta (see
 [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#transport)). A conforming batch encoder/decoder MUST
 reproduce the following bytes exactly. The header's `sequence` field is the
 per-stream monotonic message sequence (see
 [Sequence gap detection](./OPCODE.md#sequence-gap-detection)); the vectors below
 use representative values.
 
 ### 14. NETWORK:BATCH (sequence=1, one CREATE_NODE, arena delta = "Hi")
 
 The single opcode is `TREE:CREATE_NODE (id=1, VSTACK)` from vector 1. The arena
 delta is the self-describing entry for `"Hi"`: `[02 00 00 00][48 69]`.
 
 ```
 4C 50 4C 50 01 00 00 00 01 00 00 00 01 00 00 00
 01 01 00 00 01 00 00 00 10 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
 06 00 00 00 02 00 00 00 48 69
 ```
 
 - `4C 50 4C 50` = magic `PLPL` (u32 `0x504C504C`, little-endian)
 - `01 00` = version 1
 - `00 00` = flags (guest → host)
 - `01 00 00 00` = sequence = 1
 - `01 00 00 00` = opcodeCount = 1
 - `01 01 00 00 01 00 00 00 10 00 00 00 00 00 00 00` = the CREATE_NODE opcode (16 bytes)
 - `06 00 00 00` = arenaDeltaLen = 6
 - `02 00 00 00 48 69` = arena entry `[len=2]["Hi"]`
 
 ### 15. NETWORK:BATCH (sequence=2, empty opcode list, empty arena delta)
 
 ```
 4C 50 4C 50 01 00 00 00 02 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
 00 00 00 00
 ```

 A `SIZE_THAT_FITS` slot's candidate threshold table. `C` is an arena offset; the
 arena entry is a length-prefixed f32 array `[u32 count][f32 × count]`. The wire
 encoding is identical in the live (one selected child) and web-SSR snapshot
 (multiple children, container-query gated first paint) forms — the snapshot form
 differs only in the slot's **child count**, not in any opcode or value (issue #141).
 
 ```
 02 01 00 00 01 00 00 00 39 10 09 00 00 00 00 00
 ```
 
 - `02` category = PARAMETER
 - `01` command = SET_PROPERTY
 - `00 00` flags = 0
 - `01 00 00 00` A = nodeId = 1
 - `32 10 09 00` B = `(valueType << 16) | propertyId` = `(0x09 << 16) | 0x1039`
   - low two bytes `39 10` = propertyId = 0x1039 (FIT_QUERY)
   - high byte `09` = valueType = 0x09 (LIST)
 - `00 00 00 00` C = arenaRef = 0
 
 Arena (entry at offset 0) — thresholds `[0, 480, 720]` (ascending, the `FIT_QUERY`
 ordering contract; the app's candidates map 0→fallback … 2→widest, and in a
 full-snapshot emission the slot's **child order equals this table order**):
 
 ```
 03 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 F0 43 00 00 34 44
 ```
 
 - `03 00 00 00` = count = 3
 - `00 00 00 00` = 0.0f (the threshold-0 fallback)
 - `00 00 F0 43` = 480.0f (0x43F00000 LE)
 - `00 00 34 44` = 720.0f (0x44340000 LE)
 
 ### 28b. `SIZE_THAT_FITS` full-snapshot child order + visibility contract
 
 The full-snapshot (web SSR first document) form of a fit slot carries **every**
 candidate as a child, in `FIT_QUERY` order. The wire differs from the live form
 **only in the slot's child count** — the `FIT_QUERY` opcode + arena are identical
 (28a). Here two candidates with thresholds `[0, 1024]`: child 2 is candidate 0
 (the threshold-0 fallback) and child 3 is candidate 1.
 
 ```
 01 01 00 00 01 00 00 00 17 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
 02 01 00 00 01 00 00 00 39 10 09 00 00 00 00 00
 01 01 00 00 02 00 00 00 10 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
 01 01 00 00 03 00 00 00 10 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
 01 03 00 00 01 00 00 00 02 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
 01 03 00 00 01 00 00 00 03 00 00 00 01 00 00 00
 ```
 
 - `01 01 00 00 01 00 00 00 17 00 00 00 00 00 00 00` = `TREE:CREATE_NODE`
   (id=1, `SIZE_THAT_FITS` 0x17)
 - `02 01 00 00 01 00 00 00 39 10 09 00 00 00 00 00` = `PARAMETER:SET_PROPERTY`
   (id=1, `FIT_QUERY` 0x1039, LIST, arenaRef=0) — bytes per 28a
 - `01 01 00 00 02 00 00 00 10 00 00 00 00 00 00 00` = `TREE:CREATE_NODE`
   (id=2, candidate 0)
 - `01 01 00 00 03 00 00 00 10 00 00 00 00 00 00 00` = `TREE:CREATE_NODE`
   (id=3, candidate 1)
 - `01 03 00 00 01 00 00 00 02 00 00 00 00 00 00 00` = `TREE:INSERT_CHILD`
   (parent=1, child=2, index 0)
 - `01 03 00 00 01 00 00 00 03 00 00 00 01 00 00 00` = `TREE:INSERT_CHILD`
   (parent=1, child=3, index 1)
 
 Arena: `[2][0.0][1024.0]` = `02 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 80 44`.
 
 **Contract** (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §SizeThatFits): child order 2, 3 equals the
 `FIT_QUERY` order; the visible candidate is child 2 below 1024 and child 3 at
 `≥ 1024`; **exactly one** candidate is visible at any width; the `FIT_CHANGED`
 index equals this table index.

   — the old destination subtree root

   (id=6, VSTACK) — the new destination root

   (parent=4, child=6, APPEND)

 reconcile is a diff.

 ```
 04 06 00 00 02 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
 ```
 
 - `04` category = META
 - `06` command = SET_COLOR_SCHEME
 - `00 00` flags = 0
 - `02 00 00 00` A = mode = 2 (dark)
 - `00 00 00 00` B = 0
 - `00 00 00 00` C = 0
 
 ### 43. META:RESET_THEME
 
 Clears every application design-token override (base + `dark.*`) and
 re-resolves token references against the renderer's defaults. A replacement
 theme emits this immediately before its `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides.
 
 ```
 04 07 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
 ```
 
 - `04` category = META
 - `07` command = RESET_THEME
 - `00 00` flags = 0
 - `00 00 00 00` A = 0
 - `00 00 00 00` B = 0
 - `00 00 00 00` C = 0
 
 ### 44. META:SET_WINDOW_METADATA (TITLE, arenaRef=0)
 
 Sets the hosting window/surface title to the string at arena offset 0 (over the
 shared ring the offset is absolute into the guest arena; over the network it is
 relative into the batch's string section). `A=2` describes, `A=3` sets the
 locale. An empty string clears the field.
 
 ```
 04 08 00 00 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
 ```
 
 - `04` category = META
 - `08` command = SET_WINDOW_METADATA
 - `00 00` flags = 0
 - `01 00 00 00` A = fieldId = 1 (TITLE)
 - `00 00 00 00` B = string offset = 0 (`"Pathland"` in the arena)
 - `00 00 00 00` C = 0
 
 ### 45. NETWORK:BATCH (META:SET_WINDOW_METADATA, LOCALE, relative string offset=0)
 
 The same field family over the network transport: the opcode references the
 batch's string section by a **relative** offset.
 
 ```
 4C 50 4C 50 01 00 00 00 05 00 00 00 01 00 00 00
 04 08 00 00 03 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
 06 00 00 00 02 00 00 00 65 6E
 ```
 
 - `4C 50 4C 50` = magic `PLPL`
 - `01 00` = version 1
 - `00 00` = flags = `GUEST_TO_HOST`
 - `05 00 00 00` = sequence = 5
 - `01 00 00 00` = opcodeCount = 1
 - `04 08 00 00 03 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00` = SET_WINDOW_METADATA, field 3 (LOCALE), offset 0
 - `06 00 00 00` = arenaDeltaLen = 6
 - `02 00 00 00 65 6E` = `[u32 length=2]["en"]`
 
 ---
 
 ## Design-Token Resolution Conformance
 
 The token system (catalog, override/default resolution, `dark.` color-scheme
 layer) is defined in [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md). Resolution is a renderer behavior
 and is not byte-encodable; a conforming renderer MUST produce these outcomes.
 
 Given the overrides:
 
 | Token override (via `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`) | Value |
 |------------------------------------------|-------|
 | `color.primary` | `0xFF2563EB` |
 | `dark.color.primary` | `0xFF60A5FA` |
 | `space.base` | `4.0` (F32) |
 
 | Query | Active scheme | Resolves to | Rationale |
 |-------|---------------|-------------|-----------|
 | `color.primary` | dark | `0xFF60A5FA` | `dark.color.primary` override wins (dark layer) |
 | `color.primary` | light | `0xFF2563EB` | dark layer skipped; base override wins |
 | `color.primary` | dark, no `dark.*` override | base override `0xFF2563EB` | base override falls through when the dark layer is empty |
 | `font.body.size` | either | renderer default | no override; defaults are renderer-owned |
 | `font.body.size` | either, override only `font.body` | the `font.body` override | parent-path fallback |
 | `space.2` | either | `8.0` | generative family: `space.base` (4.0) × 2 |
 | `space.0.5` | either | `2.0` | generative family: fractional leaf |
 | `space.2` | either, `space.base` not overridden | renderer default × 2 | generative base falls back to renderer defaults |
 | reference `dark.color.primary` | light | `0xFF60A5FA` — **forced dark** | explicit `dark.` reference resolves the dark layer regardless of scheme |
 | reference `dark.color.primary` | dark | `0xFF60A5FA` | explicit `dark.` reference under dark |
 | reference `missing.token` | either | **unset** (no materialized value) | no override/default → renderer's own default styling, never an error |
 
 A property carrying the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (vector 18) resolves through
 the same algorithm and MUST re-resolve when the active scheme changes. An
 explicit `dark.` reference uses the forced-dark rule above. `META::RESET_THEME`
 (vector 43) clears all overrides and re-resolves.

===================================================================
--- spec/ENGINE.md	
+++ spec/ENGINE.md	
@@ -0,0 +1,204 @@
+# Pathland Engine Semantics
+
+**Status:** Draft
+**Wire protocol version:** 1
+**Last Updated:** November 1, 2026
+
+`OPCODE.md` defines the 16-byte wire format. `CONFORMANCE.md` defines individual
+opcode byte vectors. This document defines the **retained-tree engine behavior**
+that produces frames: what gets emitted, in what order, and what must emit
+nothing.
+
+The shared trace fixtures live in [`engine-traces/`](./engine-traces/). They are
+self-contained PLPL batches (opcodes + frame strings), emitted by the canonical
+Rust engine and compared byte-for-byte by the JVM engine test.
+
+---
+
+## 1. Scope
+
+The engine:
+
+- owns the application's retained tree and signal bindings;
+- compares the current tree with the last emitted snapshot;
+- emits only the `TREE` / `PARAMETER` deltas needed to reach the current tree;
+- never computes layout and never emits rectangles.
+
+The renderer owns native elements, layout, styling defaults, and input
+recognition.
+
+---
+
+## 2. Terms
+
+| Term | Meaning |
+|------|---------|
+| **Mount** | First emission of a tree. Emits the complete structure and content. |
+| **Snapshot** | A full re-emission of the current tree (`META::RESYNC` / reconnect). |
+| **Delta** | Opcodes for nodes that changed since the previous emission. |
+| **Frame** | One bounded batch of opcodes plus its string data. |
+| **Zero-op** | A recompute that emits no opcodes and produces no new frame. |
+
+A renderer may receive any number of deltas after the initial mount/snapshot.
+It must converge to the same rendered tree as a fresh snapshot of the same
+retained tree.
+
+---
+
+## 3. Node identity
+
+Node ids are assigned **pre-order**, root first, starting at `1`.
+
+```text
+VStack(id=1)
+├── Text(id=2)
+└── Text(id=3)
+```
+
+Rules:
+
+- A frame MUST NOT contain two nodes with the same id.
+- Structural reconciliation keeps ids stable for position+type-stable nodes.
+- A removed node gets `TREE::DELETE_NODE`.
+- A new node gets `TREE::CREATE_NODE`.
+- A child relationship is established with `TREE::INSERT_CHILD`.
+- `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` nodes keep their **pinned** playback id across subtree
+  re-emissions (spec/MEDIA.md).
+
+---
+
+## 4. Canonical mount order
+
+For each node, before its children:
+
+1. `TREE::CREATE_NODE`
+2. `TREE::INSERT_CHILD` (when the node has a parent)
+3. node properties (`PARAMETER::SET_PROPERTY`, including token/string/list
+   properties)
+4. node text (`PARAMETER::SET_TEXT`) and date (`PARAMETER::SET_DATE`)
+5. recurse into children, in child order
+
+The child is attached **before** its own content/properties, so an id-keyed
+renderer can create and place the native element before applying content.
+
+The trace fixtures assert this order. Property ordering within a node is
+deterministic and follows the engine's stored property order.
+
+---
+
+## 5. Reactive emission
+
+The engine records which nodes read each signal during emission:
+
+- a text binding (`node.text_binding`);
+- a property binding (`node.property_bindings`);
+- a string-property binding (`node.string_bindings`).
+
+When a signal changes, only the bound nodes re-emit:
+
+- text → `PARAMETER::SET_TEXT`
+- property → `PARAMETER::SET_PROPERTY`
+- string property → `PARAMETER::SET_PROPERTY` with the `STRING` value type
+
+An unrelated signal change emits nothing. A write that does not change the
+signal value emits nothing.
+
+### Zero-op recompute
+
+An unchanged tree or unchanged signal MUST emit **zero** opcodes and MUST NOT
+produce a new frame. This is the steady-state contract that makes the ring
+zero-allocation during idle re-renders.
+
+---
+
+## 6. Structural deltas
+
+When a tree changes structurally:
+
+| Change | Required opcodes |
+|--------|------------------|
+| Node added | `CREATE_NODE` + `INSERT_CHILD` + node content |
+| Node removed | `REMOVE_CHILD` (when parented) + `DELETE_NODE` |
+| Child reordered | `MOVE_CHILD` (same node ids) |
+| Parent changed | remove from old parent + insert under new parent |
+
+The engine does not resend unchanged subtrees. A structural change that leaves
+a descendant identical emits no descendant opcodes.
+
+---
+
+## 7. Fit, media, navigation
+
+These are engine-owned surfaces with the same diff discipline:
+
+- **`SIZE_THAT_FITS`**: only the selected candidate is normally transmitted;
+  snapshot/SSR emission may include every candidate for first paint.
+  `FIT_CHANGED` re-renders only the fit component.
+- **Media**: one non-visual `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node per controller, stable id;
+  a `VIDEO` surface references it via `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID`. Transport changes
+  emit only the changed controller property.
+- **Navigation**: a `NavigationContainer` is an ordinary tracked component; a
+  route change re-renders only its destination slot.
+
+Detailed wire contracts remain in `PRIMITIVES.md`, `MEDIA.md`, and `DSL.md`.
+
+---
+
+## 8. Shared engine traces
+
+Fixtures live under `spec/engine-traces/<scenario>/<step>.plpl.hex`.
+
+- Each file is one **self-contained PLPL batch** (`FrameCodec` format).
+- The hex is lowercase; comments start with `#`.
+- The batch includes the opcode list and the exact frame string table.
+- The fixture is emitted by the canonical Rust engine and compared byte-for-byte
+  by the JVM engine test.
+
+### Current scenarios
+
+| Scenario | Steps | Covers |
+|----------|-------|--------|
+| `mount_text_stack` | `000-mount` | Create/insert order, `SPACING`, `SET_TEXT` |
+| `signal_text_delta` | `000-mount`, `001-set-text` | Mount + text-signal delta only |
+| `property_signal_delta` | `000-mount`, `001-set-spacing` | Mount + property-signal delta only |
+| `styled_text_mount` | `000-mount` | Property-before-text emission order |
+| `structural_add_remove` | `000-mount`, `001-add-child`, `002-remove-child` | Create/insert append, remove+delete |
+
+### Generate
+
+From `lib/rust`:
+
+```bash
+cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --emit
+```
+
+### Verify
+
+```bash
+cd lib/rust && cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --check
+cd lib/java && mvn -q -pl pathland-view -am test -Dtest=EngineTraceTest
+```
+
+CI regenerates the fixtures from Rust and fails on drift; the Java reactor runs
+`EngineTraceTest` as part of `mvn test`.
+
+### Adding a scenario
+
+1. Add the scenario to `pathland-engine-golden`.
+2. Run `--emit` and commit the new fixtures with the behavior change.
+3. Add the equivalent scenario to the JVM `EngineTraceTest`.
+4. Update the table above.
+
+---
+
+## 9. Not covered yet
+
+The trace set is intentionally small at this stage. Future traces should cover:
+
+- structural insert/remove/move deltas;
+- unchanged recompute (zero-op) as a frame-level fixture;
+- design-token and string/list property deltas;
+- window metadata and theme frames;
+- fit-slot selection and snapshot emission;
+- media transport changes;
+- navigation destination swaps.

parts.text:
Need design engine traces. Could start with an initial `spec/ENGINE.md` describing semantics, and a **small set of trace fixtures** implemented in Rust and Java. Need be pragmatic.

We need choose trace format and operations. We want cross-language. Maybe use JSON/TSV. Given no JSON parser in Java core and Rust core no serde? Rust engine has std; can add serde? Could use a simple line-based format similar manifest. Example trace file:
```
# name: mount_text
MOUNT text "Hello"
SIGNAL text "World"
```
But Rust Engine and Java Emitter have different APIs; implementing evaluator for a DSL is work. Could instead define traces as **expected opcode byte frames** for hardcoded scenarios implemented in both Rust and Java tests. For cross-language conformance, a shared fixture file with expected bytes; tests construct the same tree/operations programmatically and compare to fixture bytes. The scenario definitions are duplicated in Rust/Java test code, but expected bytes shared. That catches emission drift. `spec/ENGINE.md` documents scenarios. This is simpler and useful. But "golden engine traces" ideally includes operations. Could use a neutral fixture file with named scenarios and expected hex frame(s), and both tests have matching scenarios by name. That is acceptable initial.

Need define scenarios:
1. `mount_text_vstack`: root VStack(spacing 8) with Text("Hello") → expected mount frame.
2. `signal_text_update`: after mount, set text signal → expected delta frame (`SET_TEXT` only).
3. `structural_insert_remove`: ForEach/list or VStack children change? Java/Rust APIs differ; maybe skip.
4. `unchanged_recompute`: mount then emit/render unchanged → zero opcodes.
5. `property_update`: signal-bound spacing? Could do text.
6. `media` maybe not.

We need know exact emitted bytes for both Rust and Java. They should match; existing tests likely already assert. We can generate fixtures from Rust and test Java. But need ensure both engine node IDs/ordering align. We can implement a single scenario and compare. Need understand Rust API vs Java API. Let's inspect Rust Node/Component DSL and tests, Java EmitterTest.

# Pathland Engine Semantics

**Status:** Draft
**Wire protocol version:** 1
**Last Updated:** November 1, 2026

`OPCODE.md` defines the 16-byte wire format. `CONFORMANCE.md` defines individual
opcode byte vectors. This document defines the **retained-tree engine behavior**
that produces frames: what gets emitted, in what order, and what must emit
nothing.

The shared trace fixtures live in [`engine-traces/`](./engine-traces/). They are
self-contained PLPL batches (opcodes + frame strings), emitted by the canonical
Rust engine and compared byte-for-byte by the JVM engine test.

---

## 1. Scope

The engine:

- owns the application's retained tree and signal bindings;
- compares the current tree with the last emitted snapshot;
- emits only the `TREE` / `PARAMETER` deltas needed to reach the current tree;
- never computes layout and never emits rectangles.

The renderer owns native elements, layout, styling defaults, and input
recognition.

---

## 2. Terms

| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **Mount** | First emission of a tree. Emits the complete structure and content. |
| **Snapshot** | A full re-emission of the current tree (`META::RESYNC` / reconnect). |
| **Delta** | Opcodes for nodes that changed since the previous emission. |
| **Frame** | One bounded batch of opcodes plus its string data. |
| **Zero-op** | A recompute that emits no opcodes and produces no new frame. |

A renderer may receive any number of deltas after the initial mount/snapshot.
It must converge to the same rendered tree as a fresh snapshot of the same
retained tree.

---

## 3. Node identity

Node ids are assigned **pre-order**, root first, starting at `1`.

```text
VStack(id=1)
├── Text(id=2)
└── Text(id=3)
```

Rules:

- A frame MUST NOT contain two nodes with the same id.
- Structural reconciliation keeps ids stable for position+type-stable nodes.
- A removed node gets `TREE::DELETE_NODE`.
- A new node gets `TREE::CREATE_NODE`.
- A child relationship is established with `TREE::INSERT_CHILD`.
- `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` nodes keep their **pinned** playback id across subtree
  re-emissions (spec/MEDIA.md).

---

## 4. Canonical mount order

For each node, before its children:

1. `TREE::CREATE_NODE`
2. `TREE::INSERT_CHILD` (when the node has a parent)
3. node properties (`PARAMETER::SET_PROPERTY`, including token/string/list
   properties)
4. node text (`PARAMETER::SET_TEXT`) and date (`PARAMETER::SET_DATE`)
5. recurse into children, in child order

The child is attached **before** its own content/properties, so an id-keyed
renderer can create and place the native element before applying content.

The trace fixtures assert this order. Property ordering within a node is
deterministic and follows the engine's stored property order.

---

## 5. Reactive emission

The engine records which nodes read each signal during emission:

- a text binding (`node.text_binding`);
- a property binding (`node.property_bindings`);
- a string-property binding (`node.string_bindings`).

When a signal changes, only the bound nodes re-emit:

- text → `PARAMETER::SET_TEXT`
- property → `PARAMETER::SET_PROPERTY`
- string property → `PARAMETER::SET_PROPERTY` with the `STRING` value type

An unrelated signal change emits nothing. A write that does not change the
signal value emits nothing.

### Zero-op recompute

An unchanged tree or unchanged signal MUST emit **zero** opcodes and MUST NOT
produce a new frame. This is the steady-state contract that makes the ring
zero-allocation during idle re-renders.

---

## 6. Structural deltas

When a tree changes structurally:

| Change | Required opcodes |
|--------|------------------|
| Node added | `CREATE_NODE` + `INSERT_CHILD` + node content |
| Node removed | `DELETE_NODE` |
| Child reordered | `MOVE_CHILD` (same node ids) |
| Parent changed | remove from old parent + insert under new parent |

The engine does not resend unchanged subtrees. A structural change that leaves
a descendant identical emits no descendant opcodes.

---

## 7. Fit, media, navigation

These are engine-owned surfaces with the same diff discipline:

- **`SIZE_THAT_FITS`**: only the selected candidate is normally transmitted;
  snapshot/SSR emission may include every candidate for first paint.
  `FIT_CHANGED` re-renders only the fit component.
- **Media**: one non-visual `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node per controller, stable id;
  a `VIDEO` surface references it via `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID`. Transport changes
  emit only the changed controller property.
- **Navigation**: a `NavigationContainer` is an ordinary tracked component; a
  route change re-renders only its destination slot.

Detailed wire contracts remain in `PRIMITIVES.md`, `MEDIA.md`, and `DSL.md`.

---

## 8. Shared engine traces

Fixtures live under `spec/engine-traces/<scenario>/<step>.plpl.hex`.

- Each file is one **self-contained PLPL batch** (`FrameCodec` format).
- The hex is lowercase; comments start with `#`.
- The batch includes the opcode list and the exact frame string table.
- The fixture is emitted by the canonical Rust engine and compared byte-for-byte
  by the JVM engine test.

### Current scenarios

| Scenario | Steps | Covers |
|----------|-------|--------|
| `mount_text_stack` | `000-mount` | Create/insert order, `SPACING`, `SET_TEXT` |
| `signal_text_delta` | `000-mount`, `001-set-text` | Mount + text-signal delta only |
| `property_signal_delta` | `000-mount`, `001-set-spacing` | Mount + property-signal delta only |

### Generate

From `lib/rust`:

```bash
cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --emit
```

### Verify

```bash
cd lib/rust && cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --check
cd lib/java && mvn -q -pl pathland-view -am test -Dtest=EngineTraceTest
```

CI regenerates the fixtures from Rust and fails on drift; the Java reactor runs
`EngineTraceTest` as part of `mvn test`.

### Adding a scenario

1. Add the scenario to `pathland-engine-golden`.
2. Run `--emit` and commit the new fixtures with the behavior change.
3. Add the equivalent scenario to the JVM `EngineTraceTest`.
4. Update the table above.

---

## 9. Not covered yet

The trace set is intentionally small at this stage. Future traces should cover:

- structural insert/remove/move deltas;
- unchanged recompute (zero-op) as a frame-level fixture;
- design-token and string/list property deltas;
- window metadata and theme frames;
- fit-slot selection and snapshot emission;
- media transport changes;
- navigation destination swaps.

# pathland-engine — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 27, 2026

The retained-tree **emitter**: the application's canonical UI tree and the
diff-based reactive emission into `TREE`/`PARAMETER` opcodes. Protocol contract:
`spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Window metadata bindings**: `Engine::bind_window_metadata`/`bind_window_field` bind fields to signals; mount emits the initial `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` fields, a signal write emits only the changed field, and unchanged values emit zero opcodes.

- **Retained tree** (`node.rs`): `Node` (id, component, children, properties,
  `string_properties`, `token_properties`, text/property signal bindings,
  app-side gestures). Components include `Icon` (→ `component_type::ICON`).
- **String-valued properties**: `Node::string_properties` (property → value,
  e.g. `FONT_FAMILY`, `LABEL`, `IMAGE_SOURCE`) emit as `SET_PROPERTY` with the
  `STRING` value type (arena-allocated); unchanged strings reuse their arena
  offset — steady-state emission stays zero-alloc with string props present
  (proven by test).
- **Components** (`Component` enum): the full spec set — `VStack`, `HStack`,
  `ZStack`, `Text`, `Button`, `Spacer`, `Image`, `Color`, `Shape`, `Divider`,
  `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Grid`, `ScrollView`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`,
  `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `TextField`, `TextEditor`,
  `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`, `ColorPicker` — all mapped to
  `component_type` ids via `component_type_id`.
- **Diff emitter** (`engine.rs`): create/delete/insert/move deltas,
  property/text deltas, steady-state zero emission.
- **Design-token property refs**: `Node::token_properties` (property → token
  path) emit as `SET_PROPERTY` with the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type; unchanged
  refs reuse their arena offset across passes — **steady-state emission stays
  zero-alloc with token refs present** (proven by test).
- **`Engine::set_design_token`** — emits a global `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`
  override (base or `dark.`-prefixed) into the current frame.
- **Global theme overrides** (`theme.rs`): `Theme` — single-value builders
  (`color`/`f32`/`u32`/`u8`/`string`) for one scheme; `AdaptiveTheme { light,
  dark }` composes a light + dark pair. `Engine::apply_theme` (light-only) and
  `Engine::apply_adaptive_theme` (light as base, dark with the `dark.` prefix;
  STRING values arena-alloc'd) emit the overrides once at mount — they never
  re-emit nodes.
- **Runtime theming** (`Engine::reset_theme`, `Engine::set_color_scheme`,
  `Engine::replace_theme`, `Engine::replace_adaptive_theme`): emits
  `META::RESET_THEME` / `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME`; `ColorSchemeMode`
  (`Platform`/`Light`/`Dark`) mirrors the wire modes. Replacement is
  reset + apply in one frame; no tree node is re-emitted.
- **Reactive runtime** (`signal.rs`): a shared `Runtime`
  (`Rc<RefCell<Store>>`, `no_std` — no thread-local; the "current computation"
  is an explicit stack in the store) owns value signals, **computed** signals
  (lazy, memoized, equality-suppressed, chained) and **effects** (run
  immediately, then on dependency change) plus `untracked` reads. Typed handles
  `Signal<T>`/`WritableSignal<T>` (`SignalValueKind`/`IntoSignalId`);
  `Engine::signal`/`computed`/`effect`/`read`/`set`. Node text/properties bound
  to a signal re-emit only the bound node on change — including a computed's
  bound nodes (`set_signal` re-emits every changed cell's node deps).
- **Signals bound to node text/properties**: `set_signal` re-emits only the
  bound nodes (`SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`); `get_signal` returns the current value.
- **Gestures / input sinks**: `Gesture::Tap` (app-side callback) plus the
  two-way binding sinks `Gesture::ValueInput`/`TextInput`/`DateInput` (with
  `TapHandler`/`ValueInputHandler`/`TextInputHandler`/`DateInputHandler` aliases).
  `collect_tap_handlers` and `collect_input_handlers` (→ `InputHandlers`) expose
  the app-side registries; sinks are never serialized.
- **Media controller** (`media.rs`, spec/MEDIA.md): `MediaController` — the
  app-side state object owning a resource (`source`/`bind_source`) and its
  transport as signals: commands `playing`/`position`/`volume`/`muted`/
  `looping`/`rate` (each rebindable to an app-owned signal), report feeds
  `time`/`duration`/`volume_report`, `on_ended`, and the convenience transport
  (`play`/`pause`/`toggle`/`seek`/`set_volume`/`set_muted`/`set_looping`/
  `set_rate`). A node references one through the identity-compared
  `MediaControllerRef` (`Node.media_controller`); `Component::MediaController`
  (0x30, non-visual) is the controller's node and `Component::Video` is its
  surface. **Audio has no view.**
- **String property bindings** (`Node.string_bindings`): a `STRING`-valued
  property bound to a signal (e.g. a controller's `MEDIA_SOURCE`) re-emits only
  that property (`SET_PROPERTY`, `STRING`, arena-allocated) on change — a track
  change emits exactly one opcode.
- **`assign_ids`** (pre-order stable ids) — the **single id authority**: it hands
  out unique ids, satisfying the frame's **unique-node-id invariant**
  (spec/OPCODE.md §Frame Lifecycle — a frame never carries two nodes with the same
  id). **Media controllers are pinned**: a `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node keeps the id it
  was first given, so a structural swap that shifts other ids never changes the
  Java model routes events by node id through the emitter's registries
  (`RenderResult`), so the frame (SSR) path does not set them automatically.
  On the ring (desktop) path the emitter auto-sets `BINDING_ID` for bound
  controls (see Implemented) — the GTK renderer gates value/text events on it.
- Structural reconcile does not emit `SET_PROPERTY` for a *removed* property on
  a matched node (the wire has no unset; the renderer keeps the last value) —
  consistent with the Rust engine.

## Verified by

`mvn test` (JDK 17+) — emitter, codec round-trips (incl. `NAVIGATE`), signals,
state, reactive bodies (`ReactiveBodyTest`), reactive slots (`ViewOfTest`),
reactive lists (`ForEachTest`) and the router (`RouterTest`:
initial route + `ROUTE` property + `NAV_DEPTH` depth tracking + `NAV_CHROME`
chrome mode, destination swap deltas, back-stack, params, guard redirect,
fallback, `NAVIGATE` routing, `NavigationLink`, the **declarative nav
intents** (`.navigate/.push/.replace` + router-agnostic `NavigationLink`
resolving to the nearest enclosing router via `navigateActions`), the
**`Navigation` facade / `Params` / `isActive`**, the **scoped environment
values** (`View.environment` + `Environment.value` hierarchy/restore), and the
**universal active path** (a bound router re-routing guard-aware on external
signal writes + mirroring its own navigation; `onPathChange` firing on changes));
the JNA ring
test runs when `libpathland_core` is on `java.library.path`. The v2 authoring
surface is covered by `ViewBuilderTest` (with/modifiers/children any-order) and
`ModifierWithTest` (modifier `with(...)`, enum/`Font` value-is-modifier,
`Frame.with` builder); signals-first configs by `ReactiveConfigTest` (a
non-constant value member re-emits exactly one `SET_PROPERTY` — boolean, float,
enum, string, container spacing — and a constant registers no binding). CI proves
every LTS from 17 (Temurin 17/21/25).

  override (base or `dark.`-prefixed) into the current frame.
- **Global theme overrides** (`theme.rs`): `Theme` — single-value builders
  (`color`/`f32`/`u32`/`u8`/`string`) for one scheme; `AdaptiveTheme { light,
  dark }` composes a light + dark pair. `Engine::apply_theme` (light-only) and
  `Engine::apply_adaptive_theme` (light as base, dark with the `dark.` prefix;
  STRING values arena-alloc'd) emit the overrides once at mount — they never
  re-emit nodes.
- **Runtime theming** (`Engine::reset_theme`, `Engine::set_color_scheme`,
  `Engine::replace_theme`, `Engine::replace_adaptive_theme`): emits
  `META::RESET_THEME` / `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME`; `ColorSchemeMode`
  (`Platform`/`Light`/`Dark`) mirrors the wire modes. Replacement is
  reset + apply in one frame; no tree node is re-emitted.
- **Reactive runtime** (`signal.rs`): a shared `Runtime`
  (`Rc<RefCell<Store>>`, `no_std` — no thread-local; the "current computation"
  is an explicit stack in the store) owns value signals, **computed** signals
  (lazy, memoized, equality-suppressed, chained) and **effects** (run
  immediately, then on dependency change) plus `untracked` reads. Typed handles
  `Signal<T>`/`WritableSignal<T>` (`SignalValueKind`/`IntoSignalId`);
  `Engine::signal`/`computed`/`effect`/`read`/`set`. Node text/properties bound
  to a signal re-emit only the bound node on change — including a computed's
  bound nodes (`set_signal` re-emits every changed cell's node deps).
- **Signals bound to node text/properties**: `set_signal` re-emits only the
  bound nodes (`SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`); `get_signal` returns the current value.
- **Gestures / input sinks**: `Gesture::Tap` (app-side callback) plus the
  two-way binding sinks `Gesture::ValueInput`/`TextInput`/`DateInput` (with
  `TapHandler`/`ValueInputHandler`/`TextInputHandler`/`DateInputHandler` aliases).
  `collect_tap_handlers` and `collect_input_handlers` (→ `InputHandlers`) expose
  the app-side registries; sinks are never serialized.
- **Media controller** (`media.rs`, spec/MEDIA.md): `MediaController` — the
  app-side state object owning a resource (`source`/`bind_source`) and its
  transport as signals: commands `playing`/`position`/`volume`/`muted`/
  `looping`/`rate` (each rebindable to an app-owned signal), report feeds
  `time`/`duration`/`volume_report`, `on_ended`, and the convenience transport
  (`play`/`pause`/`toggle`/`seek`/`set_volume`/`set_muted`/`set_looping`/
  `set_rate`). A node references one through the identity-compared
  `MediaControllerRef` (`Node.media_controller`); `Component::MediaController`
  (0x30, non-visual) is the controller's node and `Component::Video` is its
  surface. **Audio has no view.**
- **String property bindings** (`Node.string_bindings`): a `STRING`-valued
  property bound to a signal (e.g. a controller's `MEDIA_SOURCE`) re-emits only
  that property (`SET_PROPERTY`, `STRING`, arena-allocated) on change — a track
  change emits exactly one opcode.
- **`assign_ids`** (pre-order stable ids) — the **single id authority**: it hands
  out unique ids, satisfying the frame's **unique-node-id invariant**
  (spec/OPCODE.md §Frame Lifecycle — a frame never carries two nodes with the same
  id). **Media controllers are pinned**: a `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node keeps the id it
  was first given, so a structural swap that shifts other ids never changes the
  Java model routes events by node id through the emitter's registries
  (`RenderResult`), so the frame (SSR) path does not set them automatically.
  On the ring (desktop) path the emitter auto-sets `BINDING_ID` for bound
  controls (see Implemented) — the GTK renderer gates value/text events on it.
- Structural reconcile does not emit `SET_PROPERTY` for a *removed* property on
  a matched node (the wire has no unset; the renderer keeps the last value) —
  consistent with the Rust engine.

## Verified by

`mvn test` (JDK 17+) — emitter, codec round-trips (incl. `NAVIGATE`), signals,
state, reactive bodies (`ReactiveBodyTest`), reactive slots (`ViewOfTest`),
reactive lists (`ForEachTest`) and the router (`RouterTest`:
initial route + `ROUTE` property + `NAV_DEPTH` depth tracking + `NAV_CHROME`
chrome mode, destination swap deltas, back-stack, params, guard redirect,
fallback, `NAVIGATE` routing, `NavigationLink`, the **declarative nav
intents** (`.navigate/.push/.replace` + router-agnostic `NavigationLink`
resolving to the nearest enclosing router via `navigateActions`), the
**`Navigation` facade / `Params` / `isActive`**, the **scoped environment
values** (`View.environment` + `Environment.value` hierarchy/restore), and the
**universal active path** (a bound router re-routing guard-aware on external
signal writes + mirroring its own navigation; `onPathChange` firing on changes));
the JNA ring
test runs when `libpathland_core` is on `java.library.path`. The v2 authoring
surface is covered by `ViewBuilderTest` (with/modifiers/children any-order) and
`ModifierWithTest` (modifier `with(...)`, enum/`Font` value-is-modifier,
`Frame.with` builder); signals-first configs by `ReactiveConfigTest` (a
non-constant value member re-emits exactly one `SET_PROPERTY` — boolean, float,
enum, string, container spacing — and a constant registers no binding). CI proves
every LTS from 17 (Temurin 17/21/25).

Index: AGENTS.md
===================================================================
--- AGENTS.md	
+++ AGENTS.md	
@@ -1,701 +1,701 @@
 # Pathland Project - AI Agent Guide
 
 This document provides essential context for AI agents (or human contributors) working on the **Pathland** protocol. It captures the project's direction, architectural decisions, and implementation details to ensure consistency.
 
 **Last Updated**: November 1, 2026
 
 ---
 
 ## Architecture: Rust Opcode Engine
 
 > The canonical core is a **Rust engine** that emits the application's
 > **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding,
 > alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer** into shared linear
 > memory, consumed by host renderers. View components and modifiers are written
 > in Rust with a SwiftUI-like API, and in Java with the hand-written
 > **`dev.pathland.view` DSL** (reusable library, Java 17+); both drive the engine
 > through the flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-view-native`) over a zero-copy shared
 > ring on desktop.
 
 ### The 16-byte Opcode Engine
 
 - Every opcode is exactly **16 bytes**: `Category (1B) | Command ID (1B) | Flags (2B) | A (4B) | B (4B) | C (4B)`, `#[repr(C, packed)]`, little-endian.
 - A 64-byte cache line holds exactly **4 opcodes** → L1-cache-friendly.
 - Opcodes live in a **ring buffer** in linear memory; the guest writes at `writeCursor`, the host reads from `readCursor`; frame boundaries via a monotonic `frameCount` in the header block.
 - **Both directions are binary**: a second **event ring** (host → guest) carries `EVENT`-category opcodes. The renderer writes raw inputs at `eventWriteCursor`; the guest drains them at `eventReadCursor`. Events are 16-byte opcodes through the engine, never a side-channel callback.
 - **Variable-length data** (strings, token paths) lives in a bump **arena**; opcodes reference entries by offset (`[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`), so every opcode stays 16 bytes. A second host-owned **event arena** mirrors this in the host → guest direction (shared-memory event strings, e.g. `TEXT_CHANGED`); over the network, host → guest strings ride the batch's string section.
 - **Window metadata** (`META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA`, field family `TITLE`/`DESCRIPTION`/`LOCALE`) carries the hosting surface's presentation metadata; renderers map it to their own chrome (browser `<title>`/meta description/`<html lang>`, GTK/Qt window title). It is root-scoped and signal-backed, so a route title is a computed over the router. Web-only artifacts (canonical/robots/sitemap) stay host-owned.
 - Spec: **`spec/OPCODE.md`** (primary) + **`spec/CONFORMANCE.md`** (golden vectors). Companion catalogs: **`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`** (views), **`spec/MODIFIERS.md`** (modifiers/properties), **`spec/EVENTS.md`** (events), **`spec/LAYOUT.md`** (frame & layout allocation contract) — draft IDs are allocated there spec-first.
 
 ### Declarative, not positioned (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The engine describes WHAT the UI is — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
 > padding, alignment — never WHERE it is. It does not compute layout and does
 > not emit rects.**
 
 - The engine emits **declarative structure** (`TREE` create/delete/insert/remove/move) + **constraint properties** (`PARAMETER` spacing/padding/alignment/FILL/HUG hints).
 - **Native elements everywhere**: each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that platform's native elements — GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the browser, HTML server-side — and those native elements lay themselves out. Never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent.
 - **Reactive emission**: emission is diff-based. Only the nodes that changed emit opcodes (property diffs via `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT`, structural diffs via `TREE` opcodes). An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes. Signals in the application mark the tree dirty; the engine reconciles.
 - **Zero dynamic heap allocations** during steady-state emission (proven by test).
 
 ### no_std / wasm32 direction guard (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 `pathland-core` and `pathland-view` must remain `#![no_std]` + `alloc` and
 compile for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`. This is the guarantee that the protocol
 core can still target a browser / embedded / remote projection later (goal #15,
 Quarkus SSR + WebSocket). The desktop path (`pathland-view-native`) is the only
 consumer today, but the core must not become desktop-only. Verify with
 `lib/rust/check-wasm.sh` (i.e. `cargo build -p pathland-core -p pathland-view
 --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`).
 
 ### Reactive signals (Angular-style)
 
 `pathland-core::signal` provides writable signals that live in the engine. A
 node binds its text (`Node::text_binding`), a property
 (`Node::property_bindings`) or a **string property** (`Node::string_bindings`,
 e.g. a media controller's `MEDIA_SOURCE`) to a `SignalId`; during emit the engine
 resolves the binding and records the dependency, and `Engine::set_signal`
 re-emits **only the bound nodes** (`SET_TEXT` / `SET_PROPERTY`) — no full tree
 walk. Signal values
 are one of `F32`/`U32`/`Bool`/`Enum`/`Str` (packed to the wire's `u32` value or
 arena string). Foreign hosts reach signals via the flat C ABI
 (`pathland_native_signal_create_*` / `signal_set_*` / `node_bind_text` /
 `node_bind_property`) and the Java `Signal` type. Binding then calling `emit`
 records the dependency; a subsequent `set` is a partial emit. (Computed/derived
 signals + effects are the planned next step.)

 ### HTML base design (`design/`)
 
 The HTML renderer's built-in stylesheet is generated from a **three-layer Style
 Dictionary pipeline** plus hand-authored reset/component CSS (one built-in base
 design; no app-facing base-design selection):
 
 ```
 design/tokens/base/*.tokens.json      # internal palette + scales (not emitted)
 design/tokens/semantic/*.tokens.json  # protocol catalog semantics (emitted)
 design/tokens/component/*.tokens.json # per-component surface (emitted)
 design/html/{reset,components}.css    # hand-authored CSS consuming var(--pl-*)
 design/scripts/{build,dev,check}.mjs  # SD build, watcher/preview, validation
 design/build/base.css                 # generated: reset + tokens + components
 design/build/base.css.name            # content hash: base-<sha256-12>.css
 ```
 
 - Tokens are flat DTCG entries (`$value`/`$type`/`$extensions.pathland`) because
   the catalog has both leaf and group paths (`control.border` vs
   `control.border.width`). Dark values live on `$extensions.pathland.dark`;
   durations/z-index/`em` icon sizes are marked internal.
 - `npm --prefix design run build` generates
   `design/build/{tokens.css,manifest.json,base.css,base.css.name}`;
   `npm --prefix design run check` validates catalog coverage, layer direction,
   dark/forced-dark declarations, dimension/`isLengthToken` rules, and the CSS
   content hash.
 - `scripts/sync-design-css.sh` copies the bundle + name to
   `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/` (committed; `--check` fails on
   drift). `css.rs` embeds both with `include_str!` (`builtin_css()` /
   `builtin_css_name()`).
 - The renderer's library default is inline (`render_document`); the linked mode
   (`render_document_linked`, C ABI `pathland_html_render_linked` +
   `pathland_html_base_css[_name]`, Java `renderLinked`/`baseCss`/`baseCssName`)
   emits `{base}/base-<hash>.css`. The Spring Boot and Quarkus starters use it
   and serve the renderer-owned bytes immutable (global + mounted bases); token
   overrides/fit rules stay inline.
 - `scripts/lib.sh` (`build_rust_html`), the Maven `refresh-ide` profile, and CI
   run the design build + sync. Do not edit generated CSS by hand.
 
 ### Native C-ABI shim (`pathland-view-native` + `pathland-core-capi`)
 
 The **desktop/cross-language zero-copy path**: `pathland-view-native` exposes the
 flat world (the flat `builder`/`engine` surface) as `pathland_native_*` C
 functions with a **shared-memory ring** the host driver reads in place. Any
 language that links the dylib (Swift/Java/C# via FFI) calls the flat surface —
 no per-component wrappers — and consumes opcodes zero-copy.
 
 `pathland-core-capi` (`libpathland_core`) is the **minimal ring C ABI** for the
 Java DSL: `pathland_core_create`/`destroy`, `pathland_ring_buffer_push` (one
 raw 16-byte opcode), `pathland_core_arena_alloc`, frame boundaries, zero-copy
 `ring_ptr`/`ring_len`, and event drain/send. The Java DSL
 (`dev.pathland.view.core.ffm`) binds it with **JNA** (lazily loaded, zero JNI) and
 owns the retained tree + diff emission itself.
 
 ### GTK4 Renderer (`pathland-render-gtk`)
 
 The desktop renderer: a single crate that owns **all** GTK/glib/pango usage and
 maps opcode frames **incrementally** onto native GTK widgets (a retained
 `id → gtk::Widget` map). Both the Rust demo and the Java demo render through
 it — the demos **never call GTK or Swing directly**:
 
 - Rust demo links `pathland-render-gtk` as an `rlib` and calls `GtkRenderer::run(...)`
   with a wake closure.
 - Java demo (`pathland-gtk-demo`) loads `pathland-render-gtk` as a `cdylib` via JNA and
   calls `pathland_gtk_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` over the Java DSL's own
   `libpathland_core` ring; native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes through the shared
   ring. The renderer **writes** the events and **wakes** the host (no payload); the host
   drains the event ring itself via `pathland_core_drain_events`. Events are never
   delivered through a side-channel callback — they flow through the opcode engine.
   The demo mounts `MusicPlayerView` (the same shared views the web demos use) with the
   app-driven media contract: the renderer plays the tracks through a direct GStreamer
   `playbin` and reports `MEDIA_*` events back; the demo's web-style
   `/_pathland/assets/...` paths resolve against an extracted local asset root
   (`pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`).
 
 The renderer maps native inputs onto the raw `Event` surface via GTK4
 controllers (`Button::clicked` → pointer up, `EventControllerMotion` →
 pointer move/enter/leave), emitting events through the same `Pump::send_input`
 path.
 
 `pathland_gtk::run` passes an explicit empty argv to GTK (the process command
 line belongs to the embedding host — e.g. the JVM's `-cp`/`-D` flags — and must
 not be parsed as GTK options).
 
 ### Native Java DSL (`dev.pathland.view`, in `lib/java/pathland-view`)
 
 The **hand-written, zero-dependency Java 17+ DSL** (no codegen). It is the
 SwiftUI-like authoring surface shared by desktop, Spring Boot, and Quarkus
 apps. Components and modifiers:
 
 - `View` is an **open interface** — the library ships `Text`/`Image`/`Color`/
   `Rectangle`, `VStack`/`HStack`/`ZStack`, `Spacer`, `Button`,
   `TextField(placeholder, WritableSignal<String>)`, `Video` (a
   `MediaController`'s surface), and application code (Quarkus/Spring/desktop)
   defines its own views by implementing `View`. **Media is a state object, not a
   view** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MediaController` owns the resource + transport as
   signals, a `Video` surface renders it, and **audio has no view** — the app
   binds its own buttons/sliders (`controller.attach()` materializes the
   controller's node once, outside any swapping branch, so a band swap never
   restarts playback).
 - **Custom views and styles use the configurator** (spec DSL.md §2): an
   app-authored `View` with values implements `Configurable<View.Config>`, holds a
   **`private` constructor**, and exposes
   `static ViewBuilder<View, Config> make(Consumer<Config>)`; a style
   (`ButtonStyle`/`LabelStyle`/`VideoStyle`) expose a
   **lowercase static factory** on their own type returning the style value
   (`BorderedButtonStyle.borderedButtonStyle(s -> s…)`), mirroring the library's
   `Modifiers.*` lowercase functions (e.g.
   `borderedButtonStyle(b -> b.padding(..).background(..)…)`). Creation goes
   through the configurator, never a parameterized constructor. The
   `pathland-view-processor` `ViewAuthoringProcessor` **errors** on
   public/protected constructors **with parameters** in custom `View` **and**
   `Style` implementations (no-arg roots and abstract types are exempt), so the
   convention is compile-enforced where the processor is wired
   (`annotationProcessorPaths`). The library's own views/styles follow the same
   shape (`Video`, `Text`, `BorderedButtonStyle`, …).
 - **SwiftUI-style `body()` / reactive components**: composite views declare
   `View body()` (their subtree); the library's primitives override
   `renderNode(Environment)` to materialize a `PathlandNode` (`render(Environment)` is
   the emitter entry point and must not be overridden). `body()` is a **tracked
   render function**: a signal read there subscribes that component, and a later
   write re-renders only that component and diffs its retained subtree — so plain
   `if`/`switch`/`for` over signals works. A signal **bound** to a node
   (`Text.make(t -> t.text(Signal))`) stays fine-grained and does not re-run the
   body. Non-signal reads are mount-time only; render bodies must be pure/idempotent
   and must not write signals. Each child view is a component slot; the root chain
   (body delegation, modifiers, environment/tap/navigation wrappers) is one slot.
   `View.of(Supplier<View>)` is the inline form (Java has no `if` expression);
   `ForEach.of(list | Signal<List<T>>, (item, index) -> View)` is the reactive
   list component (static lists may use streams/`for` directly).
   `NavigationContainer` / `SizeThatFits` are ordinary components. The root
   component type must stay stable across re-renders. (Rust parity is Phase 2.)
 - **Cross-language vocabulary** (spec DSL.md §9.3.1): the same anchors across
   Swift, Java, Kotlin, Rust, and TypeScript — `View`, `body`/`build`, `Signal`,
   `computed`, `State`, `ForEach`, `View.of`, `children`, `modifiers`. Use native
   control flow (`if`/`switch` in Swift/Java, `if`/`when` in Kotlin, `if`/`match`
   in Rust, ternary/`switch` in TypeScript); Java uses `View.of` only where an
   inline expression is needed. Swift is the canonical SwiftUI-shaped reference;
-  Kotlin is implemented by `lib/java/pathland-view-kotlin` (a facade over the Java
-  library), Swift is not implemented yet, and Rust parity is Phase 2.
+  Kotlin is implemented by `lib/java/pathland-view-kotlin` (Kotlin-owned views and
+  modifiers over `pathland-view-core`), Swift is not implemented yet, and Rust
+  parity is Phase 2.
 - **The three operations (spec DSL.md §2)**: every concrete view exposes
   `make(...)` (values — the only static; `make(Consumer<Config>)`, `make(value)`,
   `make()`), and the instance operations `.modifiers(ViewModifier...)` and
   `.children(View...)` chain on the returned builder. Java's static-vs-instance
   rule means the statics sit on the view class, the chain on the builder; a bare
   `View` value applies modifiers through the interface default
   `View.modifiers(...)`. Values are a
   fluent per-view `Config` (`VStack.make(v -> v.alignment(...).spacing(8))`,
   `Text.make(t -> t.text("hi"))`); modifiers are `ViewModifier` values built by
   the **`Modifiers` facade's lowercase functions** — one
   `import static dev.pathland.view.Modifiers.*;` brings the whole modifier
   vocabulary (`padding(p -> p.uniform(16))`, `frame(f -> f.width(100))`,
   `borderedButtonStyle(b -> …)`) — or, for single values, the value itself
   (`FontWeight.BOLD`, `Font.headline()`, a `ButtonStyle`). The `View` interface has
   **no per-modifier sugar** (`font`/`navigate`/`environment`/`onPathChange` were
   removed — use `.modifiers(Font…)`, `.modifiers(NavigationIntent.navigate(…))`,
   `.modifiers(environmentBinding(e -> e.key(…).value(…)))`,
   `.modifiers(pathChange(p -> p.listener(…)))`), and the `*Mod` shims
   (`EnvironmentMod`→`EnvironmentBinding`, `router/NavigationMod`→`NavigationIntent`,
   `PathChangeMod`→`PathChange`, `FontWeightMod`→`FontWeight`, …) are **removed**.
 - **Single-value shortcuts (spec DSL.md §2)**: a view/modifier whose config has a
   designated primary member also exposes a single-value construction overload that
   is pure sugar for the lambda — views construct with `make(value)` / `make(Signal<T>)`
   (`Text.make("hi")`), modifiers with the lowercase function's value form
   (`padding(16)`, `fontSize(sizeSignal)`). Multi-member configs (`Padding.edges`, `Offset`,
   `Gauge`, `Border`, …) have **no** shortcut — use the lambda. The shortcut delegates
   to the same `make(Consumer<Config>)` (views) / `Modifiers` facade
   (modifiers) factory via the package-private
   `Configurators` helper (one construction path). The former `.of(...)` construction
   factories are **removed** — a shortcut (or the lambda / `.children(...)` / empty
   `make()` for config-less views) replaces every one. Only data/branch factories keep
   `of`: `Color.of/rgb/argb/token`, `Fit.of`, `View.of`, `ForEach.of`,
   `EnvironmentKey.of`, `Route.of`, `Params.of`, `Signals.*`.
   Sizing is the `Frame` modifier value
   (`frame(f -> f.width(w).height(h).alignment(..))` and the lambda
   configurator `frame(f -> f.minWidth(..).maxWidth(..).alignment(..))`
   (min/ideal/max bounds)); all
   compile to the same `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT`/min-max `SET_PROPERTY`s.
   Typed enums
   (`Alignment`/`TextAlignment`/`FontWeight`/`Truncation`), not raw ints.
 - **Environment scoping via a `ThreadLocal`** (Java 17+): a `ButtonStyle` modifier
   injects a style down the whole child tree; `ButtonStyle.makeBody(Configuration)`
   with built-in `PlainButtonStyle` / `BorderedButtonStyle`. Custom wrappers via
   `ViewModifier.body(View)`. The `Environment` also carries the session's
   `PersistentState`.
 - **Reactivity (Angular parity)** in `dev.pathland.view.core.signal`:
   `Signals.signal/computed/effect/untracked` — lazy+memoized computeds,
   glitch-free synchronous flush, equality suppression, error caching, write
   discipline (`allowWrites()`), circular-dependency detection.
 - **Persisted view state** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): a `State<T>` field (e.g.
   `State<Integer> count = new State<>(0);`) is auto-wired to the session's
   `PersistentState` (keyed by field name, or `new State<>(0, "key")` for an explicit
   key) by the `pathland-view-processor` annotation processor, which detects `State`
   fields by type and generates a `<View>_StateBinder` per view class. Each view
   connects its own `State` when it renders (`View.render` calls `Environment.state()
   → PersistentState.connect(view)`), so nested views can be instantiated inline in
   `body()` and need not be declared as fields. `PersistentState.signal(name, initial)`
   auto-loads the persisted value and auto-saves on change (key `name:scope`), and
   `StateStore` is untyped (one store serves all signal types).
 - **Fine-grained emitter** (`dev.pathland.view.engine`): mounts a view tree once,
   assigns stable ids, and registers a **node-level binding effect** per reactive
   text/property — a signal change re-emits only that node's `SET_TEXT` /
   `SET_PROPERTY` (unchanged signals emit zero opcodes). Sinks: `FrameOpcodeSink`
   (self-contained frames for SSR/WebSocket) and `RingOpcodeSink` (JNA into
   `libpathland_core`). The wire codec (`dev.pathland.view.core.transport`) mirrors
   `pathland_core_transport` (`PLPL` batch format, self-contained frames + events).
 
 Consistency with `pathland_core::constants` is enforced by the emitter/HTML
 tests (golden byte layout + round-trips), replacing the old codegen assert pass.
 
 - **Single signal value convention**: a view or modifier holds **one `Signal<T>`
   field** for a reactive value — never a raw field *plus* a signal field for the
   same value. Static values are authored through the raw config setter (or the
   `.of(T)` convenience), which
   wraps them in `Signals.constant(...)` (e.g. `Text.make(t -> t.text("Hello"))` ≡
   `Text.make(t -> t.text(Signals.constant("Hello")))`); the emitter treats a
   `ConstantSignal` as
   a plain, non-reactive property (no binding/effect), so statics carry zero
   binding overhead. Controls' config fields for *distinct* properties
   (`min`/`max`/`step`/`placeholder`/`mode`/`style`) stay raw.

 ## Project Vision
 
 **Pathland is a cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol** that enables retained-mode UI development with multiple renderer backends. It is **protocol-first**, meaning the protocol specification is the source of truth, not any particular implementation.
 
 **Primary Goal**: Write once, run anywhere - Enable UI code to be written once and deployed across web, mobile, desktop, and embedded platforms through different renderer implementations.
 
 **Status**: The Rust opcode engine (16-byte opcode, ring buffer, arena, diff-based reactive emission) is implemented and tested (`cargo test`). See the Architecture section above.
 
 ---
 
 ## CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLES
 
 ### Principle 1: Renderer Statelessness (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The renderer MUST NOT retain application state.**
 
 - Renderers are **pure functions** of the opcode stream: same opcodes → same output
 - A renderer MAY retain its **rendered-output tree** (id → native element + computed layout) for drawing, hit-testing, and event routing — this is a cache of its own output, not state
 - The renderer MUST NOT retain component property values as business state, application control flow, or anything the application can change without emitting an opcode
 - The application owns the canonical retained UI tree
 - The engine emits **deltas only**; the renderer applies them to its native elements
 
 **Violation of this principle is a bug, not a feature.**
 
 ### Principle 2: Command-Based Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol transmits tree mutations as a stream of commands, NOT as serialized trees.**
 
 - Each frame is a **batch of delta commands** describing changes
 - Only **actual changes** are transmitted (diff-based reactive emission)
 - Protocol acts like a **VM instruction stream** / ABI
 - Deterministic, linear decoding without schema lookup or reflection
 
 ### Principle 3: Binary Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol MUST be binary.**
 
 - Open-source, cross-platform binary format
 - Fixed **16-byte instructions** in a ring buffer shared with the host via linear memory
 - Custom instruction-based bytecode, not schema-driven serialization
 - **Both directions are binary**: tree mutations (app → renderer) AND raw-input events (renderer → app) share the same instruction format, so the wire is language- and platform-agnostic
 
 ---
 
 ## Protocol Quick Reference
 
 The semantic surface is catalogued in the companion specs: **`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`**
 (primitive views + component IDs), **`spec/MODIFIERS.md`** (core modifiers = the
 `PARAMETER` properties), **`spec/EVENTS.md`** (core events + listener bits),
 **`spec/LAYOUT.md`** (frame & layout allocation contract). The
 tables below are a quick recap of the protocol surface; the companion files
 carry the authoritative ID allocations.
 
 > **Implementation status lives in each project's `status.md`**, not in the
 > specs: `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/status.md`,
 > `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-gtk/status.md`,
 > `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/status.md`,
 > `lib/java/pathland-view-core/status.md`, `lib/java/pathland-view/status.md`, `lib/java/pathland-view-kotlin/status.md`,
 > `lib/java/pathland-render-html/status.md`,
 > and the other Rust crates' `status.md` files.
 
 ### Opcode Format
 
 Every opcode is exactly 16 bytes:
 
 ```
 [Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
 ```
 
 See `spec/OPCODE.md` for the full format, ring buffer, arena, and frame lifecycle.
 
 ### Machine-readable protocol manifest
 
 `spec/protocol.tsv` is the target-neutral ID manifest emitted from
 `pathland_core::constants` by `pathland-protocol-manifest` (`cargo run -p
 pathland-protocol-manifest`). It contains only `kind`, `group`, `name`, and
 `value`; each language binding keeps its own representation and validates or
 reads the manifest. There is no Rust→Java source generation.
 
 The JVM mirror is hand-written and checked by
 `pathland-view-core/src/test/java/.../ProtocolManifestTest`: every manifest row
 must match a Java constant, no extra public numeric constants may exist, and
 `ValueTypes.forProperty` must match `property_value_type`. CI regenerates the
 manifest from Rust and fails on drift.
 
 Engine behavior beyond individual opcodes is specified in `spec/ENGINE.md` and
 enforced by shared self-contained frame traces under `spec/engine-traces/`.
 `pathland-engine-golden` emits them from the Rust engine and the JVM
 `EngineTraceTest` compares its encoded frames byte-for-byte.
 
 ### Categories
 
 | Category | Value | Direction | Description |
 |----------|-------|-----------|-------------|
 | TREE | 0x01 | Guest → Host | Node create/delete/insert/remove/move |
 | PARAMETER | 0x02 | Guest → Host | Constraint properties (spacing, padding, …), design tokens |
 | EVENT | 0x03 | Host → Guest | Raw inputs: pointer down/move/up, key down/up |
 | META | 0x04 | Both | Reset, environment, window metadata |

 ### Key Property IDs
 
 **Stack**: SPACING=0x0001, ALIGNMENT=0x0002, CONTENT_MARGINS=0x0005  
 **Text**: TEXT=0x000A, TEXT_ALIGNMENT=0x000C, LINE_LIMIT=0x000B, TRUNCATION_MODE=0x000D  
 **Style**: COLOR=0x100A, FONT_SIZE=0x1007, FONT_WEIGHT=0x1008, FONT_FAMILY=0x1009, BACKGROUND_COLOR=0x1001, BORDER_WIDTH=0x1003, BORDER_COLOR=0x1004, BORDER_RADIUS=0x1005, OPACITY=0x100D, VISIBLE=0x100E, Z_INDEX=0x100F, CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS=0x1010, PADDING=0x1011, PADDING_TOP/RIGHT/BOTTOM/LEFT=0x1012-0x1015  
 **Special**: WIDTH=0x100B (use -1=FILL, -2=HUG_CONTENT), HEIGHT=0x100C  
 **Semantic**: ROLE=0x2001, STATE=0x2002, ENABLED=0x2003, SELECTED=0x2004, EVENT_LISTENERS=0x2005 (u32 bitmask — which raw events a node wants reported), VALUE=0x2006, MIN_VALUE=0x2007, MAX_VALUE=0x2008, LABEL=0x200A, PROMPT=0x200B  
 **Binding/action**: ACTION_ID=0x2016, BINDING_ID=0x2017, TOGGLE_STYLE=0x2018 (Switch=0, Checkbox=1, Button=2)  
 **Media** (spec/MEDIA.md): MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID=0x103A (a `VIDEO`'s controller), MEDIA_SOURCE=0x103B, MEDIA_MUTED=0x103C, MEDIA_LOOP=0x103D, MEDIA_RATE=0x103E; PLAYBACK_STATE=0x1035 / MEDIA_POSITION=0x1036 / MEDIA_VOLUME=0x1037 live on the controller
 
 ### Colors
 
 - Literal colors are **sRGB** with D65 white point, packed as `0xAARRGGBB`
 - A color property may instead carry a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference to a token path
 - Semantic token resolution and theme adaptation are **renderer-owned**
 
 ### Design Token System
 
 **Core Principle**: Application defines intent, overrides, and the theme.
 Renderer defines visual appearance, behavior, defaults, and interaction states.
 
 - The **application owns the theme**: token overrides (base = **light**, `dark.`-prefixed = **dark**) and token references in style properties. Token refs cover COLOR and non-color values (`Length` for spacing/padding/font size/radius/border/frame; `FontFamily.Token` for STRING) in the Rust and Java DSLs.
 - The **renderer owns** default token values (light + dark, the full Tier-1 catalog), token resolution (including explicit `dark.` = forced dark and parent fallback), effective color-scheme detection, interaction states (hover, pressed, focus, disabled), and theme adaptation
 - `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` identifies tokens by **dot-separated string paths** (e.g. `color.primary`, `space.2`) with the standard value-type encoding — there is no separate numeric tokenId system. A `dark.` prefix selects the dark variant (`dark.color.primary`); a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference whose path starts with `dark.` forces the dark value in either scheme
 - **Runtime theming**: `META::RESET_THEME` clears every app override; a replacement theme is reset + `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides in one frame. `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` forces `platform`/`light`/`dark`. Both are renderer state — no node is re-emitted. Java: `Emitter.replaceTheme`/`setColorScheme` + `PathlandSession.setTheme`/`setColorScheme`; Rust: `Engine::reset_theme`/`set_color_scheme`.
 - An unresolvable token reference leaves the property **unset** (renderer default), never an error or stale value.
 - The protocol MUST NEVER describe hover styles, click styles, visual transitions, conditional styling, or layout tuning for interaction states
 - **Deferred**: applying per-component tokens to native GTK/Qt leaf control chrome; web parent-path fallback.
 
 The HTML renderer's default token values are generated from `design/` (see
 "HTML base design" above). Full details: [Design Token System](./spec/OPCODE.md#design-token-system)
 and the canonical catalog / color-scheme contract in [spec/TOKENS.md](./spec/TOKENS.md).
