 ## 7. Theme management
 
 Pathland theming is **application-owned over a renderer-owned token system**
 ([TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md); the wire encoding lives in [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md)
 §Design Token System). The DSL gives the author two distinct surfaces:
 
 1. **Token references in style modifiers** — semantic intent instead of a
    literal: `foregroundStyle(f -> f.color(Color.token("color.primary")))`
    emits a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference the renderer resolves against the current
    scheme. No opcode is re-emitted when a token or the scheme changes.
 2. **Global theme overrides** — a batch of `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` commands
    rolled at mount: a single-scheme `Theme` or an `AdaptiveTheme` light+dark
    pair (base = **light**, `dark.`-prefixed = **dark**).
 
 > **Ownership**: the application owns theme values (base + `dark.*`) and token
 > references; the renderer owns token defaults (light + dark), effective
 > color-scheme detection, resolution (override → default → parent → fallback),
 > and interaction-state styling (hover/pressed/focus/disabled). The protocol
 > never transmits hover/click/transition styling.
 
 ### 7.1 Token-typed values
 
 Any property whose value type is `COLOR` / `F32` / `STRING` / `ENUM` MAY carry a
 **token reference** instead of a literal value (MODIFIERS.md §Value types). The
 reference rides the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (`0x08`) with the token path in
 the arena — **never** a packed literal. A property carries exactly one value
 (literal or reference, never both).
 
 | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL | Rust DSL | Emits |
 |----------------------------|----------|----------|-------|
 | `Color.token("color.primary")` | `Color.token("color.primary")` | `Color::token("color.primary")` | `DESIGN_TOKEN` ref (`0x08`) in any COLOR-typed property: `COLOR` 0x100A (`.foregroundStyle`), `BACKGROUND_COLOR` 0x1001, `BORDER_COLOR` 0x1004, `SHADOW_COLOR` 0x1021, `TINT` 0x1030, … |
 | `Color.token("dark.color.surface")` | `Color.token("dark.color.surface")` | `Color::token("dark.color.surface")` | same — an explicit dark-variant reference (resolves the dark layer in either scheme) |
 | `.padding(space.2)` / `Spacing(space.2)` | `Padding.with(Length.token("space.2"))` / `spacing(Length.token("space.2"))` | `Padding(Length::token("space.2"))` / `spacing(Length::token("space.2"))` | `DESIGN_TOKEN` ref in a F32-typed property: `PADDING` 0x1011 / `SPACING` 0x0001 / `CONTENT_MARGINS` 0x0005, … (see TOKENS.md §Generative token families) |
 | `Font.body.family` token | `FontFamily.token("font.body.family")` | `FontFamily::token("font.body.family")` | `DESIGN_TOKEN` ref in a STRING-typed property (`FONT_FAMILY`) |
 
 Token references are **static paths**: a signal-bound property carries a
 literal value, not a token reference.
 
 `Color` keeps its dual identity: as a **View** it is a layout-greedy fill; as a
 token reference (`Color.token(path)`) it is a **data value** passed to
 style-taking modifiers. A token-typed property resolves renderer-side and
 **re-resolves automatically** when the effective scheme changes — overrides and
 scheme are renderer state, so no node is ever re-emitted for a theme/scheme
 change.
 
 Rules:
 
 1. Reference any token path — the standard catalog (TOKENS.md §Standard Token
    Catalog) or an application-defined path. A renderer that cannot apply a token
    falls back rather than erroring.
 2. `space.<N>` members are **generative**: reference them freely (`space.2`,
    `space.0.5`), but override only `space.base` (see §7.2 rule 2).
 3. A token reference must not be combined with a literal on the same property.
 
 ### 7.2 Global theme overrides
 
 A **theme** is a batch of token overrides. Every override defines **exactly one
 value**; combine a light and a dark `Theme` via `AdaptiveTheme` for adaptive
 theming.
 
 | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (`dev.pathland.view`) | Rust DSL (`pathland-view` / `pathland-engine`) | Emits |
 |----------------------------|--------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|-------|
 | `Theme()` — one-scheme override batch | `new Theme().color(...)...` | `Theme::new()` | one `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` per override (`A` = arena path, `B` = valueType, `C` = value) |
 | `.color("color.primary", 0xFF2563EB)` | `.color("color.primary", 0xFF2563EB)` | `.color("color.primary", 0xFF2563EB)` | `COLOR`-typed override (sRGB `0xAARRGGBB`) |
 | `.f32("space.base", 4.0)` | `.f32("space.base", 4.0f)` | `.f32("space.base", 4.0)` | `F32`-typed override (lengths in device pixels) |
 | `.u32("…", v)` / `.u8("…", v)` | `.u32(path, int)` / `.u8(path, int)` | `.u32(path, v)` / `.u8(path, v)` | `U32` / `U8`-typed override |
 | `.string("font.body.family", "Inter")` | `.string(path, String)` | `.string(path, "Inter")` | `STRING`-typed override (arena) |
 | `AdaptiveTheme(light, dark)` | `new AdaptiveTheme(light, dark)` | `AdaptiveTheme::new(light, dark)` | light overrides as base tokens; dark overrides `dark.`-prefixed |
 
 Emission contract:
 
 - The theme is emitted **once at mount** as a frame of
   `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` opcodes before the tree. Java: `new Emitter(sink,
   theme)` emits it at the start of the mount and `renderFull` (resync) frames;
   Rust: `Engine::apply_theme` / `Engine::apply_adaptive_theme`.
 - Overrides are **renderer state**: they never re-emit nodes and never
   participate in the diff — an unchanged tree with a theme still emits **zero**
   per-node opcodes.
 - `AdaptiveTheme` emits the light `Theme`'s overrides as base paths and the dark
   `Theme`'s with the `dark.` prefix (added automatically when the author wrote a
   bare path). The renderer derives the effective scheme from the platform and
   resolves each override against it.
 - The renderer supplies light + dark defaults for the whole Tier 1 catalog, so
   dark mode works even when the author only overrides base tokens.
 
 Authoring rules:
 
 1. Override any token in the catalog or an application-defined path; never
    assume specific renderer default values.
 2. Override `space.base` to control the whole spacing scale — individual
    `space.<N>` members MUST NOT be overridden.
 3. Overrides are **global and renderer-wide**: apply the theme once per
    session/host at mount, not per view.
 
 ### 7.3 Runtime theming and scheme choice
 
 A host MAY replace the theme after mount. Replacement is **reset + apply**: the
 host emits `META::RESET_THEME` followed by the new theme's
 `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides in one frame. The renderer clears the
 old overrides, re-resolves every token-referencing property, and re-applies the
 new values; no node is re-emitted.
 
 The host MAY also force the effective scheme with
 `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME`:
 
 | Canonical mode | Emits | Behavior |
 |----------------|-------|----------|
 | `.platform` | `SET_COLOR_SCHEME` A=0 | follow the OS/browser light/dark signal (default) |
 | `.light` | `SET_COLOR_SCHEME` A=1 | force the light design |
 | `.dark` | `SET_COLOR_SCHEME` A=2 | force the dark design |
 
 While forced, platform scheme changes are ignored. Returning to `.platform`
 restores native detection. Both commands are renderer state — the emitter
 re-resolves, never re-emitting the tree.
 
 Java exposes this through `Emitter.replaceTheme(...)` / `resetTheme()` /
 `setColorScheme(...)`; the server runtime's host-level
 `PathlandSession.setTheme(...)` / `setColorScheme(...)` delegate to the same
 emission path. Rust exposes `Engine::reset_theme` / `set_color_scheme` (and
 `replace_theme` / `replace_adaptive_theme`).

 ## 8. Java DSL convergence (adopted)
 
 The Java DSL (`dev.pathland.view`) has the complete surface. The convergence
 below has been **adopted**: construction through the three operations
 (`with` / `modifiers` / `children`), and modifiers as `ViewModifier` values with
 **no `Mod` suffix** and **no per-modifier sugar on `View`**. The canonical

 Adopted conventions:
 
 - **`with` / `modifiers` / `children` are the one construction path.** Every
   concrete view/control exposes these three operations; the former per-view
   construction `.of(...)` is gone (`View.of` is the inline reactive-subtree
   factory, not a view-construction shortcut).
   They are available **at creation or chained, in any order**
   ([§2](#2-canonical-signature-notation)).
 - **`make(config)` is a fluent config builder.** The config holds the view's
   values and is the same type a style's `makeBody(Config)` reads
   ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)).
 - **The `View.*` static-factory surface is removed.** The entire factory block
   (`text`, `image`, `rectangle`, `spacer`, `vstack`, `hstack`, `zstack`,
   `button`, `textField`, `textEditor`, `toggle`, `slider`, `stepper`,
   `progressView`, `gauge`, `divider`, `grid`, `scrollView`, `lazyVStack`,
   `lazyHStack`, `lazyVGrid`, `lazyHGrid`, `picker`, `menu`, `colorPicker`,
   `datePicker`, `group`) is deleted from `View.java`.
 - **`Group` is a first-class view.** `Group.children(View...)` is a
   transparent container view (SwiftUI `Group`).
 - **Core and custom modifiers share one mechanism.** Core modifiers are
   `ViewModifier` values (`padding(p -> p.uniform(16))`,
   `foregroundStyle(f -> f.color(color))`) applied via `.modifiers(...)` —
   there is **no sugar on `View`**; several modifiers at once use
   `.modifiers(...)`, innermost-first. Single-value modifiers pass the value
   directly (`FontWeight.BOLD`).
 - **No `Mod` suffix.** A modifier type is named for the modifier it applies;
   where it wraps a single value, the value type is the modifier. Main's
   `FrameMod → Frame` (with the wire batch renamed `emit.Frame → ProtocolFrame`)
   is the precedent; the remaining `*Mod` types are renamed accordingly
   (`FontWeightMod → FontWeight`, `ButtonStyleMod → ButtonStyle`, …;
   `EnvironmentMod → EnvironmentBinding`, `router/NavigationMod → NavigationIntent`).
 - **Full `ShapeKind` coverage.** `Circle.make()`, `Capsule.make()`,
   `Ellipse.make()`, `RoundedRectangle.make(r -> r.cornerRadius(..))`, generic
   `Shape.make(s -> s.kind(ShapeKind))` (for `Path`).

 ## 9. Generation contract for a new language
 
 An AI (or a human) generating a Pathland DSL in a new language MUST produce the
 following and verify each item. This is a checklist; the authoritative details
 are the companion specs.
 
 ### 9.1 Required surface
 
 - [ ] **Views/controls** — every entry of [§4](#4-view-surface):
   `Text`, `Image`, `Color`, `Shape` (all `ShapeKind`s), `Divider`, `Spacer`,
   `ProgressView`, `Gauge`; `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`,
   `ScrollView`,
   `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`; `Button`,
   `TextField`, `SecureField`, `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`,
   `Picker`, `Menu`, `DatePicker`, `ColorPicker`.
 - [ ] **The three operations** — configure values, apply modifiers, supply
   children — available at creation or by chaining, in any order
   ([§2](#2-canonical-signature-notation)). Each language maps them to its idiom
   ([§9.3](#93-language-adaptation-rules)).
 - [ ] **Modifiers** — every entry of [§5](#5-modifier-surface), applicable to
   any view, innermost-first, emitting one property per underlying argument; a
   modifier's type carries no `Mod` suffix.
 - [ ] **Custom modifiers / unified mechanism** — a `ViewModifier` authoring
   surface (`body(content) -> View`) + a chainable `modifiers(...)` operation on
   **any** view; **core modifiers are implemented through the same mechanism**,
   never a separate syntax ([§5.6](#56-custom-modifiers-developer-authored)).
 - [ ] **Shared config with styles** — a style's `makeBody(Config)` receives the
   same config type the control configured via `make(...)`
   ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)).
 - [ ] **Signals** — `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `untracked`,
   `get`/`set`/`update`/`asReadonly`, with equality suppression, synchronous
   flush, glitch-free propagation, error caching, write discipline, circular
   detection ([§3.1](#31-signal-surface)).
 - [ ] **Two-way bindings** — every value control takes a writable signal (a
   config value) and exposes a sink the host routes its event into
   ([§3.2](#32-two-way-binding)).
 - [ ] **Persisted state** — `State<T>` keyed fields (or the language's
   equivalent wiring) against a platform-neutral store ([§3.3](#33-persisted-state-statet)).
 - [ ] **Gestures** — `.onTapGesture` (composed from raw pointer down/up) and
   raw `pointerEvents`/`EVENT_LISTENERS` bitmask ([§4.4](#44-gestures)).
 - [ ] **Structural reactivity (reactive bodies)** — a signal read in a
   component body (`if`/`switch`/`for`, or the language's equivalent) re-renders
   that component and reconciles it into `TREE` deltas with zero opcodes for
   identical structure; `View.of` is the inline supplier form
   ([§3.4](#34-structural-reactivity-reactive-bodies--slots)).
 - [ ] **Reactive lists** — `ForEach` over a static list or a
   `Signal<List<T>>`, each item a child component slot; static lists MAY use
   native iteration instead ([§3.4](#34-structural-reactivity-reactive-bodies--slots),
   [§9.3.1](#931-cross-language-reactive-vocabulary)).
 - [ ] **Navigation** — `Router` / `RouteTable` / `NavigationContainer` /
   `NavigationLink` over a plain `Signal<Route>`, the initial route host-seeded
   before mount, emitting `ROUTE` and `TRANSITION` and consuming the `NAVIGATE`
   event ([§4.5](#45-navigation)).
 - [ ] **Design tokens & theming** — a token surface: token-typed values usable
   in style modifiers (a `Color` accepting a token path, e.g. `Color.token("color.primary")`
   or the language's equivalent), a theme/override helper emitting
   `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (base values + `dark.`-prefixed dark values), and
   the **base=light / `dark.*`** color-scheme convention with renderer-derived
   scheme detection — see [§7](#7-theme-management) and [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md).
 
 ### 9.2 Mapping rules (signature → protocol)
 
 1. Each view/control maps to its **fixed component id** in PRIMITIVES.md.
    Application/custom component types live in `0x0100`–`0xFFFF`; a DSL must
    never reuse allocated ids.
 2. Each modifier maps to the **documented property id(s)** in MODIFIERS.md
    with the documented **value type** (U8/U32/I32/F32/STRING/ENUM/COLOR/
    DESIGN_TOKEN). Enumerated values use the numeric codes in MODIFIERS.md's
    appendix.
 3. `Color` values pack as sRGB `0xAARRGGBB`. A **token-typed** value instead
    carries the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type with the token path in the arena
    (never a packed literal); the renderer resolves it against the current
    scheme. A theme/override helper emits `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`
    (`A` = arenaRef path, `B` = valueType, `C` = value); a `dark.`-prefixed path
    supplies the dark design (base = light — [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md)).
 4. `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` sentinels: `FILL` = −1.0, `HUG_CONTENT` = −2.0.
 5. `Grid` counts map to the **config values** `GRID_COLUMNS` (`0x001E`) /
    `GRID_ROWS` (`0x001F`): a positive `int` count emits a positive F32; absent =
    auto-fit. A **`List<GridItem>`** value serializes to the **`GRID_TRACKS`**
    (`0x0020`, STRING) per-track spec, which takes precedence over the counts. A
    `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` frame on a grid is the grid's **box**, never a count
    ([§4.2](#42-layout--container-nodes)).
 6. `DatePicker` value/event use the two-field encoding **days since epoch
    (I32) + millis of day (U32)**; there is no `DATE_VALUE` property.
 7. Value/text/date events are gated by the transport-aware event guards; the
    DSL's controls emit the `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`/`EVENT_LISTENERS` that
    declare intent.
 8. Emission is **diff-based and reactive**: the DSL describes values, the
    emitter diffs. A generated DSL must keep the retained tree + emitter
    separation; it must not hand-serialize full trees.
 
 ### 9.3 Language adaptation rules
 
 **The three operations are normative; their spellings are not.** A conformant
 DSL MUST expose *configure values*, *apply modifiers*, and *supply children*,
 each available at creation or by chaining (any order), mapped to the host
 language's idioms. The canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) spelling is
 `Text("x").padding(16)`; Java spells values `make(...)` (views) / lowercase
 functions (modifiers) and chains `modifiers(...)` / `children(...)`.
 
 | Aspect | Java | C# | Rust | Go | Python |
 |--------|------|----|------|----|--------|
 | configure values | `make(c -> …)` (views) / `padding(c -> …)` (modifiers) | `Make(c => …)` | `Type::new(config)` / `with(\|c\| …)` | ctor + options | kwargs / `configure(…)` |
 | single-value shortcut | `make(value)` / `padding(value)` (sugar for the lambda) | `Make(value)` | `Type::new(value)` / `Type(sig)` | `Type(val)` | `Type(val=…)` / `Type(sig)` |
 | apply modifiers | `.modifiers(…)` | `.Modifiers(…)` | `.modifiers(…)` (single or tuple) | `.Modifiers(…)` | `.modifiers(…)` |
 | supply children | `.children(…)` | `.Children(…)` | `.children(vec![…])` / `vstack![…]` | ctor args / `.Children(…)` | `.children(*v)` |
 | creation + chaining | static on the view; chain on the returned builder | static on the view; chain via **extension methods** | associated fn `Type::new`; chain via a **trait** + macros | package ctor; chain via methods | kwargs + methods |
 | same-name static + chain | **builder split** (static on class, chain on builder) | extension methods (separate static class) | assoc fn + trait method | package func + method (not type-scoped) | **not expressible** (methods are last-wins) |
 | `with` name legal | yes | yes (`With`; lowercase `with` is the record keyword) | yes | yes | **no** — `with` is a keyword → kwargs / `configure` |
 | varargs children | yes | `params` | no — slices/arrays or macros | `...` | `*args` |
 | value *is* the modifier | enum OK | **enum can't implement an interface** → `record struct` / static readonly value | enum OK | typed const + method OK | enum member with `apply` OK |
 
 Rules:
 
 - A language that cannot express "static-or-chained under one name" (Python)
   MUST still offer the three operations — value configuration via kwargs /
   `configure(...)`, modifiers and children via chainable methods.
 - A language whose enums cannot implement the modifier interface (C#) MUST
   supply the equivalent single-value modifier form (a `record struct`, a static
   readonly value, or an implicit conversion).
 - **Reactive values are config members, in every language.** A config member
   accepts a raw value or a signal ([§2](#2-canonical-signature-notation)). Rust
   realizes this with `impl Into<Reactive<T>>` on each builder setter
   (`Reactive<T> { Static(T), Signal(SignalId) }`); the former `Bound` /
   `*.bound` modifier surface is folded into it and **removed**.
 - Names are recommendations; semantics
   ([§1](#1-design-principles-dsl-flavored)) are the contract.

# pathland-view-kotlin — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 30, 2026

The idiomatic Kotlin authoring surface (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`). A thin facade over
the Java `pathland-view` DSL, signals, emitter, and wire codec, so Kotlin-authored
trees emit byte-identical opcodes.

## Implemented

- **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text`, `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`, `Rectangle`,
  `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`, `Divider`, `Spacer`,
  `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.
- **Containers**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`,
  `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`,
  `ProxyView`.
- **Controls**: `Button` (title or label subtree), `TextField`, `SecureField`,
  `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`,
  `ColorPicker`.
- **Automatic child collection**: `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no
  `.children(...)`. A custom `KotlinView` constructed inline in a block
  auto-registers; a view stored as a field is added explicitly with `+field`
  inside `body()` (it does not leak into the enclosing scope). An explicit
  `view.add()` / `+view` is available for Java-constructed views (e.g.
  `mediaController.attach()`).
- **Signals**: `signal`, `computed`, `constant`, `effect`, `untracked`,
  `Signal<T>.value`, `WritableSignal<T>.value`, `Signal<T>.map`, `readonly`.
- **Modifier sugar**: `.padding`, `.frame`, `.offset`, `.position`, `.fixedSize`,
  layout priority/z-index/aspect ratio, the full text-formatting surface,
  foreground/background/border/corner radius/shadow, visual effects, transforms,
  visibility/disabled/hit-testing, accessibility, tap/pointer events,
  environment binding, styles, window metadata, and navigation intents. The
  Java `.modifiers(...)` operation remains available as an escape hatch.
- **Persisted state**: `KotlinView` base class + `val count by state(0)`
  (auto-keyed by property name) or `state(0, "key")`; a `mutableState(0)` signal
  form for two-way controls. Bound to the session's `PersistentState` before the
  first `body()` render — no kapt and no annotation processor.
- **Reactive bodies**: plain `if`/`when`/`for` in `body()`; `ForEach` over a static
  list or `Signal<List<T>>` with row-scoped child collection.
- **Navigation**: `navigator { route(...) }`, `NavigationStack`, `NavigationLink`,
  `isActive`, and `.navigate`/`.push`/`.replace` intents.
- **Media**: `Video(controller)`; audio remains view-less (`controller.attach()`
  can be added with `+`).
- **Tests**: byte-identical Kotlin-vs-Java frame comparison, auto-collection,
  modifier property parity, fine-grained signal deltas, persisted/stateful bodies,
  reactive `ForEach`, two-way `TextField`, navigation swaps and link intents.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Reactive **layout value** combinations that need several signals at once are
  available through the Java config builders (`Grid.make { ... }`); the Kotlin
  named-argument overloads cover raw values plus the common single-signal cases.
- A Kotlin-native annotation processor is intentionally not used. `state(...)`
  works on `KotlinView` subclasses; a plain `View` implementation should use
  signals directly or extend `KotlinView`.
- No Kotlin Multiplatform target yet — the module is JVM-only over the Java
  library.
- `SecureField` is implemented in the Kotlin facade (`TEXT_FIELD` + `IS_SECURE`)
  because the Java `TextField.Config` does not yet expose `secure`.

Phase 3 huge; current facade uses Java DSL for all views. Need migrate. Could approach by making Kotlin own **core primitives** incrementally, starting with VStack/HStack/Text/Button/Spacer/Image/Color/ForEach/Group/ScrollView? Then update tests and POM dependency to core; existing Kotlin code still uses Java DSL for others, so cannot drop dependency until all migrated.

We need complete Phase 3 to truly core-only. This is a large project. Could implement Kotlin-owned wrappers for all 50 views. But maybe feasible with a generic NodeView builder and use core `PathlandNode` directly. Kotlin DSL can construct nodes manually without Java view classes. Need replicate property setting logic for each. Lots.

Alternative: Retain Java DSL as **test-scope only** and implement Kotlin views by directly building `PathlandNode` for the tested surface, but not full parity. The plan says full surface parity gate. User expects phase 3. We need decide scope. We could implement core Kotlin primitives and leave advanced views delegating? No, production dependency must core-only.

Maybe Phase 3 can be done by creating a **Kotlin-owned view layer** that still reuses Java DSL? Can't if core-only.

Could we move the Java DSL classes into core? No, phase 1 kept DSL separate.

Maybe best incremental step: Introduce Kotlin-owned infrastructure (`KNodeView`, property helpers) and migrate primitives/containers/controls one file at a time, keeping Java DSL dependency temporarily for remaining views. We can mark progress. The user said "continue with phase 3", not necessarily finish in one turn. We can do a meaningful slice: migrate **primitives and containers** to core-owned Kotlin, while keeping Java dependency for controls/navigation/media until later. But POM still depends Java DSL; not yet core-only. Is that acceptable? It's progress.

We need eventually remove Java DSL dependency. Could do all files in this turn? Let's estimate. Kotlin DSL files 1439 lines, mostly wrappers. Migrating all views manually is large but maybe manageable with a generic builder if we leverage Java DSL class APIs? Wait we can still call **core** `PathlandNode` and set properties. We need know each component/properties. For many controls, we can mimic Java view code. There are ~50 classes. Time-consuming but possible with tools. But tests only cover subset. Full parity requires much.

Alternative architecture: Move the **Java DSL implementation** into Kotlin via typealiases? No.

Could makethe Kotlin module compile against core by **copying** Java DSL view logic into Kotlin for all classes. That's essentially reimplementing. Big.

Maybe there is a smarter approach: Add Kotlin-owned **adapter** that uses `pathland-view` at runtime but not compile-time via reflection? No, violates core-only and bad.

Given constraints, perhaps implement Phase 3 in stages. We should start with core-owned primitives and state, and report remaining. But user might say "continue" expecting completion. We can work through many.

Let's inspect all Kotlin files fully to understand helper patterns and how much.

parts.text:
Full Phase 3 is large. Maybe we can do a **complete migration** by leveraging Kotlin wrapper around Java DSL? That's not core-only. But maybe "Kotlin-owned views over core" can be achieved by moving the **Java DSL implementation** into core? No.

Alternative clever approach: Keep Kotlin DSL code mostly the same, but create Kotlin-owned thin classes that implement `View` using **Java DSL only for config objects?** No.

Could make `pathland-view` an implementation detail bundled inside Kotlin? Not.

We need decide how much to implement. Given user asked continue, we can make a meaningful first increment: migrate `KotlinView`, `Scope`, `Signals` (already core), `Text`, `VStack`, `HStack`, `Spacer`, `Group`, `Button`, and basic modifiers to core. But tests compare Java vs Kotlin; we can keep Java DSL test-scope. POM main dependency can become core, but remaining Kotlin files still import Java DSL -> won't compile. We'd need either keep Java dependency or migrate all imports. So if we want POM core-only, all files must be migrated. That's the gate.

Could we add a **temporary compatibility module** in Kotlin that maps to core but leaves advanced views unimplemented? Tests for advanced views (navigation, media, text field) require. We could keep Java DSL as test dependency and compile main with core only if all advanced files removed or stubbed. Not acceptable.

Maybe we can migrate all in one go by **copying Java DSL classes into Kotlin**. There are ~50 but many simple. The Kotlin DSL files use Java classes for construction and modifiers. We can replace them with Kotlin helper functions that directly build `PathlandNode`, and implement modifiers directly. The biggest work is modifiers: 286-line facade calls Java Modifiers. We'd need implement ~50 property modifiers in Kotlin. But we can create a generic `modifier(property, value)` and wrappers. Many config builders currently use Java classes (`Padding.Config`, `Frame.Config`, etc.). We can keep those config classes? They're in Java DSL, not core. Need core-only, so replace with Kotlin config data classes.

This is a multi-hour task. Maybe doable with AI if systematic, but risky. We have token budget. Could implement a **minimal core-owned Kotlin DSL subset** and adjust status/plan, not complete. But user said continue with phase 3, not finish. An incremental start is fine. We should perhaps implement core-owned **primitives andcontainers**, leave advanced for next. But main dependency still Java DSL. Could create a separate source set `kotlin-core-views`? Hmm.

Maybe start by adding a **Kotlin core view base** and migrate `Text`, `VStack`, `HStack`, `Spacer`, `Group`, `Button` to core, while the module still depends on Java DSL for other views. At least those views are Kotlin-owned. Tests can assert. That's progress but not phase completion. We can report that advanced views still use Java DSL temporarily.

We need maybe ask user? They said continue; better act. Let's implement a meaningful slice without breaking. We'll create `KNode` helper and migrate primitives/containers/button. But we need be careful not to duplicate function names. Existing `Text` functions in Views.kt can be changed to create Kotlin views. `VStack` etc in Containers.kt. We can keep imports for other classes.

Can Kotlin directly create `PathlandNode` and `renderNode`? Yes:
```
class PrimitiveView(private val component: Int, private val setup: (PathlandNode, Environment)->Unit) : View {
 override fun renderNode(env) = PathlandNode(component).also { setup(it,env) }
}
```
But Text needs signal binding:
- `PathlandNode` has `textBinding`? Java `Text` sets `node.textBinding` for signal, or `node.text` for static. Check `PathlandNode` fields.

parts.text:
PathlandNode has `property(int, Signal)` and maybe `text`. Kotlin can use.

We can create a Kotlin helper:
```
internal class NodeView(private val component: Int, private val configure: (PathlandNode, Environment) -> Unit) : View {
 override fun renderNode(env: Environment): PathlandNode = PathlandNode(component).also { configure(it, env) }
}
```
But for `Text` static, set node.text = text; for signal set node.textBinding = signal. For `Button`, need tap action and event listeners property (Commands.Listeners), and button label text? Java Button emits BUTTON node with style content as child; Kotlin Button can mimic without style: create BUTTON node, set text to title if no child, set event listeners pointer down/up, add tap action. But ButtonStyle support? Existing Kotlin `Button(title)` uses Java Button which applies styles. If we migrate Button to core, need handle `ButtonStyle` environment and default `PlainButtonStyle`, which is in Java DSL. Core has `ButtonStyle` interface but no `PlainButtonStyle`. We could implement a Kotlin default style or simply set label text child. For phase 3, we should implement styles in Kotlin. Could keep Java `Button` for now; but then Button isn't Kotlin-owned. Maybe start with Text, VStack, HStack, Spacer, Group only. Those don't need styles. That's a clean first slice.

Migrate:
- `Text` functions (static, Signal)
- `VStack` basic overloads
- `HStack`
- `Spacer`
- `Group`
- maybe `Divider`, `Image`, `Color`, `Rectangle` etc. Simple primitives; can migrate many with helpers.
- `ForEach` needs `View.of`? Core has `View.of` and `ForEach` is Java DSL, but we can implement Kotlin ForEach with `View.of`? `View.of` in core is reactive slot wrapping a supplier; for a Signal<List<T>>, we can use `View.of { buildGroup(items.get()) }`? This re-renders whole subtree, behavior differs from ForEach but tests may pass? Better keep Java ForEach for now.
- `Group` can be Kotlin `NodeView(VSTACK)` with children.
- `VStack`/`HStack` with alignment/spacing signals.
- `Spacer` simple.
- `Text` with text.
- `Button` maybe later.
- `Image` simple component with IMAGE_SOURCE property; signal property. Could do.
- `Color` view; `Rectangle`, `Divider` simple.

Great. Kotlin tests pass.

Now what else can migrate quickly? `Group` and `ForEach`? Group function uses Java `JGroup`; we could implement Kotlin Group but Scope.rowView uses Java Group. We can add internal `groupView` core and update Scope/Views/Containers. But ForEach still Java. Maybe not.

Modifiers are biggest. Maybe we can migrate **simple property modifiers** by writing a Kotlin `CoreModifiers` and switching `Modifiers.kt` calls? Too big. But we can at least migrate `padding`, `frame`? They are heavily used. Yet config classes are Java. Could define Kotlin config data classes and replace functions. But existing Kotlin DSL API types `Padding.Config` etc. are Java DSL. Users import? They usually call lambdas. Changing config types might break source for users who reference. But phase target.

Given this is a start, maybe stop here. But "continue with phase 3" perhaps expect more. We can migrate `Group` and `ForEach` to core using `View.of` and a custom ForEach that mimics Java. ForEach is important.

Implement core `Group`:
```
internal fun groupView(children: List<View>): View = coreView(Components.VSTACK, children)
fun Group(content): View = groupView(collectChildren(content)).registerChild()
```
Update Scope.rowView to use groupView instead of Java Group; update Containers Fit fallback and Views Label fallback to groupView. Could remove JGroup imports. Good.

ForEach core:
- Need replicate Java `ForEachView`: node VSTACK; for Signal list, tracked render reads signal; for static, maps. Children each a `View` (rowView). Use `coreView(Components.VSTACK, children)` but signal list needs read inside render. `coreView` configure runs during render; can do:
```
fun <T> ForEach(items: Signal<List<T>>, content): View = coreView(Components.VSTACK) { node, env -> items.get().forEach { i -> node.children.add(rowView{...}.render(env)) } }
```
But `rowView` calls `collectChildren` which uses scope; okay. For static list, same but no signal read. This component replace Java ForEach. Byte-identical? Java ForEach emits VSTACK group with children. Our coreView VSTACK with children. Same. Reconciliation: Emitter treats coreView as primitive, not tracked slot? `ForEach` Java is a component (renderNode) and when root/child, emitter renders it as a slot? `ForEach` Java `renderNode` reads signal; if it's used as child view, emitter `child.render(env)` creates slot for ForEach view, so signal read tracked. Our coreView object is also a View, `render(env)` creates slot; configure reads signal inside slot; tracked. Good. Byte-identical.
Need use `rowView` from Scope; update Scope rowView to use core group instead of Java Group.
- `rowView` currently returns Java Group for 0/multiple. Replace with `groupView`.
- `Group` function in Views.kt replace.
- `Fit` fallback in Containers uses JGroup; replace with groupView.
- `Label` fallback with Java JGroup only for multiple icon parts; replace with groupView.
- `NavigationLink` custom label fallback uses Java Text/Group; Text Kotlin non-registering? Could use `textView("")` internal and groupView. But NavigationLink still Java class; fine.

Let's implement Group/ForEach.

state.output:
# pathland-view-kotlin — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 1, 2026

The idiomatic Kotlin authoring surface (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`). Phase 3 is
migrating it from a Java DSL facade to Kotlin-owned views over
`pathland-view-core`; the engine, signals, emitter, and wire codec are already
core-owned and Kotlin trees remain byte-identical to the Java DSL.

## Phase 3 progress

- **Core-owned in Kotlin**: `Text`, `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`, shapes, `Divider`,
  `Spacer`, `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Group`,
  `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`, lazy stacks/grids, `ForEach`, `Button`,
  `TextField`/`SecureField`/`TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`,
  `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`, `ColorPicker`, `Video`, `NavigationLink`.
- **Still using the Java DSL**: the modifier vocabulary (`padding`, `frame`,
  fonts, colors, effects, …) and the composite `Label` / `SizeThatFits` /
  `ProxyView` helpers. These are the remaining Phase 3 surface.
- Tests now compare the core-owned controls against the Java DSL byte-for-byte.

## Implemented

- **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text`, `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`, `Rectangle`,
  `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`, `Divider`, `Spacer`,
  `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.
- **Containers**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`,
  `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`,
  `ProxyView`.
- **Controls**: `Button` (title or label subtree), `TextField`, `SecureField`,
  `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`,
  `ColorPicker`.
- **Automatic child collection**: `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no
  `.children(...)`. A custom `KotlinView` constructed inline in a block
  auto-registers; a view stored as a field is added explicitly with `+field`
  inside `body()` (it does not leak into the enclosing scope). An explicit
  `view.add()` / `+view` is available for Java-constructed views (e.g.
  `mediaController.attach()`).
- **Signals**: `signal`, `computed`, `constant`, `effect`, `untracked`,
  `Signal<T>.value`, `WritableSignal<T>.value`, `Signal<T>.map`, `readonly`.
- **Modifier sugar**: `.padding`, `.frame`, `.offset`, `.position`, `.fixedSize`,
  layout priority/z-index/aspect ratio, the full text-formatting surface,
  foreground/background/border/corner radius/shadow, visual effects, transforms,
  visibility/disabled/hit-testing, accessibility, tap/pointer events,
  environment binding, styles, window metadata, and navigation intents. The
  Java `.modifiers(...)` operation remains available as an escape hatch.
- **Persisted state**: `KotlinView` base class + `val count by state(0)`
  (auto-keyed by property name) or `state(0, "key")`; a `mutableState(0)` signal
  form for two-way controls. Bound to the session's `PersistentState` before the
  first `body()` render — no kapt and no annotation processor.
- **Reactive bodies**: plain `if`/`when`/`for` in `body()`; `ForEach` over a static
  list or `Signal<List<T>>` with row-scoped child collection.
- **Navigation**: `navigator { route(...) }`, `NavigationStack`, `NavigationLink`,
  `isActive`, and `.navigate`/`.push`/`.replace` intents.
- **Media**: `Video(controller)`; audio remains view-less (`controller.attach()`
  can be added with `+`).
- **Tests**: byte-identical Kotlin-vs-Java frame comparison, auto-collection,
  modifier property parity, fine-grained signal deltas, persisted/stateful bodies,
  reactive `ForEach`, two-way `TextField`, navigation swaps and link intents.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Reactive **layout value** combinations that need several signals at once are
  available through the Java config builders (`Grid.make { ... }`); the Kotlin
  named-argument overloads cover raw values plus the common single-signal cases.

# pathland-view-kotlin — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 1, 2026

The idiomatic Kotlin authoring surface (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`). Phase 3 is
complete: every production view/modifier is Kotlin-owned over
`pathland-view-core`; the Java DSL is a test-scope parity oracle only.

## Phase 3

- **Core-owned in Kotlin**: all primitives, shapes, stacks, grids, scroll/lazy
  containers, `ForEach`, `Button`, text/value controls, media, navigation,
  `Label`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`, `ProxyView`, and the complete modifier
  vocabulary (padding/frame/fonts/colors/borders/shadows/effects/transforms/
  interaction/accessibility/environment/styles/window metadata).
- **Dependency boundary**: main depends on `pathland-view-core` only; the Java
  DSL is test-scope for byte-for-byte parity comparisons.
- Tests compare the Kotlin-owned views and modifiers against the Java DSL.

## Implemented

- **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text`, `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`, `Rectangle`,
  `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`, `Divider`, `Spacer`,
  `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.
- **Containers**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`,
  `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`,
  `ProxyView`.
- **Controls**: `Button` (title or label subtree), `TextField`, `SecureField`,
  `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`,
  `ColorPicker`.
- **Automatic child collection**: `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no
  `.children(...)`. A custom `KotlinView` constructed inline in a block
  auto-registers; a view stored as a field is added explicitly with `+field`
  inside `body()` (it does not leak into the enclosing scope). An explicit
  `view.add()` / `+view` is available for Java-constructed views (e.g.
  `mediaController.attach()`).
- **Signals**: `signal`, `computed`, `constant`, `effect`, `untracked`,
  `Signal<T>.value`, `WritableSignal<T>.value`, `Signal<T>.map`, `readonly`.
- **Modifier sugar**: `.padding`, `.frame`, `.offset`, `.position`, `.fixedSize`,
  layout priority/z-index/aspect ratio, the full text-formatting surface,
  foreground/background/border/corner radius/shadow, visual effects, transforms,
  visibility/disabled/hit-testing, accessibility, tap/pointer events,
  environment binding, styles, window metadata, and navigation intents. The
  Java `.modifiers(...)` operation remains available as an escape hatch.
- **Persisted state**: `KotlinView` base class + `val count by state(0)`
  (auto-keyed by property name) or `state(0, "key")`; a `mutableState(0)` signal
  form for two-way controls. Bound to the session's `PersistentState` before the
  first `body()` render — no kapt and no annotation processor.
- **Reactive bodies**: plain `if`/`when`/`for` in `body()`; `ForEach` over a static
  list or `Signal<List<T>>` with row-scoped child collection.
- **Navigation**: `navigator { route(...) }`, `NavigationStack`, `NavigationLink`,
  `isActive`, and `.navigate`/`.push`/`.replace` intents.
- **Media**: `Video(controller)`; audio remains view-less (`controller.attach()`
  can be added with `+`).
- **Tests**: byte-identical Kotlin-vs-Java frame comparison, auto-collection,
  modifier property parity, fine-grained signal deltas, persisted/stateful bodies,
  reactive `ForEach`, two-way `TextField`, navigation swaps and link intents.

## Not implemented / gaps

- The Kotlin modifier config types (`Padding`, `Frame`, `Border`, `Shadow`,
  `ClipShape`, `Font`) are Kotlin ownership types; code migrating from the Java
  DSL should use the Kotlin `Modifiers` sugar instead of Java config classes.
- A Kotlin-native annotation processor is intentionally not used. `state(...)`
  works on `KotlinView` subclasses; a plain `View` implementation should use
  signals directly or extend `KotlinView`.
- No Kotlin Multiplatform target yet — the module is JVM-only over
  `pathland-view-core`.
- `SecureField` is Kotlin-owned (`TEXT_FIELD` + `IS_SECURE`).
# pathland-engine-golden — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 1, 2026

Emits shared engine trace fixtures from the canonical Rust engine. Each fixture
is a self-contained PLPL batch (opcodes + string table) stored as hex under
`spec/engine-traces/`.

## Implemented

- `mount_text_stack`: mount a `VStack(spacing: 8)` containing `Text("Hello")`.
- `signal_text_delta`: mount a bound text signal, then change it to `"World"`.
- `property_signal_delta`: mount a bound `SPACING` signal, then change `8 → 12`.
- `styled_text_mount`: styled text with `FONT_SIZE` and `SET_TEXT`, proving the

- `structural_add_remove`: append a text child, then remove it

metadata.output:
# pathland-view-kotlin — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 1, 2026

The idiomatic Kotlin authoring surface (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`). Phase 3 is
complete: every production view/modifier is Kotlin-owned over
`pathland-view-core`; the Java DSL is a test-scope parity oracle only.

## Phase 3

- **Core-owned in Kotlin**: all primitives, shapes, stacks, grids, scroll/lazy
  containers, `ForEach`, `Button`, text/value controls, media, navigation,
  `Label`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`, `ProxyView`, and the complete modifier
  vocabulary (padding/frame/fonts/colors/borders/shadows/effects/transforms/
  interaction/accessibility/environment/styles/window metadata).
- **Dependency boundary**: main depends on `pathland-view-core` only; the Java
  DSL is test-scope for byte-for-byte parity comparisons.
- Tests compare the Kotlin-owned views and modifiers against the Java DSL.

## Implemented

- **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text`, `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`, `Rectangle`,
  `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`, `Divider`, `Spacer`,
  `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.
- **Containers**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`,
  `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`,
  `ProxyView`.
- **Controls**: `Button` (title or label subtree), `TextField`, `SecureField`,
  `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`,
  `ColorPicker`.
- **Automatic child collection**: `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no
  `.children(...)`. A custom `KotlinView` constructed inline in a block
  auto-registers; a view stored as a field is added explicitly with `+field`
  inside `body()` (it does not leak into the enclosing scope). An explicit
  `view.add()` / `+view` is available for Java-constructed views (e.g.
  `mediaController.attach()`).
- **Signals**: `signal`, `computed`, `constant`, `effect`, `untracked`,
  `Signal<T>.value`, `WritableSignal<T>.value`, `Signal<T>.map`, `readonly`.
- **Modifier sugar**: `.padding`, `.frame`, `.offset`, `.position`, `.fixedSize`,
  layout priority/z-index/aspect ratio, the full text-formatting surface,
  foreground/background/border/corner radius/shadow, visual effects, transforms,
  visibility/disabled/hit-testing, accessibility, tap/pointer events,
  environment binding, styles, window metadata, and navigation intents. The
  Java `.modifiers(...)` operation remains available as an escape hatch.
- **Persisted state**: `KotlinView` base class + `val count by state(0)`
  (auto-keyed by property name) or `state(0, "key")`; a `mutableState(0)` signal
  form for two-way controls. Bound to the session's `PersistentState` before the
  first `body()` render — no kapt and no annotation processor.
- **Reactive bodies**: plain `if`/`when`/`for` in `body()`; `ForEach` over a static
  list or `Signal<List<T>>` with row-scoped child collection.
- **Navigation**: `navigator { route(...) }`, `NavigationStack`, `NavigationLink`,
  `isActive`, and `.navigate`/`.push`/`.replace` intents.
- **Media**: `Video(controller)`; audio remains view-less (`controller.attach()`
  can be added with `+`).
- **Tests**: byte-identical Kotlin-vs-Java frame comparison, auto-collection,
  modifier property parity, fine-grained signal deltas, persisted/stateful bodies,
  reactive `ForEach`, two-way `TextField`, navigation swaps and link intents.

## Not implemented / gaps

- The Kotlin modifier config types (`Padding`, `Frame`, `Border`, `Shadow`,
  `ClipShape`, `Font`) are Kotlin ownership types; code migrating from the Java
  DSL should use the Kotlin `Modifiers` sugar instead of Java config classes.
- A Kotlin-native annotation processor is intentionally not used. `state(...)`
  works on `KotlinView` subclasses; a plain `View` implementation should use
  signals directly or extend `KotlinView`.
- No Kotlin Multiplatform target yet — the module is JVM-only over
  `pathland-view-core`.
- `SecureField` is Kotlin-owned (`TEXT_FIELD` + `IS_SECURE`).
# pathland-engine-golden — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 1, 2026

Emits shared engine trace fixtures from the canonical Rust engine. Each fixture
is a self-contained PLPL batch (opcodes + string table) stored as hex under
`spec/engine-traces/`.

## Implemented

- `mount_text_stack`: mount a `VStack(spacing: 8)` containing `Text("Hello")`.
- `signal_text_delta`: mount a bound text signal, then change it to `"World"`.
- `property_signal_delta`: mount a bound `SPACING` signal, then change `8 → 12`.
- `styled_text_mount`: styled text with `FONT_SIZE` and `SET_TEXT`, proving the
  canonical property-before-text order.
- `structural_add_remove`: append a text child, then remove it
  (`REMOVE_CHILD` + `DELETE_NODE`).
- `--emit` regenerates the committed fixtures.
- `--check` compares the committed fixtures with current engine output.
- CI runs `--check` (via regeneration + `git diff --exit-code`).

The Java engine test (`EngineTraceTest`) builds the same scenarios through the
Java DSL and compares its encoded frames byte-for-byte.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Scenario construction is still duplicated between this Rust generator and the
  JVM test; a neutral scenario DSL is future work.
- Only mount + simple signal deltas are covered. Structural deltas, zero-op
  recompute, tokens/lists, fit, media, navigation, and window metadata are next.

parts.text:
User wants "see this working end to end with a demo". We need propose plan for a new demo using Kotlin DSL. Need choose desktop vs web vs both. Given existing demos, easiest **Kotlin desktop demo** using existing GTK/Qt host infrastructure. But user may prefer browser. Need ask. We can recommend one.

We should inspect available demo views and whether we can author a simple Kotlin demo. Could create a new module `pathland-kotlin-demo` (desktop) that uses Kotlin DSL -> core engine -> GTK/Qt. Or maybe add `KotlinDemoView` to existing demo and run web. Let's reason.

End-to-end goals:
- Author UI in Kotlin DSL.
- Emit via core engine.
- Render in native or browser.
- Demonstrate interactivity (counter, text field, navigation, maybe media).

Options:
A. **Kotlin GTK desktop demo**:
  - New `lib/java/pathland-kotlin-gtk-demo` module (or extend `pathland-gtk-demo` with Kotlin source and main class).
  - Kotlin views in `src/main/kotlin`, depends `pathland-view-kotlin`, `pathland-view-core`, `pathland-demo-views` maybe for assets/theme, JNA.
  - Host code can be reused from `GtkHost`, but it currently uses Java `MusicPlayerView`. We can write a Kotlin `KotlinGtkHost` that mounts a Kotlin-authored view (counter + navigation + text field + maybe media). Reuse `PathlandCore`, `RingOpcodeSink`, `InputDispatcher`, `RingEventReader`, `GtkRendererNative`, `DemoTheme`.
  - Run with `scripts/run-kotlin-gtk-demo.sh`.
  - Pros: truly end-to-end native, zero-copy, no browser/server; demonstrates Kotlin DSL, signals, controls, engine, GTK renderer. Existing infra. Cons: macOS GTK install/main thread; requires Rust dylibs; native UI maybe limited; can't see on CI.
B. **Kotlin Spring/Quarkus web demo**:
  - Add Kotlin view + `PathlandApp` to existing Spring Boot demo or new module.
  - Browser SSR + WebSocket DOM renderer; easiest to see/demo, cross-platform. Need add `pathland-view-kotlin` dep to demo, write Kotlin root view, maybe new endpoint/app. The starter already handles SSR/WS. Could add a `/kotlin` mounted app or replace MusicPlayerView at `/` with Kotlin-authored view. Better new `pathland-kotlin-web-demo` module? Or add `KotlinDemoView` to existing spring demo.
  - Pros: browser, interactive, easy to share; no GTK/Qt native deps; showcases SSR + hydration + WebSocket deltas. Cons: server runtime uses Java DSL? It only needs core `View`; Kotlin works. Starters currently tests; add Kotlin dep.
C. **Kotlin Qt demo**: similar to A, Qt Quick; maybe better visuals. Existing Qt host. Requires Qt6 libs.
D. **Two demos**: Kotlin GTK desktop + Kotlin web. More work.

User says "see this working end to end with a demo" likely wants a visual demo. We can recommend **Kotlin Spring Boot web demo** because easiest to run and see, and covers full stack (Kotlin DSL → core engine → HTML SSR/WebSocket → DOM renderer). But the architecture's desktop zero-copy ring is also compelling. Which to pick? Maybe both? We should present tradeoffs and ask.

Need inspect existing `MusicPlayerView` for features and whether easy to re-author in Kotlin. Could create a smaller demo to avoid huge port: Kotlin "Counter + Navigation + Text field" app. But to demonstrate end-to-end and parity, a small app is enough. Could use the existing shared `MusicPlayerView`? It's Java DSL, not Kotlin. We need Kotlin-authored. Maybe build a Kotlin version of a simple "Counter" or "SplitNav" using Kotlin DSL. The Kotlin module tests show counter/state/navigation. A demo view could be:
- VStack with title, counter button, text field, slider/toggle, navigation stack with two pages.
- Use `KotlinView` state/persisted signals, `Button`, `TextField`, `Toggle`, `ForEach`.
This demonstrates most features.
- For web SSR, `KotlinView` uses `Environment.state()` and `PersistentState`; starter session works. Good.

Need decide where to place demo. A new module `lib/java/pathland-kotlin-demo` with Spring Boot? Could reuse starter. Maybe simpler to add a Kotlin root view class to existing `pathland-spring-boot-demo` and change `SpringDemoApplication` to use it? But existing demo is MusicPlayerView and tests. Could add a second mounted app at `/kotlin` using Kotlin view. That demonstrates side by side with existing. Need add Kotlin source to existing `pathland-spring-boot-demo` (Maven Kotlin plugin) and dependency on `pathland-view-kotlin`. Or create a new module `pathland-kotlin-spring-demo` to avoid mixing. New module overhead but clean.
- Spring Boot starter's `PathlandApp` is Java interface; Kotlin can implement.
- Need assets? If simple controls no media, no assets. DOM renderer bundle served by starter. Good.
- Run script `scripts/run-kotlin-demo.sh`.
- Demo URL `http://localhost:8080/` with Kotlin UI; or `/kotlin` mounted.

Could reuse existing `pathland-spring-boot-demo` infrastructure; add `KotlinCounterView.kt` and a `MountedApp` at `/kotlin`? But Java and Kotlin compilation config; add `kotlin-maven-plugin` and source dir. Maybe okay. New module `pathland-kotlin-demo` with Spring Boot starter dependency and own `application.properties` and main class in Kotlin:
```
@SpringBootApplication
class KotlinDemoApplication
fun main(args) { runApplication<KotlinDemoApplication>(*args) }
@Bean fun pathlandApp(): PathlandApp = object : PathlandApp { override fun newRoot() = KotlinDemoView() }
```
Need Spring Boot plugin for fat jar. Could copy POM from spring demo. Add module to parent. This is clean but 2-3 files.
- Also add static demos? Starter serves DOM bundle from its resources? The starter's `PathlandIndexController` serves bundle; okay.
- Need ensure `pathland-view-kotlin` is on classpath.
- Run `mvn -pl pathland-kotlin-demo spring-boot:run` or package jar.
- For SSR, `KotlinDemoView` `KotlinView` state uses core `PersistentState`; server session sets env. Good.
- The Kotlin DSL's `KotlinView` auto-registration might be tricky under server render; tests cover. Fine.
- Demo view should show:
  - `@State` persisted counter (using `by state`).
  - TextField bound to `mutableState`.
  - Toggle.
  - Navigation link/route perhaps.
  - Maybe `ForEach` list with add/remove.
  - Theme? Could use `windowMetadata` and `.buttonStyle` etc. But Kotlin `ButtonStyle`? We have core style; can use `BorderedButtonStyle` from Java DSL? Not production dep. Kotlin doesn't have built-in styles; can implement a Kotlin style or use modifiers directly. For demo, use modifiers (padding/background/border) and Button.
  - Navigation: `navigator`/`NavigationStack`, NavigationLink. This demonstrates router.
  - Maybe `ViewThatFits`. Good.

Need also maybe a **desktop demo** to show zero-copy? The web demo covers end-to-end but not native zero-copy. User said "see this working end to end"; web is enough. But maybe they want to see Kotlin UI visually. Browser is easiest.

Potential plan:
1. Add `pathland-kotlin-demo` Spring Boot module with Kotlin DSL root view.
2. Add `scripts/run-kotlin-demo.sh` that builds Rust HTML renderer cdylib? The Java Spring starter's render-html jar embeds Rust dylib. Existing `run-spring-demo.sh` builds? inspect script.

A demo is the right next step. The fastest end-to-end proof is a **Kotlin-authored Spring Boot demo**: browser UI, SSR, hydration, and live WebSocket deltas, with no GTK/Qt setup.

## Recommended: Kotlin Spring Boot web demo

New module: `lib/java/pathland-kotlin-demo`

### Demo app

A single Kotlin-authored view showing:

- persisted counter with `by state(0)`
- bound `TextField`
- `Toggle` + `Slider`
- reactive `ForEach` list with add/remove
- `NavigationStack` / `NavigationLink` between two pages
- `ViewThatFits` or responsive stack layout
- Kotlin modifiers: padding, frame, background, border, fonts
- `windowMetadata` title/description
- a small custom `KotlinView` component

This exercises Kotlin DSL → core engine → SSR HTML → DOM hydration → WebSocket delta routing.

### Implementation steps

1. Add `lib/java/pathland-kotlin-demo` to the parent reactor.
2. POM:
   - `pathland-view-kotlin`
   - `pathland-spring-boot-starter`
   - Kotlin Maven plugin
   - Spring Boot repackage plugin
   - demo skip flags
3. Add `KotlinDemoApplication.kt`:
   - `@SpringBootApplication`
   - `PathlandApp` bean returning the Kotlin root view.
4. Add `KotlinDemoView.kt` and small subviews.
5. Add `scripts/run-kotlin-demo.sh`:
   - build Rust HTML renderer
   - build/install Java modules
   - package and run the demo
6. Add a smoke test that mounts the demo view through the core emitter and checks expected text/opcodes.
7. Update `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and the Kotlin/demo status files.

### Run target

```bash
./scripts/run-kotlin-demo.sh
# http://localhost:8080
```

Expected: SSR first paint, then the counter/text/list/navigation interactions update through `/ws` deltas.

## Alternative: Kotlin desktop demo

A Kotlin GTK/Qt host using the same view, `RingOpcodeSink`, and native renderer would also demonstrate zero-copy. It requires GTK/Qt native libraries and macOS main-thread handling, so it is slower to run and less portable.

## Recommendation

Do the **web demo first**. Then, if you want the native zero-copy story too, reuse the same Kotlin view in a small GTK or Qt host.

    <properties>
        <maven.deploy.skip>true</maven.deploy.skip>
        <maven.javadoc.skip>true</maven.javadoc.skip>
    </properties>

    <name>Pathland Quarkus Demo</name>
    <description>
        Quarkus demonstration app consuming the Pathland libraries: SSR
        (pathland-render-html) for instant first paint, then live 16-byte opcode deltas +
        events over WebSocket, with cross-platform state persisted through StateStore
        (Redis with an in-memory fallback). The entire app is the starter dependency + a
        PathlandApp bean returning the root view.
    </description>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-quarkus-starter</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-demo-views</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <!-- Observability (issue #62): a Prometheus scrape endpoint at /q/metrics; health
             at /q/health comes from the starter. OpenTelemetry spans are OPT-IN — add
             io.quarkus:quarkus-opentelemetry to enable them (see the application.properties
             note); the starter wires the tracing decorator when the extension is present. -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-micrometer-registry-prometheus</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-logging-json</artifactId>
        </dependency>

            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-junit5</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

                    <execution>

                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>

# --- Same-server proxy demo (spec/PROXY.md) ------------------------------------
# The music player at / embeds the small ad app mounted at /ad (this same server)
# as a sponsored slot in its Now Playing pane, via a ProxyView. This is the origin
# app's base URL the player proxies; point it at another host/port to proxy a
# remote app instead.
pathland.demo.ad-url=http://localhost:8080/ad

# --- Per-window id on the first request (issue #155) ---------------------------
# Opt the DOM client into the service worker that attaches the per-window id to
# top-level navigations, so the SSR renders the right persisted-state scope on the
# FIRST paint (instead of defaults that the live connection then corrects). The id
# never appears in the URL. Off by default; the worker is served at /_pathland/sw.js
# with Service-Worker-Allowed: / (root scope) and no-cache.
pathland.service-worker=true

# Static resources (the demo's media/icons are served from a disk extraction via
# DemoAssetsRoute, which also sends its own caching headers; this covers the rest
# of Quarkus's static resources, e.g. the DOM client bundle).
quarkus.http.static-resources.max-age=168h

# Pathland SSR debug comments: when true, every rendered HTML node is prefixed
# with a comment naming its component type and the modifiers applied, e.g.
#   <!-- #1 VStack: spacing=4, alignment=Fill -->
# Debugging aid — opt-in; the live /ws deltas are unaffected.
# pathland.debug-html=true

# --- Observability (issue #62) -------------------------------------------------
# Structured (JSON) console logging — the production-shaped reference app default.
quarkus.log.console.json.enabled=true
# Metrics: Micrometer counters/timers at pathland.* are exposed at /q/metrics
# (Prometheus); health at /q/health (smallrye-health). See pathland-observability.
#
# OpenTelemetry spans per frame send / event batch are OPT-IN. The starter wires the
# tracing decorator automatically when a Tracer is available, so to enable them just
# add the extension and point it at a collector:
#   <dependency>io.quarkus:quarkus-opentelemetry</dependency>
#   quarkus.otel.exporter.otlp.traces.endpoint=http://localhost:4317
# (the extension is intentionally NOT a dependency here, so local dev is quiet).
# Test-server config for the same-server proxy demo (spec/PROXY.md).
#
# Quarkus's @QuarkusTest HTTP port is pinned so the player's sponsored proxy
# origin (the /ad app mounted on this same server) resolves deterministically.
quarkus.http.test-port=8081
pathland.demo.ad-url=http://localhost:8081/ad

# pathland-quarkus-starter — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 28, 2026

Quarkus integration for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each app's reserved
`/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding the starter dependency + a `PathlandApp` CDI
bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at their own subpaths
(the BFF layout).

## Implemented

- **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt.

- **`PathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/_pathland/ws")` for the root app: 1:1 sessions
  per connection (a fresh `uiId` per connection + the client's `wid` state scope from
  the `?wid=` query param), binary events routed into the root registry of the
  `PathlandHost`. **Stateless (critical)**: quarkus-websockets-next endpoints default
  to `@Singleton` — one shared instance for all connections — so the per-connection
  ids come from `connection.id()` + the handshake and the `QuarkusConnection` adapters
  live in a map keyed by connection id. Memoizing `uiId`/`wid`/`transport` on the
  shared instance collapsed every connection onto ONE session (multiple browsers shared
  one UI model — a probe or second tab drove the first tab's session).
- **`MountedPathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/{app}/_pathland/ws")` for mounted apps:
  the `{app}` path param resolves the app's registry. Mount paths are single-segment.
  Same stateless rule as the root socket.
- **`IndexResource`** — JAX-RS SSR catch-all (`/` + deep links; `/_pathland/**` and the
  Quarkus non-application root `/q/**` — health/metrics — excluded via negative lookahead)
  dispatching to the longest-mount app (prefix stripped);
  SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS);
  per-app framework files (`/{app}/_pathland/...`, e.g. the mounted app's bundle) are
  served from the shared `/_pathland/**` classpath mount. Quarkus serves the global
  `/_pathland/**` bundle + asset mount from `META-INF/resources` before JAX-RS.
  **`/_pathland/{name}.css`** (global JAX-RS route + the mounted-base
  `frameworkFile` path) serves the renderer-owned content-hashed base design
  (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with
  `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. **`/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg`**
  serves the renderer-owned icon glyphs from the shared Rust renderer
  (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` → `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache
  header — no static CSS/icon files on any host. SSR links the CSS via
  `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`.
- **`PathlandRegistryProducer`** — CDI `@Produces @Singleton` `PathlandHost` from every
  `MountedApp` bean plus the lone `PathlandApp` bean (mounted at `/`); `@Disposes` shuts
  it down. Reads the `pathland.debug-html` config property (default `false`) to enable
  per-node HTML comments in SSR output, and `pathland.service-worker` (default `false`)
  to opt the DOM client into the per-window-id service worker (issue #155) — served at
  `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
- **`ServiceWorkerFilter`** — serves `/_pathland/sw.js` (root and mounted bases) with
  `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so the client's root-scoped
  registration succeeds. A `Filters` handler always runs before routes, so it wins over
  Quarkus's static-resource handler (which sends neither header, and whose configured
  max-age would otherwise cache the script and delay update detection).
- **Observability (issue #62)** — `quarkus-micrometer` (a `MeterRegistry` bean) +
  `quarkus-smallrye-health`: the producer builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over the
  registry and decorates it with `TracingTelemetry` when a `Tracer` bean is present and
  `quarkus.otel.enabled` (default `true`; the starter never touches the OTel API when
  the extension is absent/disabled). `PathlandHealthCheck` (`@Readiness`) reports the
  host UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/q/health`; the `pathland.*` meters appear
  at `/q/metrics`.
- **`QuarkusConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketConnection` to `PathlandConnection`.
  Sends are **serialized** (one `sendBinary` subscription in flight, the rest queued),
  and a **send failure closes the connection** so the session drops it and the DOM
  client reconnects + `META::RESYNC` (recoverable) instead of silently stalling on an
  "open" socket that never delivers (the remote seekbar symptom). **Send timeout**: a
  `sendBinary` that neither completes nor fails within 10 s (a half-dead connection /
  a dropped proxy upstream leg) is marked failed and closed — a hung send would
  otherwise wedge the serialized drain forever. **Keep-alive pings**: the connection
  sends a WS-protocol ping every 15 s (browsers auto-pong) to keep the connection warm
  through middleboxes and detect a dead client; `close()` stops the keep-alive
  scheduler (the sockets' `@OnClose` calls it).
- **Heartbeat** — both sockets reply to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG`
  **at the transport layer** (through their `QuarkusConnection`, no actor/session
  dependency, and a PING never creates or wakes a session); spec/OPCODE.md
  §Transport heartbeat.
- **Failure handling** — `fail()` logs the reason; `close()` (socket `@OnClose`)
  no longer calls `close()` on the already-closed connection (no spurious
  "Connection already closed" noise). A **transient write failure on a connection
  that still reports open is logged, not closed** — only a confirmed-dead channel
  (or a send hung past the timeout) warrants closing. The send-timeout task is
  **cancelled when the send completes**, so a completed-but-late callback can't
  false-time-out and kill a healthy connection. Keep-alive pings are sent directly
  (Vert.x serializes writes — no sync with `sendBinary` needed).
- `META-INF/beans.xml` so Quarkus discovers the starter.

## App DX

```java
@ApplicationScoped
public class MyApp {
    @Produces @Singleton PathlandApp main() { return () -> new MyHomeView(); }
    @Produces @Singleton MountedApp support() { return MountedApp.of("/support", ...); }
}
```

## Verified by

Manual: the `pathland-quarkus-demo` renders `/` (the music player, whose Now
Playing pane embeds the small `/ad` app via a **same-server `ProxyView`**,
spec/PROXY.md) and `/ad` (the ad app); a WebSocket handshake to `/_pathland/ws`
and `/ad/_pathland/ws` returns 101. `ProxyDemoTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts
`GET /` embeds the `/ad` app's subtree with remapped node ids
(`data-pathland-id="1073741825"` — proxy block 0 + origin id 1). Core behavior is
covered by `pathland-server-core` tests. `MultiSessionWebSocketTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) opens **100 concurrent real WS
sessions** against `/_pathland/ws` (via the shared `pathland-server-core` test-jar
probe) and asserts each connects, re-syncs, gets transport-level PONGs, stays isolated,
and is never closed by the peer.
`PathlandObservabilityTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts `/q/health` reports the Pathland
check UP and `/q/metrics` exposes the `pathland.*` namespace. `BaseCssTest`
(`@QuarkusTest`) asserts the linked SSR `<link>`, the immutable `text/css`
response at the global and mounted bases, and a 404 for an unknown hash.171:  pathland-quarkus-starter/ # com.pathland.quarkus — Quarkus CDI integration: add the dep +
178:  pathland-quarkus-demo/# Quarkus SSR + WebSocket demo (com.pathland.demo.quarkus)
191:  `cd lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo && mvn quarkus:dev` (or `mvn package && java -jar target/quarkus-app/quarkus-run.jar`).
675:**Complete**: 16-byte opcode engine (`pathland-core`), SwiftUI-style view DSL with decoupled chainable modifiers (`pathland-view`), declarative diff-based reactive emission (`pathland-core`), **reactive signals** (`pathland-core::signal` — writable `Signal` values bound to node text/properties, so a signal change re-emits only the bound nodes, reachable from Java via the `pathland_native_signal_*` / `node_bind_*` C ABI), host reader to a native-element description (`pathland-render-gtk`), opcode transport with network-batch encode/decode + time/size batching policy (`pathland-core-transport`), golden conformance vectors (incl. raw-input EVENT and network-batch bytes), typed raw-input event encode/decode, `no_std` builds, zero-alloc steady-state emission, the **bidirectional event ring** (host → guest EVENT opcodes in shared memory, drained by the host via a generic `pathland_native_drain_events` C ABI — the renderer only writes + wakes), the **GTK4 # pathland-quarkus-starter — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 28, 2026

Quarkus integration for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each app's reserved
`/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding the starter dependency + a `PathlandApp` CDI
bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at their own subpaths
(the BFF layout).

## Implemented

- **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt.

- **`PathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/_pathland/ws")` for the root app: 1:1 sessions
  per connection (a fresh `uiId` per connection + the client's `wid` state scope from
  the `?wid=` query param), binary events routed into the root registry of the
  `PathlandHost`. **Stateless (critical)**: quarkus-websockets-next endpoints default
  to `@Singleton` — one shared instance for all connections — so the per-connection
  ids come from `connection.id()` + the handshake and the `QuarkusConnection` adapters
  live in a map keyed by connection id. Memoizing `uiId`/`wid`/`transport` on the
  shared instance collapsed every connection onto ONE session (multiple browsers shared
  one UI model — a probe or second tab drove the first tab's session).
- **`MountedPathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/{app}/_pathland/ws")` for mounted apps:
  the `{app}` path param resolves the app's registry. Mount paths are single-segment.
  Same stateless rule as the root socket.
- **`IndexResource`** — JAX-RS SSR catch-all (`/` + deep links; `/_pathland/**` and the
  Quarkus non-application root `/q/**` — health/metrics — excluded via negative lookahead)
  dispatching to the longest-mount app (prefix stripped);
  SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS);
  per-app framework files (`/{app}/_pathland/...`, e.g. the mounted app's bundle) are
  served from the shared `/_pathland/**` classpath mount. Quarkus serves the global
  `/_pathland/**` bundle + asset mount from `META-INF/resources` before JAX-RS.
  **`/_pathland/{name}.css`** (global JAX-RS route + the mounted-base
  `frameworkFile` path) serves the renderer-owned content-hashed base design
  (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with
  `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. **`/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg`**
  serves the renderer-owned icon glyphs from the shared Rust renderer
  (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` → `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache
  header — no static CSS/icon files on any host. SSR links the CSS via
  `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`.
- **`PathlandRegistryProducer`** — CDI `@Produces @Singleton` `PathlandHost` from every
  `MountedApp` bean plus the lone `PathlandApp` bean (mounted at `/`); `@Disposes` shuts
  it down. Reads the `pathland.debug-html` config property (default `false`) to enable
  per-node HTML comments in SSR output, and `pathland.service-worker` (default `false`)
  to opt the DOM client into the per-window-id service worker (issue #155) — served at
  `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
- **`ServiceWorkerFilter`** — serves `/_pathland/sw.js` (root and mounted bases) with
  `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so the client's root-scoped
  registration succeeds. A `Filters` handler always runs before routes, so it wins over
  Quarkus's static-resource handler (which sends neither header, and whose configured
  max-age would otherwise cache the script and delay update detection).
- **Observability (issue #62)** — `quarkus-micrometer` (a `MeterRegistry` bean) +
  `quarkus-smallrye-health`: the producer builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over the
  registry and decorates it with `TracingTelemetry` when a `Tracer` bean is present and
  `quarkus.otel.enabled` (default `true`; the starter never touches the OTel API when
  the extension is absent/disabled). `PathlandHealthCheck` (`@Readiness`) reports the
  host UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/q/health`; the `pathland.*` meters appear
  at `/q/metrics`.
- **`QuarkusConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketConnection` to `PathlandConnection`.
  Sends are **serialized** (one `sendBinary` subscription in flight, the rest queued),
  and a **send failure closes the connection** so the session drops it and the DOM
  client reconnects + `META::RESYNC` (recoverable) instead of silently stalling on an
  "open" socket that never delivers (the remote seekbar symptom). **Send timeout**: a
  `sendBinary` that neither completes nor fails within 10 s (a half-dead connection /
  a dropped proxy upstream leg) is marked failed and closed — a hung send would
  otherwise wedge the serialized drain forever. **Keep-alive pings**: the connection
  sends a WS-protocol ping every 15 s (browsers auto-pong) to keep the connection warm
  through middleboxes and detect a dead client; `close()` stops the keep-alive
  scheduler (the sockets' `@OnClose` calls it).
- **Heartbeat** — both sockets reply to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG`
  **at the transport layer** (through their `QuarkusConnection`, no actor/session
  dependency, and a PING never creates or wakes a session); spec/OPCODE.md
  §Transport heartbeat.
- **Failure handling** — `fail()` logs the reason; `close()` (socket `@OnClose`)
  no longer calls `close()` on the already-closed connection (no spurious
  "Connection already closed" noise). A **transient write failure on a connection
  that still reports open is logged, not closed** — only a confirmed-dead channel
  (or a send hung past the timeout) warrants closing. The send-timeout task is
  **cancelled when the send completes**, so a completed-but-late callback can't
  false-time-out and kill a healthy connection. Keep-alive pings are sent directly
  (Vert.x serializes writes — no sync with `sendBinary` needed).
- `META-INF/beans.xml` so Quarkus discovers the starter.

## App DX

```java
@ApplicationScoped
public class MyApp {
    @Produces @Singleton PathlandApp main() { return () -> new MyHomeView(); }
    @Produces @Singleton MountedApp support() { return MountedApp.of("/support", ...); }
}
```
