name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, 'docs/**', 'feature/**', 'fix/**', 'refactor/**', 'spec/**']
  pull_request:

jobs:
  design:
    name: Design (Style Dictionary)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: design/package-lock.json

      # Build the generated token CSS / manifest / bundle and validate the
      # three token layers against the protocol catalog, dark/forced-dark
      # rules, and the canonical length conventions.
      - name: Install, build, check
        working-directory: design
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run build
          npm run check

      # The Rust renderer embeds the generated bundle (committed for packaging).
      - name: Verify the committed renderer CSS matches the design build
        run: scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check

  rust:
    name: Rust (workspace + C ABI + no_std/wasm)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [design]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # The workspace includes pathland-render-gtk (GTK4 + libadwaita + GStreamer)
      # and pathland-render-qt (Qt Quick), so the runner needs the GTK4,
      # libadwaita, GStreamer, and Qt system libraries before `cargo test` can
      # link them. GStreamer is required because the GTK renderer plays app-driven
      # media through a direct GStreamer playbin (GTK4's own media backend is
      # compiled out of some builds); the plugins are the runtime set the audio
      # stack uses (playbin, volume/audioconvert, mp3 decode). The Qt libraries
      # are installed in the next step.
      - name: Install GTK4 + libadwaita + GStreamer system dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libgtk-4-dev \
            libadwaita-1-dev \
            libglib2.0-dev \
            libcairo2-dev \
            libpango1.0-dev \
            libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-dev \
            libgraphene-1.0-dev \
            libgstreamer1.0-dev \
            gstreamer1.0-plugins-base \
            gstreamer1.0-plugins-good \
            gstreamer1.0-libav

      - name: Install Qt6 (QML/Quick) system dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            qt6-base-dev \
            qt6-declarative-dev \
            qt6-declarative-private-dev \
            qt6-multimedia-dev \
            qml6-module-qtqml \
            qml6-module-qtqml-models \
            qml6-module-qtqml-workerscript \
            qml6-module-qtquick \
            qml6-module-qtquick-layouts \
            qml6-module-qtquick-controls \
            qml6-module-qtquick-templates \
            qml6-module-qtquick-window \
            qml6-module-qtmultimedia
        # The dev headers alone don't ship the QML runtime modules; the Qt
        # renderer's offscreen tests instantiate the QML (QtQml + WorkerScript,
        # Items, stacks/Grid via QtQuick.Layouts, Qt Quick Controls, Multimedia)
        # through QQmlComponent, so the qml6-module-* runtime files are required
        # too. Note the Qt6 package names: `-window` (the Qt5 `-window2` name
        # does not exist), and private headers need qt6-declarative-private-dev.

      - name: Install Rust (stable + wasm32 target)
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown

      - name: Cache cargo
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: lib/rust -> target

      - name: Test workspace
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo test

      - name: Qt renderer headless smoke
        working-directory: lib/rust
        env:
          QT_QPA_PLATFORM: offscreen
          QT_QUICK_BACKEND: software
        run: cargo test -p pathland-render-qt

      # The DOM renderer's constants/token conventions and the cross-renderer SSR
      # golden fixtures are GENERATED from Rust (pathland-ts-codegen /
      # pathland-html-golden). Regenerate them here and fail if the committed
      # files drifted — so a renumbered constant or a changed SSR shape can't land
      # without its TS/fixture counterparts.
      - name: Verify generated TS + golden fixtures are current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen
          cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit
          git diff --exit-code -- \
            lib/typescript/src/constants.ts \
            lib/typescript/src/generated \
            lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr

      # The neutral protocol manifest is the machine-readable mirror consumed by
      # non-Rust bindings. Regenerate it from the canonical Rust constants and fail
      # if the committed `spec/protocol.tsv` drifted. The Java job validates its
      # hand-written constants against this file.
      - name: Verify the protocol manifest is current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          cargo run -p pathland-protocol-manifest
          git -C ../.. diff --exit-code -- spec/protocol.tsv

      # The shared engine traces are emitted by the canonical Rust engine and
      # compared byte-for-byte by the JVM engine test. Verify the committed
      # fixtures have not drifted from the current engine behavior.
      - name: Verify engine trace fixtures are current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --check

      - name: Build the C ABI (cdylib, used by the Java JNA ring interop / native hosts)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-core-capi

      - name: no_std / wasm32 direction guard
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: ./check-wasm.sh

      # The Java HTML renderer shim needs the Rust renderer cdylib (the jar embeds
      # it so it travels with the artifact). Build it here and hand it to the java
      # job via an artifact.
      - name: Build the HTML renderer cdylib
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-render-html

      - name: Upload the renderer dylib for the java job
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pathland-render-html-native
          path: lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_html.so
          retention-days: 1

  java:
    name: Java (Maven reactor, JDK ${{ matrix.java }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [rust]
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        java: ['17', '21', '25']
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Whole-stack floor is Java 17 (maven.compiler.release=17; JNA native binding,
      # thread-local environment); the matrix proves every LTS from 17.
      - name: Set up JDK ${{ matrix.java }}
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: ${{ matrix.java }}
          cache: maven

      # The renderer jar embeds the Rust cdylib (built by the rust job). Restore it
      # into the debug dir the jar-embed step copies.
      - name: Download the Rust renderer dylib
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pathland-render-html-native
          path: lib/rust/target/debug

      - name: Test reactor (incl. the SSR web demos)
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: mvn -q -B test

  web-client:
    name: Web client (TypeScript DOM renderer)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: lib/typescript/package-lock.json

      - name: Install, typecheck, test, build
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run typecheck
          npm test
          npm run build

      # The demos serve the committed bundle from their static resource dirs
      # (content-hashed dom-renderer-<sha256>.js + the dom-renderer.current
      # pointer; stale hashed copies are pruned); copying the freshly built one
      # must not change the working tree.
      - name: Verify the committed bundle matches the source (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: |
          npm run copy-to-demos
          git diff --exit-code -- lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/src/main/resources lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-demo/src/main/resources

      # Real-browser guard for the per-window-id service worker: the browser-variance
      # bugs (WebKit reports an empty clientId on navigations; relative cache keys are
      # rejected) only appear in a real worker engine, never in jsdom/happy-dom.
      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit

      - name: Service worker E2E (Chromium + WebKit)
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: npm run test:e2ename: Release

# Publishing a GitHub Release (which creates the tag, e.g. `v0.1.1`) builds and
# publishes every artifact — the Rust crates to crates.io and the Java libraries
# to Maven Central (with the renderer's native libraries for every supported
# platform) — then attaches the built files to the Release.
#
# The tag drives the version: the workflow writes the tag's `X.Y.Z` into the Rust
# workspace version and the Java parent version (in CI only) before building, and
# a `bump` job commits that version back to `main` afterwards. No pre-bump commit
# is required. Tags must be `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` (an optional pre-release
# suffix is allowed).
#
# The publish steps are idempotent, so re-running a partially failed release is
# safe (a crate+version already on crates.io is skipped; Maven Central rejects a
# re-deploy of an existing version).
#
# Secrets:
#   CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN  crates.io API token (publish scope)
#   GPG_PRIVATE_KEY       armored GPG private key (signing)
#   GPG_PASSPHRASE        its passphrase
#   CENTRAL_USERNAME      Sonatype Central Portal user token username
#   CENTRAL_PASSWORD      Sonatype Central Portal user token password

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: 'Tag to release (e.g. v0.1.1); blank = current ref'
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  version:
    name: Resolve + validate version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      tag: ${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
      version: ${{ steps.v.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - id: v
        name: Derive the version from the tag
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          tag="${{ github.event.release.tag_name || inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}"
          if [[ ! "$tag" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::tag '$tag' must be v<major>.<minor>.<patch>"
            exit 1
          fi
          version="${tag#v}"
          echo "tag=$tag version=$version"
          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  rust:
    name: Publish crates to crates.io
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: version
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Set the version from the tag
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cargo install cargo-edit --locked
          cargo set-version --workspace "${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
          # Sanity: the workspace version + the intra-workspace path-dep pins.
          awk -F'"' '/^version = /{print "workspace:", $2; exit}' Cargo.toml
          grep -rho 'pathland-[a-z-]*", version = "[^"]*"' crates/*/Cargo.toml | sort -u

      - name: Test the publishable crates
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo test -p pathland-core -p pathland-engine -p pathland-view -p pathland-core-transport -p pathland-render-html

      - name: Publish in dependency order
        working-directory: lib/rust
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
          crates=(pathland-core pathland-engine pathland-view pathland-core-transport pathland-render-html)
          for c in "${crates[@]}"; do
            echo "::group::publish $c $version"
            # Idempotent: skip a crate+version already on crates.io.
            if curl -sf -A "pathland-release-ci" "https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/$c/$version" >/dev/null; then
              echo "$c $version already published — skipping"
              echo "::endgroup::"
              continue
            fi
            # `cargo publish` packages (leaving the .crate in target/package) then uploads.
            # `--allow-dirty`: `cargo set-version` above intentionally edits the
            # crates' manifests (the path-dep version pins), so the tree is "dirty".
            cargo publish --allow-dirty -p "$c"
            echo "::endgroup::"
            # Let the index propagate so the next dependent crate resolves it.
            sleep 20
          done

      - name: Package (guarantee .crate files for the release assets)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # All dependencies are published by now, so packaging every crate works.
          for c in pathland-core pathland-engine pathland-view pathland-core-transport pathland-render-html; do
            cargo package --allow-dirty -p "$c"
          done

      - name: Upload the .crate files
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: crates
          path: lib/rust/target/package/*.crate
          if-no-files-found: error

  java-natives:
    name: Build renderer natives (${{ matrix.platform }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: version
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { platform: windows-x86_64, runner: windows-latest }
          - { platform: linux-x86_64, runner: ubuntu-latest }
          - { platform: linux-aarch64, runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm }
          - { platform: macos-aarch64, runner: macos-14 }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Build the renderer cdylib
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build --release -p pathland-render-html

      - name: Stage the platform lib
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "${{ matrix.platform }}" in
            windows-*) src="pathland_render_html.dll";      dst="libpathland_render_html.dll" ;;
            macos-*)   src="libpathland_render_html.dylib"; dst="libpathland_render_html.dylib" ;;
            *)         src="libpathland_render_html.so";    dst="libpathland_render_html.so" ;;
          esac
          dest="lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native/${{ matrix.platform }}"
          mkdir -p "$dest"
          cp "lib/rust/target/release/$src" "$dest/$dst"
          ls -la "$dest"

      - name: Upload the platform lib
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: native-${{ matrix.platform }}
          path: lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native/${{ matrix.platform }}/*
          if-no-files-found: error

  java:
    name: Publish to Maven Central
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [version, java-natives]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}

      - name: Set up JDK + Maven credentials + GPG
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'
          cache: maven
          server-id: central
          server-username: CENTRAL_USERNAME
          server-password: CENTRAL_PASSWORD
          gpg-private-key: ${{ secrets.GPG_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          gpg-passphrase: MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE

      # Maven 3.10 (the runner default since 2026-10-04) writes a
      # `maven-metadata-local.xml` beside each artifact in the Central staging,
      # which central-publishing-maven-plugin bundles and the Portal rejects
      # ("content that does NOT have a .pom file"). 3.9.x does not. Pin it here.
      - name: Pin Maven 3.9.9
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          v=3.9.9
          curl -sSL "https://archive.apache.org/dist/maven/maven-3/$v/binaries/apache-maven-$v-bin.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$HOME"
          echo "$HOME/apache-maven-$v/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          mvn -v

      - name: Set the version from the tag
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: mvn -B -q versions:set -DnewVersion="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}" -DgenerateBackupPoms=false -DprocessAllModules=true

      - name: Download the platform natives
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: natives

      - name: Stage the natives for the jar embed
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native
          for d in natives/native-*; do
            platform="${d#natives/native-}"
            mkdir -p "lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native/$platform"
            cp "$d"/* "lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native/$platform/"
          done
          find lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native -type f

      # The demos are excluded from the release reactor: central-publishing-maven-plugin
      # bundles every reactor module (it ignores maven.deploy.skip), and the demos must
      # not be published.
      - name: Deploy to Maven Central
        working-directory: lib/java
        env:
          CENTRAL_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_USERNAME }}
          CENTRAL_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_PASSWORD }}
          MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.GPG_PASSPHRASE }}
        run: >-
          mvn -B -P release deploy
          -pl '!pathland-demo-views,!pathland-gtk-demo,!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo'

      - name: Collect the published main jars
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p dist/jars
          for m in pathland-view-core pathland-view pathland-view-processor pathland-render-html pathland-state-redis \
                   pathland-server-core pathland-observability pathland-test-kit \
                   pathland-spring-boot-starter pathland-quarkus-starter; do
            cp lib/java/"$m"/target/"$m"-*.jar dist/jars/ 2>/dev/null || true

metadata.output:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, 'docs/**', 'feature/**', 'fix/**', 'refactor/**', 'spec/**']
  pull_request:

jobs:
  design:
    name: Design (Style Dictionary)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: design/package-lock.json

      # Build the generated token CSS / manifest / bundle and validate the
      # three token layers against the protocol catalog, dark/forced-dark
      # rules, and the canonical length conventions.
      - name: Install, build, check
        working-directory: design
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run build
          npm run check

      # The Rust renderer embeds the generated bundle (committed for packaging).
      - name: Verify the committed renderer CSS matches the design build
        run: scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check

  rust:
    name: Rust (workspace + C ABI + no_std/wasm)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [design]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # The workspace includes pathland-render-gtk (GTK4 + libadwaita + GStreamer)
      # and pathland-render-qt (Qt Quick), so the runner needs the GTK4,
      # libadwaita, GStreamer, and Qt system libraries before `cargo test` can
      # link them. GStreamer is required because the GTK renderer plays app-driven
      # media through a direct GStreamer playbin (GTK4's own media backend is
      # compiled out of some builds); the plugins are the runtime set the audio
      # stack uses (playbin, volume/audioconvert, mp3 decode). The Qt libraries
      # are installed in the next step.
      - name: Install GTK4 + libadwaita + GStreamer system dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libgtk-4-dev \
            libadwaita-1-dev \
            libglib2.0-dev \
            libcairo2-dev \
            libpango1.0-dev \
            libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-dev \
            libgraphene-1.0-dev \
            libgstreamer1.0-dev \
            gstreamer1.0-plugins-base \
            gstreamer1.0-plugins-good \
            gstreamer1.0-libav

      - name: Install Qt6 (QML/Quick) system dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            qt6-base-dev \
            qt6-declarative-dev \
            qt6-declarative-private-dev \
            qt6-multimedia-dev \
            qml6-module-qtqml \
            qml6-module-qtqml-models \
            qml6-module-qtqml-workerscript \
            qml6-module-qtquick \
            qml6-module-qtquick-layouts \
            qml6-module-qtquick-controls \
            qml6-module-qtquick-templates \
            qml6-module-qtquick-window \
            qml6-module-qtmultimedia
        # The dev headers alone don't ship the QML runtime modules; the Qt
        # renderer's offscreen tests instantiate the QML (QtQml + WorkerScript,
        # Items, stacks/Grid via QtQuick.Layouts, Qt Quick Controls, Multimedia)
        # through QQmlComponent, so the qml6-module-* runtime files are required
        # too. Note the Qt6 package names: `-window` (the Qt5 `-window2` name
        # does not exist), and private headers need qt6-declarative-private-dev.

      - name: Install Rust (stable + wasm32 target)
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown

      - name: Cache cargo
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: lib/rust -> target

      - name: Test workspace
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo test

      - name: Qt renderer headless smoke
        working-directory: lib/rust
        env:
          QT_QPA_PLATFORM: offscreen
          QT_QUICK_BACKEND: software
        run: cargo test -p pathland-render-qt

      # The DOM renderer's constants/token conventions and the cross-renderer SSR
      # golden fixtures are GENERATED from Rust (pathland-ts-codegen /
      # pathland-html-golden). Regenerate them here and fail if the committed
      # files drifted — so a renumbered constant or a changed SSR shape can't land
      # without its TS/fixture counterparts.
      - name: Verify generated TS + golden fixtures are current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen
          cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit
          git diff --exit-code -- \
            lib/typescript/src/constants.ts \
            lib/typescript/src/generated \
            lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr

      # The neutral protocol manifest is the machine-readable mirror consumed by
      # non-Rust bindings. Regenerate it from the canonical Rust constants and fail
      # if the committed `spec/protocol.tsv` drifted. The Java job validates its
      # hand-written constants against this file.
      - name: Verify the protocol manifest is current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          cargo run -p pathland-protocol-manifest
          git -C ../.. diff --exit-code -- spec/protocol.tsv

      # The shared engine traces are emitted by the canonical Rust engine and
      # compared byte-for-byte by the JVM engine test. Verify the committed
      # fixtures have not drifted from the current engine behavior.
      - name: Verify engine trace fixtures are current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --check

      - name: Build the C ABI (cdylib, used by the Java JNA ring interop / native hosts)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-core-capi

      - name: no_std / wasm32 direction guard
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: ./check-wasm.sh

      # The Java HTML renderer shim needs the Rust renderer cdylib (the jar embeds
      # it so it travels with the artifact). Build it here and hand it to the java
      # job via an artifact.
      - name: Build the HTML renderer cdylib
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-render-html

      - name: Upload the renderer dylib for the java job
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pathland-render-html-native
          path: lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_html.so
          retention-days: 1

  java:
    name: Java (Maven reactor, JDK ${{ matrix.java }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [rust]
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        java: ['17', '21', '25']
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Whole-stack floor is Java 17 (maven.compiler.release=17; JNA native binding,
      # thread-local environment); the matrix proves every LTS from 17.
      - name: Set up JDK ${{ matrix.java }}
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: ${{ matrix.java }}
          cache: maven

      # The renderer jar embeds the Rust cdylib (built by the rust job). Restore it
      # into the debug dir the jar-embed step copies.
      - name: Download the Rust renderer dylib
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pathland-render-html-native
          path: lib/rust/target/debug

      - name: Test reactor (incl. the SSR web demos)
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: mvn -q -B test

  web-client:
    name: Web client (TypeScript DOM renderer)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: lib/typescript/package-lock.json

      - name: Install, typecheck, test, build
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run typecheck
          npm test
          npm run build

      # The demos serve the committed bundle from their static resource dirs
      # (content-hashed dom-renderer-<sha256>.js + the dom-renderer.current
      # pointer; stale hashed copies are pruned); copying the freshly built one
      # must not change the working tree.
      - name: Verify the committed bundle matches the source (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: |
          npm run copy-to-demos
          git diff --exit-code -- lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/src/main/resources lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-demo/src/main/resources

      # Real-browser guard for the per-window-id service worker: the browser-variance
      # bugs (WebKit reports an empty clientId on navigations; relative cache keys are
      # rejected) only appear in a real worker engine, never in jsdom/happy-dom.
      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit

      - name: Service worker E2E (Chromium + WebKit)
        working-directory: lib/typescript
        run: npm run test:e2ename: Release

      # which central-publishing-maven-plugin bundles and the Portal rejects
      # ("content that does NOT have a .pom file"). 3.9.x does not. Pin it here.
      - name: Pin Maven 3.9.9
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          v=3.9.9
          curl -sSL "https://archive.apache.org/dist/maven/maven-3/$v/binaries/apache-maven-$v-bin.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$HOME"
          echo "$HOME/apache-maven-$v/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          mvn -v

      - name: Set the version from the tag
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: mvn -B -q versions:set -DnewVersion="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}" -DgenerateBackupPoms=false -DprocessAllModules=true

      - name: Download the platform natives
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: natives

      - name: Stage the natives for the jar embed
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native
          for d in natives/native-*; do
            platform="${d#natives/native-}"
            mkdir -p "lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native/$platform"
            cp "$d"/* "lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native/$platform/"
          done
          find lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native -type f

      # The demos are excluded from the release reactor: central-publishing-maven-plugin
      # bundles every reactor module (it ignores maven.deploy.skip), and the demos must
      # not be published.
      - name: Deploy to Maven Central
        working-directory: lib/java
        env:
          CENTRAL_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_USERNAME }}
          CENTRAL_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_PASSWORD }}
          MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.GPG_PASSPHRASE }}
        run: >-
          mvn -B -P release deploy
          -pl '!pathland-demo-views,!pathland-gtk-demo,!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo'

      - name: Collect the published main jars
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p dist/jars
          for m in pathland-view-core pathland-view pathland-view-processor pathland-render-html pathland-state-redis \
                   pathland-server-core pathland-observability pathland-test-kit \
                   pathland-spring-boot-starter pathland-quarkus-starter; do
            cp lib/java/"$m"/target/"$m"-*.jar dist/jars/ 2>/dev/null || true

  bump:
    name: Commit the version back to main
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [version, rust, java]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - name: Set the Rust version
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cargo install cargo-edit --locked
          cargo set-version --workspace "${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"

      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'
      - name: Set the Java version
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: mvn -B -q versions:set -DnewVersion="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}" -DgenerateBackupPoms=false -DprocessAllModules=true

      - name: Commit + push
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          if git diff --quiet; then
            echo "version already current on main — nothing to commit"
            exit 0
          fi
          git add -A
          git commit -m "chore(release): v${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
          git push origin HEAD:main

  release-assets:
    name: Attach release assets
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [version, rust, java-natives, java]
    steps:
      - name: Download all build artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: dist

      - name: Collect the files to attach
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p out
          find dist -type f \( -name '*.crate' -o -name '*.jar' -o -name '*.dll' -o -name '*.so' -o -name '*.dylib' \) -exec cp {} out/ \;
          ls -la out

      - name: Attach to the GitHub Release
        env:

Need plan likely enough, but need understand Quarkus extension standard layout and plugin. Could inspect installed quarkus extension POM structure. We can cite exact plugin. Need decide modules names. Existing artifact `pathland-quarkus-starter`; renaming breaks current demo/docs. Plan could:
Phase A dependency split:
- Rename `pathland-quarkus-starter` -> `pathland-quarkus` core extension? Or keep starter? User asked plan. We need recommend.

Artifact naming:
- Core extension runtime artifact `pathland-quarkus` and deployment `pathland-quarkus-deployment` (Quarkus convention: deployment artifact in same group, `<artifact>-deployment`; plugin sets it).
- Java DSL extension: `pathland-quarkus-java` runtime + `pathland-quarkus-java-deployment`? Does a dependency-only extension need code? It could be a true extension with deployment module, even if empty. But Quarkus ecosystem variants like `quarkus-hibernate-orm-panache-kotlin` have runtime + deployment. Yes.
- Kotlin DSL extension: `pathland-quarkus-kotlin` runtime + `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-deployment`.
- Existing `pathland-quarkus-starter` maybe legacy aggregator that depends core + Java to preserve users. But if eventual Java removal, deprecated. Could keep as compatibility alias to `pathland-quarkus-java` (i.e., depends on Java extension) or core? Existing docs promise Java DSL authoring. If alias to core, Java demo breaks unless it adds Java extension. But public users of starter expect Java DSL. Preserve behavior by alias to `pathland-quarkus-java`, deprecate. Yet its name "starter" okay.
- However, Quarkus extension names are usually one artifact; aliases can be plain POM/jar dependencies, not extension. If alias depends on an extension, Quarkus resolves. Good.
- For core extension, perhaps preserve `pathland-quarkus-starter` as name? But that's not semantically core and Kotlin extension would depend on "starter". Could still, but less clean. Better create new core name and deprecate starter. User likely okay pre-release.
- Maybe rename existing module to `pathland-quarkus` (runtime) and add deployment. Then new `pathland-quarkus-java`, `pathland-quarkus-kotlin`. That's a big rename but plan.
- Alternatively just `pathland-quarkus` core, no alias `starter` (pre-release 0.1.5). But docs and demos updated. Need consider Maven Central previous release maybe 0.1.5? We don't know if published. Current version 0.1.5. User may have published. Better preserve alias for compatibility. Plan can say "decide"; recommend deprecated alias.
- Quarkus version 3.39.1, Kotlin 2.2.20.

Need understand Quarkus extension config:
- runtime module POM has `quarkus-extension-maven-plugin` with `<capabilities>` maybe. Deployment module POM has dependencies on runtime + `quarkus-core-deployment`, `quarkus-arc-deployment`, maybe `quarkus-rest-deployment`, `quarkus-websockets-next-deployment`, `quarkus-micrometer-deployment`, `quarkus-smallrye-health-deployment`, `pathland-quarkus-deployment`.
- Extension processor generates `META-INF/quarkus-extension.properties`.
- A deployment class `PathlandProcessor` with `@BuildStep` returning `FeatureBuildItem("pathland")` is minimal.
- For core extension, since runtime has CDI beans discovered via `beans.xml`, may not need deployment code beyond feature. But extension descriptor needed.
- Need consider conditional dependencies and capabilities. Core `pathland-quarkus` provides capability `dev.pathland.quarkus`. Kotlin extension depends core, `quarkus-kotlin`; maybe `dependencyCondition` not necessary. If we want Kotlin extension to be conditional, it's the app adding it anyway. But typical `quarkus-rest-kotlin` uses `<dependencyCondition>` on `quarkus-kotlin` so it activates only when Kotlin extension present (if pulled transitively). For DSL extension, hard dependency on quarkus-kotlin is fine; but Quarkus extension best practice is use `dependencyCondition` to avoid forcing Kotlin if user adds Kotlin DSL? Actually if user adds `pathland-quarkus-kotlin`, they expect Kotlin, so direct dep is fine.
- Java extension depends core + pathland-view.
- Kotlin extension depends core + pathland-view-kotlin + quarkus-kotlin. Should it also depend `quarkus-kotlin-deployment`? Runtime dependency on `quarkus-kotlin` lets deployment module resolve; deployment module maybe not need direct. Quarkus extension dependencies are handled automatically. But could add deployment counterpart? In POM, runtime extensions are added normally; deployment dependencies are resolved by Quarkus. For build steps, deployment module may need `quarkus-kotlin-deployment` if using classes. Not needed.
- Pathland Kotlin extension may need no custom deployment; just feature. But to ensure Kotlin live reload? Quarkus-kotlin extension handles.
- Need codestarts? Maybe out of scope. User wants plan; include optional codestart. "DX" suggests codestart useful. But implementing codestart requires Quarkus codestart modules and resources; could be phase 4 optional. But plan should include.
- Need ensure Kotlin extension doesn't force Java DSL: Maven Enforcer banned dependency `dev.pathland:pathland-view` in `pathland-quarkus-kotlin` and Kotlin demo. Also check transitive `pathland-demo-views` not used. Add `maven-enforcer-plugin` rule. Maybe use `dependency:tree` in tests? CI.
- Need add a `PathlandQuarkusKotlinTest` or demo `@QuarkusTest` to verify Kotlin app works.
- Need Kotlin demo. Could reuse `MusicPlayerView`? It's Java DSL in demo-views, no. Need create a Kotlin-only demo view. Could port a simplified demo (counter/name/list/nav) in Kotlin. Need include `pathland-demo-assets`? If media not needed. We can keep simple. But user wanted end-to-end demo perhaps. Need plan for new demo. Could include tests SSR + WS.
- Need update existing Java demo to depend on `pathland-quarkus-java` (or alias `starter`) and `pathland-demo-views`.
- Need update starter tests to use core-only test view, not Java DSL; or move CounterApp test to Java extension. Better:
  - Core extension tests should use a tiny core `View` implementation? That's cumbersome. Could keep `pathland-view` test dependency (test-only) in core extension; this does not affect consumers. But user wants core extension DSL-free production; test-scope okay. Yet to prove core is DSL-free, enforcer can ban compile dependency. Fine.
  - Better create test view using core `Node`? But test-scope Java DSL is okay.
  - However if Java DSL eventually removed, core extension tests would need rewrite. Not urgent.
- `pathland-quarkus-java` might have no code; if tests need CounterApp? Could move Quarkus integration tests that need Java DSL there? But core tests already. Maybe Java extension should be a plain aggregator with no tests? For parity, we can put a minimal `@QuarkusTest` using Java DSL in Java extension to prove dependency. But if no runtime classes, does extension need deployment? It can just be a runtime extension with an empty deployment. Could also keep it as a **starter aggregator** that is not a Quarkus extension because it just brings dependencies. In Quarkus, a library that only brings deps does not need extension metadata. But user asked extensions; a "Java DSL extension" with no integration code can just be a normal artifact. Yet for consistency and future Java-specific build steps (annotation processing?), true extension is okay.
- Important: annotation processor `pathland-view-processor` for Java State fields. The current Java demo's `pathland-demo-views` configures processor itself. Java extension could carry processor? It can't add annotation processor paths either. Codestart/docs can. Not necessary.
- Kotlin extension cannot add compiler plugin. Codestart.
- Need add extension descriptors, deployment modules to root POM. Quarkus extension builds with `quarkus-extension-maven-plugin` and `quarkus-extension-processor` maybe through `quarkus-extension-maven-plugin`? In Quarkus POM examples, extension runtime module uses `quarkus-extension-maven-plugin`; deployment module uses `quarkus-extension-maven-plugin`? # pathland-view-kotlin — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 1, 2026

The idiomatic Kotlin authoring surface (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`). Phase 3 is
complete: every production view/modifier is Kotlin-owned over
`pathland-view-core`; the Java DSL is a test-scope parity oracle only.

## Phase 3

- **Core-owned in Kotlin**: all primitives, shapes, stacks, grids, scroll/lazy
  containers, `ForEach`, `Button`, text/value controls, media, navigation,
  `Label`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`, `ProxyView`, and the complete modifier
  vocabulary (padding/frame/fonts/colors/borders/shadows/effects/transforms/
  interaction/accessibility/environment/styles/window metadata).
- **Dependency boundary**: main depends on `pathland-view-core` only; the Java
  DSL is test-scope for byte-for-byte parity comparisons.
- Tests compare the Kotlin-owned views and modifiers against the Java DSL.

## Implemented

- **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text`, `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`, `Rectangle`,
  `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`, `Divider`, `Spacer`,
  `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.
- **Containers**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`,
  `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`,
  `ProxyView`.
- **Controls**: `Button` (title or label subtree), `TextField`, `SecureField`,
  `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`,
  `ColorPicker`.
- **Automatic child collection**: `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no
  `.children(...)`. A custom `KotlinView` constructed inline in a block
  auto-registers; a view stored as a field is added explicitly with `+field`
  inside `body()` (it does not leak into the enclosing scope). An explicit
  `view.add()` / `+view` is available for Java-constructed views (e.g.
  `mediaController.attach()`).
- **Signals**: `signal`, `computed`, `constant`, `effect`, `untracked`,
  `Signal<T>.value`, `WritableSignal<T>.value`, `Signal<T>.map`, `readonly`.
- **Modifier sugar**: `.padding`, `.frame`, `.offset`, `.position`, `.fixedSize`,
  layout priority/z-index/aspect ratio, the full text-formatting surface,
  foreground/background/border/corner radius/shadow, visual effects, transforms,
  visibility/disabled/hit-testing, accessibility, tap/pointer events,
  environment binding, styles, window metadata, and navigation intents. The
  Java `.modifiers(...)` operation remains available as an escape hatch.
- **Persisted state**: `KotlinView` base class + `val count by state(0)`
  (auto-keyed by property name) or `state(0, "key")`; a `mutableState(0)` signal
  form for two-way controls. Bound to the session's `PersistentState` before the
  first `body()` render — no kapt and no annotation processor.
- **Reactive bodies**: plain `if`/`when`/`for` in `body()`; `ForEach` over a static
  list or `Signal<List<T>>` with row-scoped child collection.
- **Navigation**: `navigator { route(...) }`, `NavigationStack`, `NavigationLink`,
  `isActive`, and `.navigate`/`.push`/`.replace` intents.
- **Media**: `Video(controller)`; audio remains view-less (`controller.attach()`
  can be added with `+`).
- **Tests**: byte-identical Kotlin-vs-Java frame comparison, auto-collection,
  modifier property parity, fine-grained signal deltas, persisted/stateful bodies,
  reactive `ForEach`, two-way `TextField`, navigation swaps and link intents.

## Not implemented / gaps

- The Kotlin modifier config types (`Padding`, `Frame`, `Border`, `Shadow`,
  `ClipShape`, `Font`) are Kotlin ownership types; code migrating from the Java
  DSL should use the Kotlin `Modifiers` sugar instead of Java config classes.
- A Kotlin-native annotation processor is intentionally not used. `state(...)`
  works on `KotlinView` subclasses; a plain `View` implementation should use
  signals directly or extend `KotlinView`.
- No Kotlin Multiplatform target yet — the module is JVM-only over
  `pathland-view-core`.
- `SecureField` is Kotlin-owned (`TEXT_FIELD` + `IS_SECURE`).
# pathland-view (Java DSL) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 1, 2026

The hand-written, framework-agnostic Java 17+ authoring DSL
(`dev.pathland.view`). The engine/runtime now lives in `pathland-view-core`
(`dev.pathland.view.core*` + `dev.pathland.view.engine`); this module owns only
the concrete Java views, controls, styles, and the `Modifiers` facade. Protocol
contract: `spec/`. Runs on every LTS from Java 17.

> Engine/runtime items below (signals, state, emitter, transport, router, JNA) are
> implemented in `pathland-view-core` and are listed here because this module's
> tests exercise them end-to-end through the Java DSL.

## Implemented

- **Window metadata** (`windowMetadata(w -> w.title(...).description(...).locale(...))`): a root-scoped `ViewModifier` with signal-backed fields. The emitter emits the initial `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` fields at mount, re-emits only the changed field on a signal write, and re-sends every field in `renderFull` (resync). `FrameOpcodeSink` and the JNA `RingOpcodeSink` carry it; a route title is a `computed` over the router.
- **Per-component reactive bodies (#88)**: `body()` / `renderNode(Environment)` is a
  tracked render. Each child view is a `ViewSlot` with its own synchronous
  `Signals.tracked` computation; a signal read there re-renders only that component
  and the emitter diffs its retained subtree. Plain `if`/`switch`/`for` over signals
  now works in `body()` (bare control flow), with `View.of(Supplier<View>)` as the
  inline supplier form. The root chain (`body()` delegation, modifiers,
  environment/tap/navigation wrappers) stays in one slot; child views are child
  slots. A bound signal (`Text.make(t -> t.text(signal))`) remains fine-grained and
  does not re-run the body (initial binding reads are untracked). Non-signal reads
  are mount-time only. The root component type must stay stable. `render(Environment)`
  is the emitter entry point; primitives override `renderNode(Environment)`.
  `Conditional`/`Case` are removed (replaced by bare control flow + `View.of`).
- **`ForEach`** (`ForEach.of(list | Signal<List<T>>, (item, index) -> View)`):
  a Group-backed reactive list component. A static list maps once per render; a
  `Signal<List<T>>` re-renders only the list slot. Each item is a child component
  slot; null children are skipped; reconciliation is position + type (no keys).
  `ForEachTest`.
- **Cross-language vocabulary** (spec DSL.md §9.3.1): the shared anchors
  (`View`, `body`/`build`, `Signal`, `computed`, `State`, `ForEach`, `View.of`,
  `children`, `modifiers`) and the native spellings for Swift/Java/Kotlin/Rust/
  TypeScript. Swift is the canonical SwiftUI-shaped reference; Rust parity is
  Phase 2.
- **`ProxyView`** (`ProxyView.make(p -> p.endpoint(...).route(...).credential(...))`):
  a `PROXY_VIEW` (0x1E) container whose child subtree is served by **another**
  Pathland server (spec/PROXY.md). It authors **no** children — the origin root is
  spliced in at runtime — and takes size modifiers like any view. The immutable
  `ProxyConfig` snapshot rides the node (`PathlandNode.proxyConfig`) and is
  surfaced to the host through `RenderResult.proxyViews()` (node id → config) so
  `pathland-server-core` opens an origin connection per proxy node. The emitter's
  internal `onStructureReconciled(Runnable)` hook (like `snapshotEmission`) fires
  after each structural reconcile — after the routing maps reflect the new subtree
  — so the host reconciles origin connections against the live `proxyViews` map
  (a proxy lives exactly while its node is in the retained tree, spec/PROXY.md §7).
- **`SizeThatFits` fit slot** (`SizeThatFits.make(Fit...)` + `Fit.of(view, minWidth)`):
  a structural slot (`SIZE_THAT_FITS` 0x17) emitting `FIT_QUERY` (LIST, ascending
  thresholds) + the single selected child — unselected candidates never transmit.
  The host routes `FIT_CHANGED` into the slot's fit sink
  (`RenderResult.fitInputs`, via `InputDispatcher`), which re-renders only the fit
  component (an unchanged index re-emits zero opcodes). The LIST
  value type is written by `FrameOpcodeSink`/`RingOpcodeSink`
  (`[count][f32 × count]` arena entries). A slot's selection is **retained node
  state** (`PathlandNode.fitSelection`): a parent re-render creates a fresh fit
  component with a default index, so the emitter seeds it from the node it replaces
  (`ViewSlot.oldNodeHint` / `Emitter.currentSlotOldFitSelection`) — a nested fit
  (the player bar's controls slot under the root row) keeps its candidate instead
  of resetting to compact (a reset would strand the DOM client, which never
  re-reports an unchanged width). The **web-SSR full-snapshot emission** (issue #141) is an
  internal emitter mode (`Emitter.snapshotEmission(true)`, armed by
  `PathlandSession`): on mount/resync the slot emits EVERY candidate in `FIT_QUERY`
  order so the SSR renders all branches gated by CSS container queries (a no-JS
  correct first paint) — the authored DSL is unchanged. `PathlandNode.fitReported`
  and the emitter's `snapshotActive` flag keep the multi-candidate presentation
  until the first `FIT_CHANGED`; that report re-renders the fit component with one
  selected child, and the web client unwraps the gated branches. The downgrade is a
  **clean N→1** (`Emitter.reconcileSnapshotFit`): it keeps the SELECTED candidate's
  node as-is (retaining its id + subtree, zero churn) and removes the others — it
  never positionally diffs, because both candidates are frequently the same
  component and morphing the loser's node into the winner would relocate the winner
  into the SSR's loser wrapper and break the renderer's candidate-position CSS gate.
  **View reuse** (issue #159): the same `View` instance may not be the candidate
  of two `Fit`s — `SizeThatFits.make` rejects it (`IllegalStateException`), since
  it would be materialized once per candidate and leak shared state / ids.
  Sharing a subtree **inside** two distinct candidate roots stays allowed; every
  materialized copy gets a distinct node id. The emitter enforces the frame's
  **unique-node-id invariant** (spec/OPCODE.md §Frame Lifecycle) with
  `Emitter.duplicateIds` / a fail-loud guard at mount, resync, and after each
  structural reconcile, so an id-overriding pass (an identity-stable node pinning
  a playback key) can never silently corrupt an id-keyed consumer.
- **v2 authoring surface (complete)**: every concrete view exposes
  the three operations — values via the static `View.make(...)`
  (`make(Consumer<Config>)`, `make(value)` shortcuts, empty `make()`),
  `.modifiers(ViewModifier...)` (an **instance** operation — the `View` interface
  ships a `default View.modifiers(ViewModifier...)` so a bare `View` value
  (a style's `config.label()`, a `Color`, a `FitSlot`) applies modifiers too, and
  `ViewBuilder` overrides it covariantly), and (content-bearing views) `.children(View...)`
  (static first-call retained as a value-less convenience). Values are configured
  via `make(c -> …)`, the chain lives on the returned generic
  `ViewBuilder<V, C>` (`View.Config`, `Configurable<C>`, `ChildrenView`; `View`
  keeps only `body()`/`render()`/`modifiers(...)` — Java's static-vs-instance rule
  means `make(...)` is the only static of the three; the former static
  `X.modifiers(...)` first-call entry points are **removed**). Modifiers/styles are
  built through the **`Modifiers` facade's lowercase functions** — one
  `import static dev.pathland.view.Modifiers.*;` brings the whole vocabulary
  (`padding(p -> p.uniform(16))`, `frame(f -> f.width(100).height(24))`,
  `foregroundStyle(f -> f.color(c))`, `borderedButtonStyle(b -> …)`); the
  former per-type `with(...)` configurators are **removed** (a same-package
  construction seam remains for the facade). **Single-value modifiers are the value
  itself** (`FontWeight.BOLD`, `TextAlignment.CENTER`, `Truncation.TAIL`,
  `TextCase.UPPERCASE`, `ControlSize.LARGE`, `FontStyle.ITALIC`,
  `FontDesign.SERIF`, `Font.system(18)` — the enums + `Font` implement
  `ViewModifier`), and `Style extends ViewModifier`, so `.modifiers(MyButtonStyle)`
  scopes the matching environment key — an app-authored style exposes a lowercase
  static factory on its own type (`BorderedButtonStyle.borderedButtonStyle(s -> s…)`).
  The `View` per-modifier sugar
  (`font`/`navigate`/`environment`/`onPathChange`), the former
  `View.with(ViewModifier...)` general modifier chain, and the `*Mod` shims
  (`EnvironmentMod`→`EnvironmentBinding`, `NavigationMod`→`NavigationIntent`,
  `PathChangeMod`→`PathChange`, `FontWeightMod`→`FontWeight`, …) are **removed** —
  every consumer (demo views, starters, renderers) is on the v3 surface. The
  former `.of(...)` **construction factories are removed**: a **single-value
  construction overload** replaces them where the config has
  a designated primary member (views `make(value)` — `Text.make("hi")`;
  modifiers the lowercase value form — `padding(16)`,
# pathland-view-core (JVM engine) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 1, 2026

The shared, framework-agnostic JVM engine and runtime for the Pathland protocol.
It owns the `View` SPI and shared authoring vocabulary, the retained-tree
diff emitter, signals/computed/effects, the wire codec, router, cross-platform
state, and JNA ring interop. The Java DSL (`pathland-view`) and the Kotlin DSL
(`pathland-view-kotlin`) are authoring layers over this module; server and
renderer modules depend on core only.

## Implemented

- **Protocol** (`dev.pathland.view.core.protocol`): `Components`, `Properties`,
  `Commands`, `Categories`, `ValueTypes`, `Opcode`, `ValueEncoder`, `WireValue`,
  `TokenPath`.
- **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.core.signal`): `signal`/`computed`/`effect`/
  `untracked`, synchronous glitch-free flush, equality suppression, error
  caching/retry, circular-dependency detection, and a thread-safe global
  `Scheduler`.
- **State** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): `State`/`PersistentState`,
  untyped `StateStore`, in-memory store and provider.
- **Transport** (`dev.pathland.view.core.transport`): `ProtocolFrame`,
  `FrameCodec`, `Event`, `EnvironmentData`, `OpcodeSink`, `FrameOpcodeSink`.
- **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.core.router`): `Route`, `RouteTable`, `Router`,
  `Navigation`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationIntent`, `Params`, `Chrome`,
  `NavOp`. `NavigationLink` stays in the Java DSL because it composes `Button`.
- **JNA interop** (`dev.pathland.view.core.ffm`): lazy `PathlandCore` binding and
  `RingOpcodeSink` over `libpathland_core`.
- **Emitter** (`dev.pathland.view.engine`): `Emitter`, `PathlandNode`, `ViewSlot`,
  `RenderResult`, `InputDispatcher`, `ReactiveValues`, `DateInput`, `MediaInput`.
  Implements mount/id assignment, diff-based reactive emission, node-level binding
  effects, structural reconciliation, fit/media/navigation routing, and the
  zero-opcode unchanged recompute contract.
- **Shared SPI/values** (`dev.pathland.view.core`): `View`, `ViewModifier`,
  `Configurable`, `ChildrenView`, `Modified`, `ViewBuilder`, `Configurators`,
  `Environment*`, `Platform`, `Theme*`, `MediaController`, `WindowMetadata`,
  `ProxyConfig`, `Color`, `Length`, shared enums, style protocols, and modifier
  wrappers.
- **Protocol manifest validation** (`ProtocolManifestTest`): the hand-written
  protocol constants (`Components`, `Properties`, `Commands`, `Categories`,
  `ValueTypes`) are checked against `spec/protocol.tsv` — including no extra
  public numeric constants and the full `ValueTypes.forProperty` mapping. No
  Java source is generated.
- **Shared engine traces**: `EngineTraceTest` (in `pathland-view`) runs the
  mount/text/property scenarios against the Rust-emitted PLPL fixtures under
  `spec/engine-traces/`, byte-for-byte. The canonical order lives in
  `spec/ENGINE.md`.
- **Test coverage**: the Java DSL module's test suite exercises the engine
  end-to-end (emitter/reconcile, signals, state, router, transport, JNA ring),
  plus the server/HTML/desktop consumers.

## Package boundary

- `pathland-view-core` is one Maven module for now: `core`/`engine` are logical
  subpackages inside it, with a few deliberate intra-module references
  (`Color`/`MediaController`/`Modified` materialize `PathlandNode`). Splitting
  `core` and `engine` into separate artifacts requires a node SPI first.
- Production runtimes/renderers (`pathland-server-core`,
  `pathland-render-html`, `pathland-state-redis`, `pathland-test-kit`) depend on
  core, not on the Java DSL. Tests that author views through the DSL add
  `pathland-view` in test scope. The app-facing starters do depend on
  `pathland-view` because application code authors its root `View` with the DSL.

# pathland-view (Java DSL) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 1, 2026

The hand-written, framework-agnostic Java 17+ authoring DSL
(`dev.pathland.view`). The engine/runtime now lives in `pathland-view-core`
(`dev.pathland.view.core*` + `dev.pathland.view.engine`); this module owns only
the concrete Java views, controls, styles, and the `Modifiers` facade. Protocol
contract: `spec/`. Runs on every LTS from Java 17.

> Engine/runtime items below (signals, state, emitter, transport, router, JNA) are
> implemented in `pathland-view-core` and are listed here because this module's
> tests exercise them end-to-end through the Java DSL.

## Implemented

- **Window metadata** (`windowMetadata(w -> w.title(...).description(...).locale(...))`): a root-scoped `ViewModifier` with signal-backed fields. The emitter emits the initial `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` fields at mount, re-emits only the changed field on a signal write, and re-sends every field in `renderFull` (resync). `FrameOpcodeSink` and the JNA `RingOpcodeSink` carry it; a route title is a `computed` over the router.
- **Per-component reactive bodies (#88)**: `body()` / `renderNode(Environment)` is a
  tracked render. Each child view is a `ViewSlot` with its own synchronous
  `Signals.tracked` computation; a signal read there re-renders only that component
  and the emitter diffs its retained subtree. Plain `if`/`switch`/`for` over signals
  now works in `body()` (bare control flow), with `View.of(Supplier<View>)` as the
  inline supplier form. The root chain (`body()` delegation, modifiers,
  environment/tap/navigation wrappers) stays in one slot; child views are child
  slots. A bound signal (`Text.make(t -> t.text(signal))`) remains fine-grained and
  does not re-run the body (initial binding reads are untracked). Non-signal reads
  are mount-time only. The root component type must stay stable. `render(Environment)`
  is the emitter entry point; primitives override `renderNode(Environment)`.
  `Conditional`/`Case` are removed (replaced by bare control flow + `View.of`).
- **`ForEach`** (`ForEach.of(list | Signal<List<T>>, (item, index) -> View)`):
  a Group-backed reactive list component. A static list maps once per render; a
  `Signal<List<T>>` re-renders only the list slot. Each item is a child component
  slot; null children are skipped; reconciliation is position + type (no keys).
  `ForEachTest`.
- **Cross-language vocabulary** (spec DSL.md §9.3.1): the shared anchors
  (`View`, `body`/`build`, `Signal`, `computed`, `State`, `ForEach`, `View.of`,
  `children`, `modifiers`) and the native spellings for Swift/Java/Kotlin/Rust/
  TypeScript. Swift is the canonical SwiftUI-shaped reference; Rust parity is
  Phase 2.
- **`ProxyView`** (`ProxyView.make(p -> p.endpoint(...).route(...).credential(...))`):
  a `PROXY_VIEW` (0x1E) container whose child subtree is served by **another**
  Pathland server (spec/PROXY.md). It authors **no** children — the origin root is
  spliced in at runtime — and takes size modifiers like any view. The immutable
  `ProxyConfig` snapshot rides the node (`PathlandNode.proxyConfig`) and is
  surfaced to the host through `RenderResult.proxyViews()` (node id → config) so
  `pathland-server-core` opens an origin connection per proxy node. The emitter's
  internal `onStructureReconciled(Runnable)` hook (like `snapshotEmission`) fires
  after each structural reconcile — after the routing maps reflect the new subtree
  — so the host reconciles origin connections against the live `proxyViews` map
  (a proxy lives exactly while its node is in the retained tree, spec/PROXY.md §7).
- **`SizeThatFits` fit slot** (`SizeThatFits.make(Fit...)` + `Fit.of(view, minWidth)`):
  a structural slot (`SIZE_THAT_FITS` 0x17) emitting `FIT_QUERY` (LIST, ascending
  thresholds) + the single selected child — unselected candidates never transmit.
  The host routes `FIT_CHANGED` into the slot's fit sink
  (`RenderResult.fitInputs`, via `InputDispatcher`), which re-renders only the fit
  component (an unchanged index re-emits zero opcodes). The LIST
  value type is written by `FrameOpcodeSink`/`RingOpcodeSink`
  (`[count][f32 × count]` arena entries). A slot's selection is **retained node
  state** (`PathlandNode.fitSelection`): a parent re-render creates a fresh fit
  component with a default index, so the emitter seeds it from the node it replaces
  (`ViewSlot.oldNodeHint` / `Emitter.currentSlotOldFitSelection`) — a nested fit
  (the player bar's controls slot under the root row) keeps its candidate instead
  of resetting to compact (a reset would strand the DOM client, which never
  re-reports an unchanged width). The **web-SSR full-snapshot emission** (issue #141) is an
  internal emitter mode (`Emitter.snapshotEmission(true)`, armed by
  `PathlandSession`): on mount/resync the slot emits EVERY candidate in `FIT_QUERY`
  order so the SSR renders all branches gated by CSS container queries (a no-JS
  correct first paint) — the authored DSL is unchanged. `PathlandNode.fitReported`
  and the emitter's `snapshotActive` flag keep the multi-candidate presentation
  until the first `FIT_CHANGED`; that report re-renders the fit component with one
  selected child, and the web client unwraps the gated branches. The downgrade is a
  **clean N→1** (`Emitter.reconcileSnapshotFit`): it keeps the SELECTED candidate's
  node as-is (retaining its id + subtree, zero churn) and removes the others — it
  never positionally diffs, because both candidates are frequently the same
  component and morphing the loser's node into the winner would relocate the winner
  into the SSR's loser wrapper and break the renderer's candidate-position CSS gate.
  **View reuse** (issue #159): the same `View` instance may not be the candidate
  of two `Fit`s — `SizeThatFits.make` rejects it (`IllegalStateException`), since
  it would be materialized once per candidate and leak shared state / ids.
  Sharing a subtree **inside** two distinct candidate roots stays allowed; every
  materialized copy gets a distinct node id. The emitter enforces the frame's
  **unique-node-id invariant** (spec/OPCODE.md §Frame Lifecycle) with
  `Emitter.duplicateIds` / a fail-loud guard at mount, resync, and after each
  structural reconcile, so an id-overriding pass (an identity-stable node pinning
  a playback key) can never silently corrupt an id-keyed consumer.
- **v2 authoring surface (complete)**: every concrete view exposes
  the three operations — values via the static `View.make(...)`
  (`make(Consumer<Config>)`, `make(value)` shortcuts, empty `make()`),
  `.modifiers(ViewModifier...)` (an **instance** operation — the `View` interface
  ships a `default View.modifiers(ViewModifier...)` so a bare `View` value
  (a style's `config.label()`, a `Color`, a `FitSlot`) applies modifiers too, and
  `ViewBuilder` overrides it covariantly), and (content-bearing views) `.children(View...)`
  (static first-call retained as a value-less convenience). Values are configured
  via `make(c -> …)`, the chain lives on the returned generic
  `ViewBuilder<V, C>` (`View.Config`, `Configurable<C>`, `ChildrenView`; `View`
  keeps only `body()`/`render()`/`modifiers(...)` — Java's static-vs-instance rule
  means `make(...)` is the only static of the three; the former static
  `X.modifiers(...)` first-call entry points are **removed**). Modifiers/styles are
  built through the **`Modifiers` facade's lowercase functions** — one
  `import static dev.pathland.view.Modifiers.*;` brings the whole vocabulary
  (`padding(p -> p.uniform(16))`, `frame(f -> f.width(100).height(24))`,
  `foregroundStyle(f -> f.color(c))`, `borderedButtonStyle(b -> …)`); the
  former per-type `with(...)` configurators are **removed** (a same-package
  construction seam remains for the facade). **Single-value modifiers are the value
  itself** (`FontWeight.BOLD`, `TextAlignment.CENTER`, `Truncation.TAIL`,
  `TextCase.UPPERCASE`, `ControlSize.LARGE`, `FontStyle.ITALIC`,
  `FontDesign.SERIF`, `Font.system(18)` — the enums + `Font` implement
  `ViewModifier`), and `Style extends ViewModifier`, so `.modifiers(MyButtonStyle)`
  scopes the matching environment key — an app-authored style exposes a lowercase
  static factory on its own type (`BorderedButtonStyle.borderedButtonStyle(s -> s…)`).
  The `View` per-modifier sugar
  (`font`/`navigate`/`environment`/`onPathChange`), the former
  `View.with(ViewModifier...)` general modifier chain, and the `*Mod` shims
  (`EnvironmentMod`→`EnvironmentBinding`, `NavigationMod`→`NavigationIntent`,
  `PathChangeMod`→`PathChange`, `FontWeightMod`→`FontWeight`, …) are **removed** —
  every consumer (demo views, starters, renderers) is on the v3 surface. The
  former `.of(...)` **construction factories are removed**: a **single-value
  construction overload** replaces them where the config has
  a designated primary member (views `make(value)` — `Text.make("hi")`;
  modifiers the lowercase value form — `padding(16)`,
# pathland-view-core (JVM engine) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 1, 2026

The shared, framework-agnostic JVM engine and runtime for the Pathland protocol.
It owns the `View` SPI and shared authoring vocabulary, the retained-tree
diff emitter, signals/computed/effects, the wire codec, router, cross-platform
state, and JNA ring interop. The Java DSL (`pathland-view`) and the Kotlin DSL
(`pathland-view-kotlin`) are authoring layers over this module; server and
renderer modules depend on core only.

## Implemented

- **Protocol** (`dev.pathland.view.core.protocol`): `Components`, `Properties`,
  `Commands`, `Categories`, `ValueTypes`, `Opcode`, `ValueEncoder`, `WireValue`,
  `TokenPath`.
- **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.core.signal`): `signal`/`computed`/`effect`/
  `untracked`, synchronous glitch-free flush, equality suppression, error
  caching/retry, circular-dependency detection, and a thread-safe global
  `Scheduler`.
- **State** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): `State`/`PersistentState`,
  untyped `StateStore`, in-memory store and provider.
- **Transport** (`dev.pathland.view.core.transport`): `ProtocolFrame`,
  `FrameCodec`, `Event`, `EnvironmentData`, `OpcodeSink`, `FrameOpcodeSink`.
- **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.core.router`): `Route`, `RouteTable`, `Router`,
  `Navigation`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationIntent`, `Params`, `Chrome`,
  `NavOp`. `NavigationLink` stays in the Java DSL because it composes `Button`.
- **JNA interop** (`dev.pathland.view.core.ffm`): lazy `PathlandCore` binding and
  `RingOpcodeSink` over `libpathland_core`.
- **Emitter** (`dev.pathland.view.engine`): `Emitter`, `PathlandNode`, `ViewSlot`,
  `RenderResult`, `InputDispatcher`, `ReactiveValues`, `DateInput`, `MediaInput`.
  Implements mount/id assignment, diff-based reactive emission, node-level binding
  effects, structural reconciliation, fit/media/navigation routing, and the
  zero-opcode unchanged recompute contract.
- **Shared SPI/values** (`dev.pathland.view.core`): `View`, `ViewModifier`,
  `Configurable`, `ChildrenView`, `Modified`, `ViewBuilder`, `Configurators`,
  `Environment*`, `Platform`, `Theme*`, `MediaController`, `WindowMetadata`,
  `ProxyConfig`, `Color`, `Length`, shared enums, style protocols, and modifier
  wrappers.
- **Protocol manifest validation** (`ProtocolManifestTest`): the hand-written
  protocol constants (`Components`, `Properties`, `Commands`, `Categories`,
  `ValueTypes`) are checked against `spec/protocol.tsv` — including no extra
  public numeric constants and the full `ValueTypes.forProperty` mapping. No
  Java source is generated.
- **Shared engine traces**: `EngineTraceTest` (in `pathland-view`) runs the
  mount/text/property scenarios against the Rust-emitted PLPL fixtures under
  `spec/engine-traces/`, byte-for-byte. The canonical order lives in
  `spec/ENGINE.md`.
- **Test coverage**: the Java DSL module's test suite exercises the engine
  end-to-end (emitter/reconcile, signals, state, router, transport, JNA ring),
  plus the server/HTML/desktop consumers.

## Package boundary

- `pathland-view-core` is one Maven module for now: `core`/`engine` are logical
  subpackages inside it, with a few deliberate intra-module references
  (`Color`/`MediaController`/`Modified` materialize `PathlandNode`). Splitting
  `core` and `engine` into separate artifacts requires a node SPI first.
- Production runtimes/renderers (`pathland-server-core`,
  `pathland-render-html`, `pathland-state-redis`, `pathland-test-kit`) depend on
  core, not on the Java DSL. Tests that author views through the DSL add
  `pathland-view` in test scope. The app-facing starters do depend on
  `pathland-view` because application code authors its root `View` with the DSL.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for the Pathland demo scripts. Source this file; it defines
# $ROOT (the repository root) and the prerequisite-build helpers each demo uses.

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

# Build the generated HTML base design and sync it into the renderer crate.
build_design() {
  if [[ ! -d "$ROOT/design/node_modules" ]]; then
    (cd "$ROOT/design" && npm ci)
  fi
  (cd "$ROOT/design" && npm run build)
  "$ROOT/scripts/sync-design-css.sh"
}

# Build the Rust HTML renderer cdylib (embedded in the Java pathland-render-html jar).
build_rust_html() {
  build_design
  (cd "$ROOT/lib/rust" && cargo build -p pathland-render-html)
}

# Build the Rust dylibs the desktop demos link: the core ring (libpathland_core)
# and the GTK4 renderer (libpathland_gtk).
build_gtk_dylibs() {
  (cd "$ROOT/lib/rust" && cargo build -p pathland-core-capi -p pathland-render-gtk)
}

# Build the Rust dylibs the Qt desktop demo links: the core ring
# (libpathland_core) and the Qt Quick renderer (libpathland_qt).
build_qt_dylibs() {
  (cd "$ROOT/lib/rust" && cargo build -p pathland-core-capi -p pathland-render-qt)
}

# Install the Java reactor (everything except the two web demos, which need a
# newer JDK to run; they are not required to launch the other demos).
java_install() {
  (cd "$ROOT/lib/java" && mvn -q install -DskipTests \
    -pl '!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo')
}#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the Pathland Quarkus demo (SSR + WebSocket deltas, dev mode with hot reload).
# → http://localhost:8080

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for the Pathland demo scripts. Source this file; it defines
# $ROOT (the repository root) and the prerequisite-build helpers each demo uses.

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

# Build the generated HTML base design and sync it into the renderer crate.
build_design() {
  if [[ ! -d "$ROOT/design/node_modules" ]]; then
    (cd "$ROOT/design" && npm ci)
  fi
  (cd "$ROOT/design" && npm run build)
  "$ROOT/scripts/sync-design-css.sh"
}

# Build the Rust HTML renderer cdylib (embedded in the Java pathland-render-html jar).
build_rust_html() {
  build_design
  (cd "$ROOT/lib/rust" && cargo build -p pathland-render-html)
}

# Build the Rust dylibs the desktop demos link: the core ring (libpathland_core)
# and the GTK4 renderer (libpathland_gtk).
build_gtk_dylibs() {
  (cd "$ROOT/lib/rust" && cargo build -p pathland-core-capi -p pathland-render-gtk)
}

# Build the Rust dylibs the Qt desktop demo links: the core ring
# (libpathland_core) and the Qt Quick renderer (libpathland_qt).
build_qt_dylibs() {
  (cd "$ROOT/lib/rust" && cargo build -p pathland-core-capi -p pathland-render-qt)
}

# Install the Java reactor (everything except the two web demos, which need a
# newer JDK to run; they are not required to launch the other demos).
java_install() {
  (cd "$ROOT/lib/java" && mvn -q install -DskipTests \
    -pl '!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo')

- SSR blocking is safe: the origin is a **different registry/actor**, so A's request thread blocking on `awaitSnapshot` cannot deadlock the origin.

## What's missing (all demo/wiring, not protocol)
- **No demo authors a `ProxyView`** yet.
- **No plumbing exposes the server's own address** (no Host/base-URL is passed into `PathlandSession`).
- **No starter passes a `ProxyTransport.Factory`** through `PathlandRegistry` → the JDK WS client is always used (fine for the demo).

A new **`lib/java/pathland-proxy-demo`** (Spring Boot, matching the demo you have running):
- `/` → **shell app**: `VStack` of a header `Text` + `ProxyView.make(p -> p.endpoint(originUrl).route("/"))`.

- **(a) Network loopback** (recommended for the demo): endpoint = the server's own URL + mount. **Zero new core code**; needs a configured URL/port; one WS hop to itself; request thread blocks briefly on the origin snapshot.

## Why same-server works today
- Both demos **already mount two apps** — root `/` and `/app2` (`SpringDemoApplication.java:35,41`, `QuarkusDemoApp.java:26,33`), each with its own registry, actor, state scope, base `/app2/_pathland`, and WS endpoint `/app2/_pathland/ws` (`PathlandRegistry.base():94`, Spring `PathlandAutoConfiguration.java:119`, Quarkus `MountedPathlandSocket.java:35`).

So for a mounted origin the endpoint carries the mount: `endpoint("http://localhost:8080/app2")` → `ws://localhost:8080/app2/_pathland/ws`. **That resolves exactly to the mounted app's real endpoint — no core change needed.**
- SSR blocking is safe: the origin is a **different registry/actor**, so A's request thread blocking on `awaitSnapshot` cannot deadlock the origin.

## What's missing (all demo/wiring, not protocol)
- **No demo authors a `ProxyView`** yet.
- **No plumbing exposes the server's own address** (no Host/base-URL is passed into `PathlandSession`).
- **No starter passes a `ProxyTransport.Factory`** through `PathlandRegistry` → the JDK WS client is always used (fine for the demo).
- A new demo module needs the DOM bundle copied (`scripts/copy-to-demos.mjs`), reactor registration, and (if published) the release exclusion list.

## Proposed demo
A new **`lib/java/pathland-proxy-demo`** (Spring Boot, matching the demo you have running):
- `/` → **shell app**: `VStack` of a header `Text` + `ProxyView.make(p -> p.endpoint(originUrl).route("/"))`.
- `/app2` → **origin app**: `MusicPlayerView` (rich + interactive) — or `CounterView` for a crisper demo.
- `originUrl` from a property `pathland.proxy.origin` (default `http://localhost:8080`), `server.port=8080`.
- Reuse `pathland-demo-views` + `DemoAssets.extractToTemp()` (as the Spring demo does).
- **Test** (`@SpringBootTest(RANDOM_PORT)` + `@DynamicPropertySource` setting `pathland.proxy.origin=http://localhost:<port>`): assert `GET /` HTML contains the origin's remapped ids + a known origin string, and a WS round-trip (event on a proxied node reaches the origin).

## Same-server mechanism — the one real fork
- **(a) Network loopback** (recommended for the demo): endpoint = the server's own URL + mount. **Zero new core code**; needs a configured URL/port; one WS hop to itself; request thread blocks briefly on the origin snapshot.
- **(b) In-process loopback transport** (new core code, ~150–250 lines): a `ProxyTransport` that bridges straight to the local registry (`registry.open/environment/dispatch/resync`), so `endpoint("/app2")` (a relative path) means "this server" — no URL, no port, no network hop.   target-neutral ID manifest), and `engine-traces/` (shared frame fixtures).

- Test: `cd lib/rust && cargo test` (runs all crates).
- Build/test the Java libraries: `cd lib/java && mvn install`.
- Run the GTK demo (native, zero-copy shared ring): `cd lib/rust && cargo run -p pathland-render-gtk-demo`.
- Run the Qt Quick demo (native, zero-copy shared ring): `cd lib/rust && cargo run -p pathland-render-qt-demo`
  (needs Qt6 dev libs — Homebrew: `brew install qtbase qtdeclarative`; on macOS point `QMAKE`
  at `$(brew --prefix qtbase)/bin/qmake` if it isn't on PATH, see `scripts/run-rust-qt-demo.sh`).

  `cd lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo && mvn quarkus:dev` (or `mvn package && java -jar target/quarkus-app/quarkus-run.jar`).

- Run the Spring Boot demo (SSR + WebSocket deltas):
  `cd lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-demo && mvn package && java -jar target/pathland-spring-boot-demo-0.1.0.jar`.
  Needs JDK 17+ (the whole stack runs on every LTS from 17) and Spring Boot ≥ 3.5.
  Prefer the fat jar over an IDE run: an IntelliJ classpath can mix stale `~/.m2`
  jars with fresh `target/classes`, which has been observed to make the Rust SSR
  decode an empty tree (a valid but blank page). If running from IntelliJ:
  **Reload All Maven Projects → Build**, and only one instance at a time. The
  DOM bundle is content-hashed (`dom-renderer-<sha256>.js`, pointer in
  `_pathland/dom-renderer.current`) so a rebuilt bundle always busts the
  immutable asset cache by URL — restart the app (fresh HTML references the new
  name) and reload normally; no hard refresh is needed. After any Rust/TS
  change, refresh the two layers the IDE cannot
  rebuild itself with `mvn -P refresh-ide validate` (root `pom.xml`: `cargo build
  -p pathland-render-html`, `npm run build:all`, and the render-html embedded
  dylib re-copy), then Reload/Build → Run → reload.

**Pathland is a cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol** that enables retained-mode UI development with multiple renderer backends. It is **protocol-first**, meaning the protocol specification is the source of truth, not any particular implementation.

**Status**: The Rust opcode engine (16-byte opcode, ring buffer, arena, diff-based reactive emission) is implemented and tested (`cargo test`). See the Architecture section above.
