<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <parent>
        <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
        <artifactId>pathland-parent</artifactId>
        <version>0.1.5</version>
    </parent>

    <artifactId>pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo</artifactId>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <!-- Demo application — not published to Maven Central. -->
    <properties>
        <maven.deploy.skip>true</maven.deploy.skip>
        <maven.javadoc.skip>true</maven.javadoc.skip>
        <!-- Quarkus 3.39.1 manages Kotlin 2.4.10; use the same compiler for the app. -->
        <kotlin.version>2.4.10</kotlin.version>
    </properties>

    <name>Pathland Quarkus Kotlin Demo</name>
    <description>
        Kotlin Quarkus demonstration app: SSR plus live 16-byte opcode deltas over
        WebSocket, authored entirely through pathland-view-kotlin and the Kotlin DSL
        Quarkus extension. It deliberately does not depend on the Java DSL or the
        shared Java demo views.
    </description>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-quarkus-kotlin</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-view-kotlin</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-junit</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <sourceDirectory>${project.basedir}/src/main/kotlin</sourceDirectory>
        <testSourceDirectory>${project.basedir}/src/test/kotlin</testSourceDirectory>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>compile</id>
                        <phase>process-sources</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>compile</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                    <execution>
                        <id>test-compile</id>
                        <phase>process-test-sources</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>test-compile</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
                <configuration>
                    <jvmTarget>${maven.compiler.release}</jvmTarget>
                    <compilerPlugins>
                        <plugin>all-open</plugin>
                    </compilerPlugins>
                    <pluginOptions>
                        <option>all-open:annotation=jakarta.enterprise.context.ApplicationScoped</option>
                        <option>all-open:annotation=jakarta.enterprise.context.Dependent</option>
                        <option>all-open:annotation=jakarta.inject.Singleton</option>
                        <option>all-open:annotation=jakarta.ws.rs.Path</option>
                    </pluginOptions>
                </configuration>
                <dependencies>
                    <dependency>
                        <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                        <artifactId>kotlin-maven-allopen</artifactId>
                        <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
                    </dependency>
                </dependencies>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
                <artifactId>quarkus-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>build</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-enforcer-plugin</artifactId>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>ban-java-dsl</id>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>enforce</goal>
                        </goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <rules>
                                <bannedDependencies>
                                    <excludes>
                                        <exclude>dev.pathland:pathland-view</exclude>
                                        <exclude>dev.pathland:pathland-demo-views</exclude>
                                    </excludes>
                                </bannedDependencies>
                            </rules>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

input.content:
# pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 1, 2026

Kotlin-first Quarkus demo: SSR plus live 16-byte opcode deltas over WebSocket,
authored with `pathland-view-kotlin` and hosted by `pathland-quarkus-kotlin`.

## Implemented

- Kotlin `PathlandApp` CDI bean (`KotlinDemoApplication`) and a Kotlin-owned
  `KotlinView` root (`KotlinDemoView`).
- Exercises persisted state (`count`, `items`), two-way text input (`name`),
  reactive computed text, `ForEach`, and Kotlin modifier sugar.
- Quarkus Kotlin build setup: `kotlin-maven-plugin`, `all-open` for CDI/JAX-RS
  annotations, `jvmTarget=17`.
- Maven Enforcer bans `pathland-view` and `pathland-demo-views`: the demo is
  Kotlin-DSL-only.
- `KotlinDemoSmokeTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts the CDI bean is discovered and
  SSR renders the Kotlin tree.
- The DOM renderer bundle + service worker are copied by
  `lib/typescript/scripts/copy-to-demos.mjs`.
- Run with `scripts/run-quarkus-kotlin-demo.sh` → `http://localhost:8080`.

## Not implemented / gaps

- No WebSocket delta integration test yet; SSR discovery is covered.
- No Quarkus codestart yet.
- Native image is not supported (Rust HTML renderer via JNA).

Updates are tiny binary deltas, not re-rendered pages or JSON trees. - **Native elements, not a canvas.** The platform lays out and animates real elements — you get native layout, text rendering, and accessibility for free, whether those elements are DOM nodes or GTK widgets. - **A thin client.** The web client is a small static file that hydrates the server HTML and applies updates in place. No framework, no virtual DOM, no re-render cost. ## The part you don't write The web client is a single prebuilt JavaScript file you copy into your static resources. It's shipped, not maintained — all the real logic lives in your backend. (There's also a native GTK renderer for desktop.) ## Where it runs today - **Web (SSR + live WebSocket deltas)** — Java, with Spring Boot and Quarkus starters and demos; the flagship getting-started path. - **Native desktop (GTK4)** — a renderer driven by the same protocol, from both the Rust DSL and the shared Java demo views (`pathland-gtk-demo`). Two surfaces, one protocol — the demos' shared views run under both without a rewrite. ## See it in action The same shared demo views, rendered by two of Pathland's surfaces — server-side HTML in the browser and native GTK4 widgets on the desktop:

Browser — SSR + live WebSocket deltas
Desktop — native GTK4 renderer
Try the hosted Quarkus demo live: **[pathland.onrender.com](https://pathland.onrender.com)**. ## Where it's headed The SSR path above is the on-ramp — the protocol isn't limited to it. Write the app logic once, run it on embedded, mobile, desktop, and browser. Pathland is an open protocol, so the same code that drives the server-rendered UI today can also run on the device itself: - **In the browser**, the app logic compiles to WASM, writes to a shared buffer, and the main thread is left to rendering alone. - **On embedded devices**, the logic runs on one core while another core renders, with the ring buffer carrying the protocol between them — mapped onto a lightweight UI toolkit like LVGL. - **On mobile and desktop**, the same logic drives native renderers — SwiftUI/UIKit on Apple platforms, Jetpack Compose on Android, Qt and GTK on desktop. Wherever it runs, only tiny binary updates travel across the ring buffer and are applied in place — nothing is re-rendered or serialized, which is what keeps the UI stutter-free, even on small devices. ## Try it Each demo has a one-command launcher in [`scripts/`](./scripts/). Run one from the repository root — it builds its own prerequisites (Rust dylibs, the Java reactor) and launches: | Script | Demo | What you get | |--------|------|--------------| | `./scripts/run-spring-demo.sh` | Spring Boot SSR + WebSocket | http://localhost:8080 | | `./scripts/run-quarkus-demo.sh` | Quarkus SSR + WebSocket (hot reload) | http://localhost:8080 | | `./scripts/run-rust-gtk-demo.sh` | Rust DSL → GTK4 desktop renderer | a native window | | `./scripts/run-java-gtk-demo.sh` | Java DSL → GTK4 desktop renderer (the shared `SplitNavDemo`) | a native window | ```bash # e.g. the Spring Boot demo ./scripts/run-spring-demo.sh ``` Notes: - The web demos need a JDK 17+ (the whole stack runs on every LTS from 17). - The GTK demos need the GTK4 + libadwaita system libraries. - On macOS the Java GTK demo hands GTK the main thread automatically (`-XstartOnFirstThread`); Linux needs nothing special. The same commands without the scripts: ```bash # one-time: build the Rust HTML renderer (embedded in the jar), then the Java reactor cd lib/rust && cargo build -p pathland-render-html cd lib/java && mvn install # Spring Boot demo cd lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-demo mvn -q package && java -jar target/pathland-spring-boot-demo-0.1.0.jar # → http://localhost:8080 # Quarkus demo (dev mode with hot reload) cd lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo mvn quarkus:dev # → http://localhost:8080 # Same protocol, native GTK desktop renderer (no browser) cd lib/rust && cargo run -p pathland-render-gtk-demo # Same protocol via Java: the shared demo views (SplitNavDemo) under the GTK renderer cd lib/rust && cargo build -p pathland-core-capi -p pathland-render-gtk cd lib/java/pathland-gtk-demo MAVEN_OPTS="-XstartOnFirstThread" mvn -q compile exec:java \ -Dpathland.core.lib=$PWD/../../lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_core.dylib \ -Dpathland.gtk.lib=$PWD/../../lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_gtk.dylib # (macOS needs -XstartOnFirstThread; Linux can drop it) ``` ## The technical details This README is the *what*. The *how* — the wire protocol, the DSL contract, the conformance vectors, and the implementation notes — lives in [`spec/`](./spec/): - [OPCODE.md](./spec/OPCODE.md) — the binary protocol - [DSL.md](./spec/DSL.md) — the authoring surface (what you write) - [PRIMITIVES.md](./spec/PRIMITIVES.md), [MODIFIERS.md](./spec/MODIFIERS.md), [EVENTS.md](./spec/EVENTS.md) - [CONFORMANCE.md](./spec/CONFORMANCE.md) — golden byte vectors ## Status & license Proof of concept. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md), [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md), [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md), and [GENAI.md](./GENAI.md) (generative-AI transparency). state.output:
- `bump` — commit the version back to `main`.
    - `release-assets` — attach the `.crate` files, the Java main jars, and the
      four native libs to the GitHub Release.

The Java deploy runs on **Maven 3.9.9** (pinned in the workflow): Maven 3.10
writes a `maven-metadata-local.xml` beside each artifact in the Central staging,
which the Portal rejects ("content that does NOT have a .pom file"). The demos
are **excluded from the release reactor** (`-pl '!pathland-demo-views,!pathland-gtk-demo,!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo'`)
— `central-publishing-maven-plugin` bundles every reactor module, ignoring
`maven.deploy.skip`, and the demos must not be published.

The publish steps are **idempotent**: a crate+version already on crates.io is
skipped, so re-running a partially failed release is safe (re-run the workflow
via `workflow_dispatch`, passing the `tag`). Maven Central rejects a re-deploy of
an existing version, so a Java re-run only helps if the Java deploy did not
complete.

## Published Java modules

`pathland-view`, `pathland-view-processor`, `pathland-render-html`,
`pathland-state-redis`, `pathland-server-core`, `pathland-observability`,
`pathland-test-kit`, `pathland-spring-boot-starter`, `pathland-quarkus-starter`
(plus the `pathland-parent` POM). The demo modules
(`pathland-demo-views`, `pathland-gtk-demo`, `pathland-quarkus-demo`,
`pathland-spring-boot-demo`) set `maven.deploy.skip`.

  (the Java DSL, `dev.pathland.view`), `pathland-view-processor`,
  `pathland-view-kotlin` (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`), `pathland-render-html`,
  `pathland-state-redis`, `pathland-demo-views`, the Quarkus/Spring demos, and
  the TypeScript DOM renderer (`lib/typescript`).
- `spec/` — the protocol contract: `OPCODE.md` (primary), `PRIMITIVES.md`,
  `MODIFIERS.md`, `EVENTS.md`, `CONFORMANCE.md` (golden vectors), `ENGINE.md`
  (retained-tree behavior), `DSL.md` (authoring surface), `protocol.tsv` (the
  target-neutral ID manifest), and `engine-traces/` (shared frame fixtures).

Implementation status per project lives in each crate/module's `status.md`.

# C ABI (cdylib) used by Java JNA / native hosts

# CI but buildable with: cd lib/java && mvn -q install)
cd lib/java && mvn -q -B test -pl '!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo'

parts.text:
This is not a missing bundle file. It is a classloader regression from the extension split.

## Root cause

`PathlandAssets.bundleName()` resolves `_pathland/dom-renderer.current` with:

```java
PathlandAssets.class.getClassLoader().getResourceAsStream(path)
```

After `pathland-server-core` became a dependency of the `pathland-quarkus` extension, Quarkus loads it in the base/extension classloader. The app’s `META-INF/resources/_pathland/dom-renderer.current` lives in the application runtime classloader. The core loader cannot see it, so `PathlandAssets` falls back to the literal `dom-renderer.js`, which was never copied. The browser then requests a nonexistent file and gets 404.

This is the same classloader pattern as the `_StateBinder` issue already fixed.

## Plan

1. **Fix manifest lookup in `PathlandAssets`**
   - Resolve through the thread context classloader first.
   - Fall back to `PathlandAssets.class.getClassLoader()`, then system classloader.
   - Cache keyed by the classloader used, or at minimum do not permanently cache the fallback from a classloader that cannot see the app resources.
   - Keep `resetForTests()` working.

2. **Add regression coverage**
   - `PathlandAssetsTest`: add a test where the synthetic TCCL provides the manifest while the default loader does not.
   - `KotlinDemoSmokeTest`: assert SSR references a content-hashed `dom-renderer-<hash>.js`, not `dom-renderer.js`, and that GET on that URL returns 200.
   - Optionally mirror the script assertion in `ProxyDemoTest` for the Java demo.

3. **Verify**
   - `mvn -q -B -pl pathland-server-core -am test`
   - `mvn -q -B -pl pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo -am clean test`
   - `mvn -q -B -pl pathland-quarkus-demo -am clean test`
   - Full `mvn -q -B test`

4. **Restart the demo**
   - Stop and rerun `scripts/run-quarkus-kotlin-demo.sh`.
   - If the old page or service worker cached `dom-renderer.js`, clear the service worker / hard reload once.

Likely commit: `fix(quarkus): resolve the DOM bundle from the app classloader`.

Index: lib/java/pathland-server-core/status.md =================================================================== --- lib/java/pathland-server-core/status.md +++ lib/java/pathland-server-core/status.md @@ -1,214 +1,216 @@ # pathland-server-core — implementation status **Last updated:** October 28, 2026 The transport-agnostic Pathland server runtime: one app instance per session (SSR + live 16-byte opcode deltas + environment), the session registry, and the **multi-app host** (the BFF), shared by the Spring Boot and Quarkus starters. No web-framework dependency — framework glue lives in the starters. ## Implemented - **Window metadata + SSR head attrs**: `PathlandSession.renderHtml` injects host attrs into the renderer's opening `` (which now carries `lang`), and `FrameRebase` rebases `SET_WINDOW_METADATA` string offsets. Proxy origin metadata is dropped with the other META opcodes. - **`PathlandApp`** — the app's root-view factory (`View newRoot()` + optional `theme()`); the single app-specific piece a starter needs. - **`MountedApp`** — `record MountedApp(String path, PathlandApp app)`: one app mounted at a subpath prefix (normalized; `/` = root). Hosts any number of them. - **`PathlandHost`** — the multi-app dispatcher: one `PathlandRegistry` per mounted app (own actor thread, own sessions). `match(requestUri)` resolves the owning registry by **longest mount-prefix match** and reports the **mount-stripped route** (a root mount claims every unclaimed path). Duplicate mount paths are rejected at construction. - **`PathlandRegistry`** — session lifecycle per app: single actor thread, 1:1 sessions keyed by a **per-connection `uiId`** (a fresh id per WebSocket connection, so two windows of the same browser never share a UI model), lazy creation on first environment message, pending connections (each carrying the mount-prefixed state scope from the client's per-window `wid`), `open(uiId, wid, conn)`/`environment`/`dispatch`/`resync`/`close`/`renderHtml`/`shutdown`. New: - `mountPath()`/`base()` — each app's framework base is `//_pathland` (`/_pathland` for the root), emitted as `data-pathland-base` in SSR; - `stateScope(windowId)` — app-qualified state-store scope (`mount:wid`) so apps and windows sharing a store never collide; - `stripRoute(route)` — strips the mount prefix from SSR routes, WS environment ROUTE fields, **and inbound `NAVIGATE` URLs** (browser back/forward sends the real address, e.g. `http://host/app2/home`), so a mounted app always sees its own route space (`/app2/home` → `/home`). `Router.pathOf` is reused for URL→path extraction. - **Per-window isolation (no session cookie)**: session identity (the `uiId` map key) is deliberately separate from the persisted-state scope (the client's `wid`, carried only on the WebSocket URL — never in the page URL, so the address bar stays clean). The SSR request therefore has no `wid`: `renderHtml(route, wid)` with a null `wid` renders defaults; the client's live session is scoped by the WS `wid`, and a same-tab reload re-syncs that window's persisted state over the WebSocket. The old `session` cookie is removed. - **`PathlandSession`** — per-session: builds the `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` signal, mounts `app.newRoot().modifiers(environmentBinding(e -> e.key(ACTIVE_PATH).value(activePath)))`, **delta-batched send-on-`endFrame`** (`DeltaBatcher` coalesces per-signal frames into one batch — flush ~20 ms or 16 KB, string offsets rebased — so a continuous input burst can't overflow a remote WebSocket send queue), `applyEnvironment` (re-route guard-aware via the bound router), `dispatch` (tap/nav-intent/text/value/date/NAVIGATE), `resync`, `renderHtml`, `close`. Runtime theming: `setTheme(ThemeData)`, `resetTheme()`, and `setColorScheme(ThemeMode)` emit one `META::RESET_THEME` + `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` frame or `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` to the live client (renderer state; no tree re-emission). The SSR document keeps the mount theme until a resync/reload. `sendBatch` drops the connection on any send failure (a client reconnect then re-syncs via `META::RESYNC` instead of silently stalling on an "open" socket); `closeConnection` best-effort closes an `AutoCloseable` adapter (the starters now close their underlying WebSocket on failure). Now takes the app's `base` and `stateScope` explicitly (the registry supplies them). - **`DeltaBatcher`** — merges session delta frames (opcodes + a single rebased string section) and flushes as one network batch on a timer/byte threshold; the Java analogue of the Rust transport's `Batcher`. It owns the per-session **message sequence** (stamped on each flushed batch via `FrameCodec.encodeFrame(frame, sequence)`) so the DOM client can detect a lost batch and recover with `META::RESYNC` (spec/OPCODE.md §Sequence gap detection); an empty flush consumes no sequence. The **sender runs OUTSIDE the monitor** — a blocking/queueing send can never stall the actor thread's `append` or the flush scheduler. Coalescing tests cover merging + rebasing, a 100-frame burst collapsing to one send, incrementing sequences, and a blocking sender not holding the lock. - **`PathlandConnection`** — the transport seam (`send(byte[])`/`isOpen()`); each starter adapts its WebSocket type to it. - **Observability seam** — `PathlandTelemetry` (default `NOOP`): the runtime emits session open/close, inbound event batches, flushed batches (frames/opcodes/bytes + merge-encode time), SSR render latency, resync requests, and send failures; the host binds a pull-based active-sessions gauge. `PathlandHost`/`PathlandRegistry`/ `PathlandSession`/`DeltaBatcher` thread it through (a host with no telemetry pays nothing). `pathland-observability` provides the Micrometer + OpenTelemetry adapters; the starters auto-wire them. Logging is **SLF4J** (both frameworks bind it) — the old ad-hoc `System.out` is gone. See issue #62. - **Concurrency stress** — `RegistryConcurrencyTest`: 100 sessions driven through the registry concurrently (clicks on each session's button) while SSR-style requests construct throwaway sessions on request threads — the shared-actor / global-`Scheduler` cross-session corruption guard. Each session must reach exactly its own click count (no lost effects, no cross-session values). - **Shared WS test harness** — `dev.pathland.server.test.{WsSession,MultiSessionProbe}` (a JDK-WebSocket client speaking the PLPL protocol: env/resync/click/ping) lives in the **`pathland-test-kit`** module (main scope, so package builds resolve it as a normal jar); the starters' 100-session stress tests reuse it. - **`StateStores`** — default state store: Redis when reachable, else the supplied fallback. - **SSR debug comments (property-gated)**: `PathlandSession`/`PathlandRegistry` take a `debugHtml` flag (constructor + `isDebugHtml()`); when set, `renderHtml` uses the renderer's debug mode so every rendered node is prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component and the modifiers applied. The Spring/Quarkus starters bind it to the `pathland.debug-html` property (default `false`). - **Reserved framework root**: `PathlandSession.PATHLAND_BASE` (`/_pathland`) — the SSR page carries the app's base as `data-pathland-base` and the DOM-client bundle is injected at `{base}/dom-renderer-.js` (`PathlandAssets` reads the current - name from the `_pathland/dom-renderer.current` manifest on the classpath, falling - back to the literal `dom-renderer.js` when absent) so the client's WebSocket and + name from the `_pathland/dom-renderer.current` manifest on the classpath, resolving + through the thread context classloader first so a Quarkus extension parent loader + can see the application's static resources; it falls back to the literal + `dom-renderer.js` only when absent) so the client's WebSocket and asset refs resolve from the same reserved prefix (spec DSL.md). The content-hashed name busts the immutable asset cache with a fresh URL per build. The built-in base design is linked the same way: `renderHtml` renders through `HtmlRenderer.renderLinked(frame, root, base)`, so the CSS href is `{base}/base-.css` (token overrides/fit rules stay inline). Multi-app hosts give each mount its own base. - **Per-window-id service worker (opt-in, issue #155)**: `PathlandHost` carries a host-level `serviceWorker` flag (default `false`; one registration covers the whole origin) threaded to every `PathlandRegistry`; `PathlandSession.renderHtml` emits `data-pathland-service-worker="true"` on `` when set, and the DOM client registers `{base}/sw.js` (root scope) / unregisters when absent (the kill switch). `PathlandRegistry.serviceWorkerUrl()` names the served script. `renderHtml` also emits `data-pathland-ssr-scoped="true"` when the request carried a real per-window id, so the client can skip its initial `META::RESYNC` (the SSR was already rendered with that window's state and the live session shares it). ## Not implemented / gaps - No multi-node/shared sessions (each server owns its sessions in-memory). - Quarkus mounted-app WebSocket endpoints require a **single-segment** mount path (the `/{app}` path param); Spring supports any depth. ## Proxy views (spec/PROXY.md) — M1 (live) - **`proxy.ProxyIdMap`** — node-id namespacing: the reserved high range `[0x4000_0000, 0x8000_0000)`, 1024 blocks of `2^20`, the block math, and the opcode remap in both directions (`TREE` node ids + the node-id-bearing `PARAMETER` ops `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DATE` on ingress; `EVENT` targets on egress; `META` untouched). `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` is **not** remapped — its `A` is a token-path arena offset, not a node id (remapping it produced a huge out-of-bounds string offset → the client's RESYNC loop; regression-tested). Pure + unit-tested. - **`proxy.ProxyTransport`** + **`proxy.JdkWebSocketTransport`** — the outbound connection seam (default: the JDK `HttpClient` WebSocket client, no new dependency) with a `Factory` so a starter can swap a native client. - **`proxy.ProxySession`** — one origin connection: sends `META::ENVIRONMENT` + `META::RESYNC`, **remaps** the origin snapshot into the proxy's block and attaches the origin root under the proxy node, forwards live deltas remapped, routes client events back (target unmapped), replies `PONG` to origin `PING`, translates origin `META::RESET` into a **scoped** subtree teardown (never a global reset), tears the subtree down on disconnect (the origin session is per-connection), and reconnects with exponential backoff. The service credential + a cycle-guard instance id ride the handshake headers. **Backpressure** (spec/PROXY.md §8): a "chatty origin" breaker (a per-second batch cap → drop + `RESYNC`) and event coalescing (pointer-moves coalesce by target; discrete events flush immediately). - **`proxy.ProxyHost`** — one `ProxySession` per `PROXY_VIEW` node, each with its own block; routes inbound events whose target is in a proxy range to the owning origin connection; owns the proxy scheduler. `reconcile(wanted)` starts a session for every `PROXY_VIEW` node and closes the session of every node that left the tree; released id blocks go to a **free-block pool** and are reused, so repeated removal/re-add cycles never exhaust the 1024-block range. - **`PathlandSession`** integration — captures `RenderResult.proxyViews()` and registers the emitter's structural-reconcile callback (`Emitter.onStructureReconciled`) to `reconcileProxies()`, so a proxy lives **exactly while its node is in the retained tree** (spec/PROXY.md §7): a `SizeThatFits` slot dropping the candidate that held it closes the origin connection, and re-adding it opens a fresh one (re-seeded by `META::RESYNC`). The host's frames feed the session's `DeltaBatcher` (a single unified sequence); `dispatch` splits proxy-range events to the origin and everything else to the app's own bindings; `close` tears the proxies down. `proxyTransportFactory(...)` lets a host supply a framework transport. - **`PathlandTelemetry`** — `proxyConnected`/`proxyDisconnected`/`proxyBatchDropped`/ `proxyResyncRequested` (all default no-ops). **SSR embed (M2).** `renderHtml` starts the proxies and **blocks** for each origin's snapshot (`ProxySession.awaitSnapshot`, bounded by a 2s timeout), then splices the remapped origin frames into the session's mount frame (`FrameMerger`, reusing the batcher's string rebasing via `FrameRebase`) so the renderer emits **one** document — the origin subtree plus its fit band rules in the same head. The origin's **global** token overrides (`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`) are **dropped** (live + SSR): a proxied app renders under the **host's** theme, while its token *references* resolve against that theme (spec/PROXY.md §9). A proxy whose origin does not answer in time renders empty (a placeholder) and hydrates over the live connection. A client `META::RESYNC` also replays A's tree **and** asks every origin for a fresh snapshot (`ProxyHost.resyncAll`). **Gaps (M3):** nested proxies and per-proxy theme scoping are deferred (the origin's global overrides are dropped, not scoped, spec/PROXY.md §9). A tiny orphan window remains on removal: an origin batch already queued in the `DeltaBatcher` (≤20 ms) when the proxy node is removed can still create an unattached element in the client's `byId` (not in the DOM); eliminating it needs the `ProxySession` to track the ids it emitted and `DELETE` them on close. ## Verified by `mvn test` — `PathlandSessionTest`: mounts + routes taps through the binding maps, `applyEnvironment`/`resync`/`close` idempotent, registry SSR + lifecycle/teardown, and **two windows with the same `wid` still get separate sessions** (a tap to one never reaches the other). `PathlandHostTest`: longest-prefix dispatch + route stripping, mount-boundary respect, no-root-mount 404, per-app base + state scope, duplicate-mount rejection, normalization, SSR emits the mounted app's base. `PathlandTelemetryTest`: a recording telemetry double asserts the registry emits session/event/resync/flush/SSR/close events, the host binds the active-sessions gauge, a failed send reports `connectionFailed`, and `DeltaBatcher` reports the flushed batch. `proxy.ProxyIdMapTest`: the reserved range, block round-trips, overflow rejection, and the opcode remap (TREE/PARAMETER node ids remapped, APPEND/META untouched, EVENT targets unmapped). `proxy.ProxySessionTest` (a fake origin transport): the ENVIRONMENT+RESYNC handshake + handshake headers, snapshot remap + root attachment, delta remap with the string section passed through verbatim, event egress unmapped, pointer-move coalescing, `META::RESET` → scoped teardown, disconnect teardown, and the chatty-origin drop+resync breaker. `proxy.ProxyIntegrationTest`: a `ProxyView` in the app tree opens an origin connection on `connect`, the remapped origin snapshot reaches the client (with the root attached), a client event in the proxy range routes back to the origin unmapped, and the SSR document embeds the origin subtree (remapped ids) in one render. `FrameMergerTest`: splicing a proxy's origin frame into an SSR frame rebases its string offsets (SET_TEXT / LIST / STRING operands) and returns the base unchanged when there is nothing to append. \ No newline at end of file
